and the ascertainment of its existence, [which is the basis for] engagement in transactions and the like, is established. // Pramāṇav 2.68 //
A means of knowledge [is valid] because of non-deception; if [you say] there is no confidence because of occasional deviation —
that is a bad view of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>); such is this. // Pramāṇav 2.69 //
Since sometimes the cognition of an established thing [arises] somewhere,

children.text: tadvaśya tato jātaṃ tatsvabhāvo 'pi vā bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.70 //
children.translated_text: [it must have] arisen from the power of that [thing]; or it may have that [thing's] nature. // Pramāṇav 2.70 //

children.text: svanimittāt svabhāvād vā vinā nārthasya sambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without its own cause or without [its own] nature, there is no possibility of an object;

children.text: yacca rūpaṃ tayordṛṣṭaṃ tadevānyatra lakṣaṇam // Pramāṇav_2.71 //
children.translated_text: and that form which is observed in those two — that alone is the mark elsewhere. // Pramāṇav 2.71 //
When one's own nature or one's own cause is observed — [those are] the causes of seeing;

children.text: anyeṣu satsvadṛśye ca satta vā tadvataḥ katham // Pramāṇav_2.72 //
children.translated_text: when other [causes] exist but [the object] is not seen — how can the existence of that-which-has-[the-mark] [be established]? // Pramāṇav 2.72 //
And if the cognition of the universal is invalid, the loss of that [cognition] follows;
just as [the cognition of] existence after death — that is apprehended through the senses alternately. // Pramāṇav 2.73 //
And that [determination] is not in the capacity of the senses and the like, because of the impossibility of sense-cognition;
in the ascertainment of non-existence, the arising of cognition would be indefinite. // Pramāṇav 2.74 //
And perception [operates] on the own-characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), being non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>);
the grasping of the universal is not in that [perception] without conceptual construction — therefore [that grasping is] inference (<s>anumā</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.75 //
When the object of knowledge is delimited, the impermanence of phonemes is not apprehended;
Another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) [is postulated], since cognition of that [object] is possible without a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.76 //
Because the connection of the logical mark is not established when a particular is perceived,

children.text: tat pramāṇāntaraṃ meyabahutvād bahutāpi vā // Pramāṇav_2.77 //
children.translated_text: that [inference] is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>; or there may even be multiplicity [of <s>pramāṇas</s>] due to the multiplicity of objects to be known. // Pramāṇav_2.77 //
Since a single <s>pramāṇa</s> may operate in multiple [domains], or multiple [<s>pramāṇas</s>] in one,
the exclusion of the number one or three [of <s>pramāṇas</s>] may or may not follow from the non-observation of a distinguishing feature. // Pramāṇav_2.78 //
Due to the non-restriction of objects, and because another object of knowledge is possible,

children.text: yojanād varṇasāmānye nāyaṃ doṣaḥ prasajyate // Pramāṇav_2.79 //
children.translated_text: this fault does not arise when the analysis is applied to the universal of phonemes (<s>varṇasāmānya</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.79 //
It is not a non-real form, since it establishes the proof of that very [thing] as such;
if there is no establishment of another elsewhere, that is because of the establishment of that very [thing]. // Pramāṇav_2.80 //

children.text: yo hi bhāvo yathābhūto sa tadṛgliṅ gacetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: For whatever entity exists in whatever manner, that is the cause of the cognition of the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) having that form;

children.text: hetustajjā tathābhūte tasmād vastuni liṅigadhīḥ // Pramāṇav_2.81 //
children.translated_text: born from that, the cognition of the mark-bearer (<s>liṅgin</s>) [arises] with respect to that very real object. // Pramāṇav_2.81 //
Thus, of the cognitions of the logical mark and the mark-bearer, through their successive connection to the real object,
there is non-deception even for those [cognitions] that are devoid of the appearance of that [object]. // Pramāṇav_2.82 //
And because of the determination as having that form, for those two [cognitions] which are devoid of that form,
even though they are non-deceptive regarding that form, the distinction of error has been established. // Pramāṇav_2.83 //
Therefore, with respect to the object to be known, the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is the cause of the cognition of the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>);

children.text: nimittaṃ tatsvabhāvo vā kāraṇam tacca taddhiyaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.84 //
children.translated_text: or its own essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the cause, and that [is the cause] of the cognition of that [object]. // Pramāṇav_2.84 //
Negation, however, is everywhere established through non-perception (<s>anupalambha</s>),
since for those who assert establishment through <s>pramāṇas</s>, [negation follows] from the opposite of the [positive] meaning itself. // Pramāṇav_2.85 //
The statement of a contradictory property (<s>viruddhadharma</s>) of that [object] or of its cause is observed;
that which is used in the negation of that very [thing] also indicates the status of being a <s>pramāṇa</s>. // Pramāṇav_2.86 //
Otherwise, by stating the essential nature of one property, how could the non-existence of another

children.text: nāstitvaṃ kena gamyeta virodhācced asāvapi // Pramāṇav_2.87 //
children.translated_text: be known? If [you say] through contradiction — then that too // Pramāṇav_2.87 //

children.text: siddhaḥ kenāsahasthānāditi cet tat kuto matam /
children.translated_text: is established by what, since [contradictory things] cannot coexist? If [you say] from the absence of perception of what is perceptible — then that is [itself] the status of being a <s>pramāṇa</s>. // Pramāṇav_2.88 //
— if [you say] from the absence of perception of what is perceptible — then that is [itself] the status of being a <s>pramāṇa</s>. // Pramāṇav_2.88 //
Therefore, even when stated by its own term, that [non-perception] is the establisher of the absence of the [object];
for which there is no <s>pramāṇa</s>, that is to be called a negation in every respect. // Pramāṇav_2.89 //
By this, the statement of an effect of a meaning contradictory to that has been explained;

children.text: prayogaḥ kevalaṃ bhinnaḥ sarvatrārtho na bhidyate // Pramāṇav_2.90 //
children.translated_text: only the formulation differs — the meaning does not differ anywhere. // Pramāṇav_2.90 //
And that contradictory [factor], together with its means, without establishing [the object] and by blocking [it] —
the statement of a <s>pramāṇa</s> in negation does not follow the tradition. // Pramāṇav_2.91 //
Like the negation of an omniscient being, afterlife, and so forth through [mere] statement and the like,
because contradiction regarding objects beyond the senses (<s>atīndriya</s>) is not established. // Pramāṇav_2.92 //
What sublating-sublated relationship could there be? If there were reasoning and awareness of such a kind,
if [you say] of non-perception of that kind — let that very [non-perception] be stated as the means of proof. // Pramāṇav_2.93 //
Such non-perception has been declared to be non-ascertaining;
therefore, regarding things completely beyond [perception], there is no determination of existence or non-existence. // Pramāṇav_2.94 //

children.text: bhinno 'bhinno 'pi vā dharmaḥ sa viruddhaḥ prayujjate /
children.translated_text: A property, whether different or non-different, is employed as contradictory,

children.text: yathāgnirahime sādhye sattā vā janmabādhanī // Pramāṇav_2.95 //
children.translated_text: just as fire [is used] when the absence of cold is to be proved, or existence [is used] as negating origination. // Pramāṇav_2.95 //

children.text: yathā vastveva vastūnāṃ sādhane sādhanaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: Just as a real thing is considered the means of establishing real things,

children.text: tathā vastveva vastūnāṃ svanivṛttau nivarttakam // Pramāṇav_2.96 //
children.translated_text: so too a real thing is the remover of real things in [effecting] their own cessation. // Pramāṇav_2.96 //
By this, the imagined [property] posited anywhere whatsoever,
[characterized by] being in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus), <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue), or otherwise, has been refuted. // Pramāṇav_2.97 //
Even there, a pervading property (<s>vyāpaka dharma</s>) is considered indicative of cessation,
if the cessation of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) itself is somehow ascertained. // Pramāṇav_2.98 //
That which is stated as the logical mark of the very [thing] in the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> [for it],
that is [intended] for those who are utterly confused in meaning, [obvious] even to cowherds, and not concealed. // Pramāṇav_2.99 //
This much is the fruit of ascertainment: non-perception (<s>anupalambhana</s>) in the case of absence;

children.text: tacca hetau svabhāve vā dṛśye dṛśyatā mate // Pramāṇav_2.100 //
children.translated_text: and that [non-perception applies] when the cause or the essential nature, being perceptible, is regarded as perceptible. // Pramāṇav_2.100 //
In the apprehension of impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>) and the like through inference (<s>anumāna</s>), this order is accepted;
validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) alone [is established], not the apprehension of [the object] elsewhere. // Pramāṇav_2.101 //

children.text: nānyāsyānityatā bhāvāt pūrva siddhaḥ sa cenidriyāt /
children.translated_text: The impermanence of another [entity] does not [follow] from [its] existence; that [impermanence] was previously established through the senses;

children.text: nānekarūpo vācyo 'sau vācyo dharmo vikalpajaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.102 //
children.translated_text: that [entity] which is to be expressed is not of multiple forms — the expressible property arises from conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.102 //
When the substrate of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is established, that universal is indeed established;
when that is not established, inference (<s>anumāna</s>) operates precisely for establishing that very [thing]. // Pramāṇav_2.103 //
In some cases, the non-recognition of that [impermanence] is due to the possibility of [confusion with] similar other [entities],
due to the error of one who does not perceive the distinction, like the difference between a magical illusion and a [real] ball. // Pramāṇav_2.104 //
For indeed, a person perceiving [something] without a mark, from [its] beginning, without a connected subsequent arising,

children.text: paśyan paricchinattyeva dīpādi nāśinaṃ janaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.105 //
children.translated_text: ascertains that a lamp and so forth are perishable. // Pramāṇav_2.105 //
Even regarding the capacity (<s>śakti</s>) that constitutes the essential nature of an entity, with respect to [its] effect and perception,
confusion [arises] from the lack of immediacy, due to the inability to determine [the sequence]. // Pramāṇav_2.106 //
The exposition of inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is for the purpose of removing that very [confusion];
great intellects discern all aspects from a single moment. // Pramāṇav_2.107 //
When that [object] has ceased in every respect, cognitions whose basis is [that] cessation

children.text: buddhayo 'rthe pravarttante bhinne bhinnāśrayā iva // Pramāṇav_2.108 //
children.translated_text: engage with the object as if having distinct substrates, though [the object] is differentiated. // Pramāṇav_2.108 //
Just as injunctions and designations, when there is no cause of error,
[the intellect] connects appearances (<s>pratibhā</s>) conforming to its own nature, by its own nature. // Pramāṇav_2.109 //
Or, destruction (<s>dhvaṃsa</s>) is also established here through a logical mark — from non-perception (<s>anupalambha</s>);
for an entity that existed before and then ceased to exist is called impermanent (<s>anitya</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.110 //
For one whose inquiry concerns the connection with existence delimited by both ends [i.e., beginning and end],
the statement of impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>) by that [person means] that [existence extends] just so far — in what two recollections? // Pramāṇav_2.111 //
If there is non-existence both before and after, is that not itself impermanence (<s>anityatā</s>)?

children.text: ṣaṣṭhayādyayogāditi cedū antayoḥ sa kathaṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.112 //
children.translated_text: If [you object] due to the inapplicability of the genitive case and so forth — how could that [relation] obtain at the two ends? // Pramāṇav_2.112 //
Due to the permanence of existence and connection, there is no qualification by the two ends;
if there were no qualification at all, the two ends would be [mere] cause and effect. // Pramāṇav_2.113 //
Due to the absence of connection, one desires the prior non-existence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>) of the entity;

children.text: tadupādhisamākhyāne te 'pyasya ca na sidhyataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.114 //
children.translated_text: in the designation of that condition (<s>upādhi</s>), those two also do not establish that [entity]. // Pramāṇav_2.114 //
Existence (<s>sattā</s>) is [said to be] produced by the non-contact with its own cause — the cause, they say;

children.text: sā sattā sa ca sambandho nityau kāryamatheha kim // Pramāṇav_2.115 //
children.translated_text: that existence and that connection are permanent — then what is the effect here? // Pramāṇav_2.115 //
That whose non-existence is produced — that entity does not have prior non-existence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>);
from the non-acceptance of connection, this entire universe would be permanent. // Pramāṇav_2.116 //
Therefore, cognitions that do not stumble upon [wrong] meanings, even regarding words held to have non-different meanings,
being differentiators of the expressible, are the basis for exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.117 //
Recognition of a particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) is not [possible] due to momentary difference;

children.text: na vā viśeṣaviṣayaṃ dṝṣṭasāmyena tadgrahāt // Pramāṇav_2.118 //
children.translated_text: nor is it directed toward a particular, since it is grasped through perceived similarity. // Pramāṇav_2.118 //
If [you say] 'that is the example (<s>nidarśana</s>)' — that is the non-apprehension of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>);

children.text: nidarśanatvāt siddhasya pramāṇenāsya kiṃ punaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.119 //
children.translated_text: since what is already established serves as the example, what further [need] is there for a <s>pramāṇa</s> for this? // Pramāṇav_2.119 //
If [you say] there is no fault because [the universal] has been forgotten — then for that very reason it is not an example;
if [you say] the existence of that is established in what is perceived — [that is established] through a <s>pramāṇa</s> regarding another object. // Pramāṇav_2.120 //
In the superimposition of reality, there is error; the establishment of that lacks the status of a <s>pramāṇa</s>;
due to the identity of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and the other [<s>pramāṇa</s>], the establishment of one is the establishment of both. // Pramāṇav_2.121 //
That which is being connected with another determination is known as memory (<s>smṛti</s>);
if [memory] were not [so defined] because of its dependence on a mark (<s>liṅga</s>), then memory would not [occur] due to deviation. // Pramāṇav_2.122 //
That perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) is established by perception itself;
<s>Vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction), which depends on names, is self-experienced by all. // Pramāṇav_2.123 //
Having withdrawn all thought, with a stilled inner self,

children.text: sthito 'pi cakṣuṣā rūpamīkṣate sākṣajā matiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.124 //
children.translated_text: even while remaining [still], one sees form with the eye — this is sense-born cognition (<s>sākṣajā mati</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.124 //
Then, again engaging in conceptualization: 'such was my conceptualization' —

children.text: vetti ceti na pūrvoktāvasthāyāmindriyād gatau // Pramāṇav_2.125 //
children.translated_text: one knows thus; but in the previously described state, there is no conceptualization in cognition arising from the senses. // Pramāṇav_2.125 //

children.text: ekatra dṛṣṭau bhedo hi kvacinnānyatra dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: For when a difference is seen in one [instance], it is not seen elsewhere;

children.text: na tasmād bhinnamastyanyat sāmānyaṃ buddhyabhedataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.126 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no separate universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) [as a real entity], since the non-difference is [merely] of cognition. // Pramāṇav_2.126 //
Therefore, sense-born cognition has only particulars (<s>viśeṣa</s>) as its object;

children.text: na viśeṣeṣu śabdānāṃ pravṛttāvasti sambhavaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.127 //
children.translated_text: there is no possibility of the application of words to particulars. // Pramāṇav_2.127 //
Due to the non-continuity of particulars, since convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) does not operate [on them],

children.text: viṣayo yaśca śabdānāṃ saṃyojyeta sa eva taiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.128 //
children.translated_text: the object of words is that which can be conjoined — that alone [is denoted] by them. // Pramāṇav_2.128 //
In the relation 'this belongs to that,' the two meanings that appear

children.text: tayoreva hi sambandho na tadendriyagocaraḥ // Pramāṇav_2.129 //
children.translated_text: — it is of those very [conceptual appearances] that there is a connection, and that is not within the range of the senses. // Pramāṇav_2.129 //
Because of the non-manifestation of the object of that which has a vivid appearance,
the difference in the appearance of cognition (<s>vijñānābhāsa</s>) is indeed what distinguishes objects. // Pramāṇav_2.130 //
Even when an object appears through the eye, that which another indicates as 'this is his' —

children.text: sa eva yojyate śabdairna khalvindriyagocaraḥ // Pramāṇav_2.131 //
children.translated_text: that alone is conjoined with words, and it is certainly not within the range of the senses. // Pramāṇav_2.131 //
Because one whose senses are not engaged cannot manifest [an object] merely through the speech of another,
and one in whom the connection [between word and object] has not arisen does not [have] cognition by itself, for it would follow absurdly. // Pramāṇav_2.132 //
Due to the simultaneous operation of the mind in both conceptual (<s>savikalpa</s>) and non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>) [cognition],
one who is confused, or due to the rapidity of their operation, determines the two to be identical. // Pramāṇav_2.133 //
If [you say] perception would be interrupted by the intervention of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) —

children.text: iti ced bhinnajātīyavikalpe 'nyasya vā katham // Pramāṇav_2.134 //
children.translated_text: then how [would this apply] when the <s>vikalpa</s> is of a different kind, or regarding another [object]? // Pramāṇav_2.134 //
If [you say] the view of the existence-side is strong, like the firebrand perception (<s>alātadṛṣṭi</s>) —

children.text: anyatrāpi samānaṃ tad varṇayorvā sakṛcchutiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.135 //
children.translated_text: that is equally [applicable] elsewhere too; or [there would be] a single perception of two colors. // Pramāṇav_2.135 //
Even though the senses here are in contact with all objects at once,
that [cognition] which appears as if uninterrupted despite the intervention of the five [sense cognitions] — // Pramāṇav_2.136 //
that cognition, due to its mixing with momentary cognitions extending to my limit,

children.text: vicchinnābheti taccitraṃ tasmāt santu sakṛddhiyaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.137 //
children.translated_text: is interrupted — therefore that [appearance of continuity] is variegated; hence, let there be momentary cognitions. // Pramāṇav_2.137 //
And how [can there be] non-difference of appearance in [cognitions] with and without an intervening [moment]?

children.text: śuddhe manovikalpe ca na kramagrahaṇaṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.138 //
children.translated_text: In a pure mental <s>vikalpa</s> too, there would be no sequential apprehension. // Pramāṇav_2.138 //
The non-apprehension that occurs even regarding an object in contact [with the senses], for one whose mind is attached elsewhere,
[arises] from the deficiency in the capacity of the other's arising — this objection applies indeed to both [sides]. // Pramāṇav_2.139 //
The rapid operation of a firebrand and the like, which obstructs [perception of] continuity,

children.text: cakrabhrāntiṃ dṛgādhatte na dṛśāṃ ghaṭanena sā // Pramāṇav_2.140 //
children.translated_text: produces the illusion of a circle (<s>cakrabhrānti</s>) — that [illusion] is not [produced] by the combination of [individual] perceptions. // Pramāṇav_2.140 //
Some assert that [sense-cognition] is free from conceptual construction because it is born of the senses, like the cognition of an infant;
and [they say] the reason for the absence of <s>vikalpa</s> in an infant is the weakness of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.141 //
For them, the [cognition] of infants would be perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) alone, since there is no conceptualization;
due to the loss of the means of convention, even afterward that [perception without conceptualization] would not occur. // Pramāṇav_2.142 //
If [you say] the mind, which has acquired convention, is considered [the basis] — therefore [conceptualization occurs] through that —
then even in sense-born [cognition] it would be the same, and if [you say] the remainder [differs], this is as follows: // Pramāṇav_2.143 //
Let that which is the means of proof in the case of an infant be stated here too;
due to the similarity of sense-cognitions, experience and the like have been stated by this [argument]. // Pramāṇav_2.144 //
Having grasped the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), the qualificand (<s>viśeṣya</s>), the connection, and the worldly convention,

children.text: gṛhītvā saṅkalayayaitat tathā pratyeti nānyathā // Pramāṇav_2.145 //
children.translated_text: one constructs this [conceptual cognition] and cognizes thus, not otherwise. // Pramāṇav_2.145 //
Just as in [the cognition of] one possessing a staff, because of the non-discrimination of genus (<s>jāti</s>) and the like,

children.text: tadvatā yojanā nāsti kalpanāpyatra nāstyataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.146 //
children.translated_text: there is no conjunction with that which possesses it — conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) also does not exist here, for that reason. // Pramāṇav_2.146 //
Moreover, that cognition which is continuous and which manifests word-particulars —
cowness (<s>gotva</s>) is described as devoid of the form of phonemes, shapes, and syllables. // Pramāṇav_2.147 //
Even though there is sameness of that very [universal], [it is] not apprehended within the range of the eye;
due to the absence of a dual appearance in cognition, the differentiation of cognition is difficult to obtain. // Pramāṇav_2.148 //
Since <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) is not apprehended by the senses, the non-perception of the relation is established.
Words such as 'the cloth is in the threads,' 'here,' and so forth — these are self-made [conventional expressions]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.149 //

children.text: śṛṅgaṃ gavīti loke syāt śṛṃge gaurityalaukikam /
children.translated_text: In the world one says 'the horn of a cow,' but 'in the horn of a cow' [as a locative of inherence] is non-conventional,
because there is no apprehension of the severance of the remaining limbs designated by the word 'cow.' // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.150 //
'This cloth is [made] from those threads' — here the effect is spoken of as subsequent;
it arises from the transformation of threads and is never simultaneous [with them]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.151 //
Someone, through superimposition on the cause, or through extraction of a single [aspect],

children.text: tantvākhyāṃ vartayet kārye darśayan nāśrayaṃ śruteḥ // Pramāṇav_2.152 //
children.translated_text: may apply the designation 'thread' to the effect, [thereby] showing that it is not the basis of the verbal expression. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.152 //
The relation of benefactor and beneficiary, or merely the perception [arising] from separation —
what is primary is that cognition which does not stumble, [and] which is the domain of the original convention. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.153 //

children.text: anumānaṃ ca jātyādau vastuno nāsti bhedini /
children.translated_text: And <s>anumāna</s> (inference) regarding <s>jāti</s> (universal) and the like does not exist in a real thing that is differentiated;

children.text: sarvatra vyapadeśo hi daṇḍādernāpi sāṃvṛtāt // Pramāṇav_2.154 //
children.translated_text: for designation everywhere — of a stick and so on — is not even from the conventional [universal]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.154 //
Words such as 'thing,' 'palace,' 'garland,' and the like do not depend on anything else [i.e., no inherence relation];

children.text: geho yadyapi saṃyogastanmālā kinnu tad bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.155 //
children.translated_text: if a house is [merely] a <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), then what would a garland of them be? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.155 //
If <s>jāti</s> (universal) were [the basis], then even a single house would be called a 'garland,' like a tree [being called a forest];
when there are many garlands, how could that word [apply] to the universal, since the universal [itself] has no universal? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.156 //
And in the case of a garland and so forth, [qualities] such as greatness, which are held to be metaphorical —
they are not metaphorical, because they are apprehended by a cognition indistinct from the primary [cognition]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.157 //
The absence of any other cause is equally [present] in those considered primary as well;

children.text: padārthaśabdaḥ kaṃ hetumanyaṃ ṣaṭsu samīkṣate // Pramāṇav_2.158 //
children.translated_text: the word '<s>padārtha</s>' (category) — what other cause does it look for among the six [categories]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.158 //
That which is established as it is through convention, and that which is called so due to similarity with it —
these are the primary and the <s>gauṇa</s> (secondary/metaphorical); even among existents, [the designation] of non-existence is through metaphor. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.159 //
Convention follows the <s>rūḍhi</s> (established usage), and that [secondary usage] follows the intention of the speaker;
it is made for the purpose of everyday practice, like the words for metre, syllable, and name. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.160 //
Objects, solely by virtue of being properties of real things, are the cause of such cognition;

children.text: bhede 'pi yatra tajjñānaṃ tāṃstathā pratipadyate // Pramāṇav_2.161 //
children.translated_text: even when there is difference, wherever that cognition [arises], it apprehends them as such. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.161 //
Cognitions too, likewise, despite difference, in the reflective awareness of difference —
thus the connection of the non-separation from effects of that [cognition] is not of a single real thing. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.162 //

children.text: vastūnāṃ vidyate tasmāt tanniṣṭhā vastuni śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, among real things there exists [such connection]; hence verbal expression is grounded in a real thing;
even in the absence of grounding in the exclusion of external capacities, that verbal expression [still operates]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.163 //
It is bound to the <s>vikalpa</s>-reflections (conceptual images) that are grounded in that [object];
therefore, since it is grounded in the exclusion of others, verbal expression is said to operate through <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other). // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.164 //
That which appears in cognition as a reflection of the object, as if through differentiation —

children.text: śabdāt tadapi nārthātmā bhrāntiḥ sā vāsanodbhavā // Pramāṇav_2.165 //
children.translated_text: that too, [arising] from words, is not the nature of the [real] object; it is an error born of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions). // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.165 //
In the designation of that [reflection], what aspect of the [real] object is apprehended through verbal expressions?

children.text: tasyāgato ca saṃketakriyā vyarthā tadarthikā // Pramāṇav_2.166 //
children.translated_text: And the activity of convention directed toward that [reflection] is futile for one who seeks the [real] object. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.166 //
Which aspect of the object does a word convey? — In that regard, <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) is stated;

children.text: ākāraḥ sa ca nārthe 'sti taṃ vadannarthabhāk katham // Pramāṇav_2.167 //
children.translated_text: and that form does not exist in the [external] object — how then can one who speaks of it partake of the object? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.167 //
The effect of a word that has a connection is [produced] together with the object that has a connection, and that [word]
is non-connected [with the object directly]; due to non-difference from cognition, [the connection] is constructed through the habit of seeing. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.168 //
Through the superimposition of that form, and again through the apprehension of exclusion from others,

children.text: śabdārtho 'rthaḥ sa eveti vacane na virudhyate // Pramāṇav_2.169 //
children.translated_text: the statement 'the meaning of the word is the object itself' is not contradicted. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.169 //
Indeed, these cognitions produced by words are falsely appearing;
and [yet] they follow this portion of the object — thus verbal expression operates through <s>apoha</s> (exclusion). // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.170 //
Therefore, even at the time of convention, [the word] being associated with the indicated object,
<s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) is connected with verbal expression through the fruit of its own cognition. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.171 //
Because it depends on the non-seeing [of something] elsewhere, and because in some cases it depends on seeing that [elsewhere],

children.text: śrutau sambadhyate 'poho naitad vastuni yujyate // Pramāṇav_2.172 //
children.translated_text: <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is connected with verbal expression — this does not apply to a real thing. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.172 //

children.text: tasmād jātyāditadyogā nārthe teṣu ca na śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>jāti</s> (universal) and the like, and their connections, do not [exist] in the object, and verbal expression is not
connected with those [universals]; it is connected only with the exclusion of others, through the application of words alone. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.173 //
The means of recollecting the convention has the nature of combining what has been seen;
how [can this occur] in visual cognition, which is devoid of reflection on prior and subsequent [moments]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.174 //
Even one whose mind has gone elsewhere perceives form with the eye;
the non-apprehension of the convention regarding that [form] is clear there, and conceptual construction born from it [comes later]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.175 //
Conceptual constructions arise there where a word has been applied;
therefore they would operate from intention — sense-born [cognitions] would not perceive external [objects conceptually]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.176 //
One perceives 'form, form' — what does one perceive of the cognition of it?

children.text: asti cānubhavastasyāḥ so 'vikalpaḥ kathaṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.177 //
children.translated_text: And there is experience of that [cognition]; how could it be <s>avikalpa</s> (non-conceptual)? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.177 //
Through that very [cognition] in experience it is seen — two conceptual cognitions do not [occur] simultaneously;
by this, the experience of another cognition simultaneous [with the first] is also accounted for. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.178 //
And memory would occur regarding the past — how could it occur regarding what has not been apprehended?
And the cognition of one's own cognition could have a form indistinct from the determination by another cognition. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.179 //
Cognition of an object that is past, not seen, and without any inferential mark —

children.text: siddhaṃ tatkena tasmin hi na pratyakṣaṃ na laiṅgikam // Pramāṇav_2.180 //
children.translated_text: that is established [as impossible]; for regarding it, there is neither <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) nor inference from marks. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.180 //
If it were apprehended by an immediately subsequent cognition that manifests its own form,

children.text: rūpādiriva gṛhyeta na syāt tatpūrvadhīgrahaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.181 //
children.translated_text: like form and the like, then there would be no apprehension of the preceding cognition [as past]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.181 //
That [cognition] is <s>avikalpa</s> (non-conceptual), having its own object — just as the experience of consciousness [is];
likewise, that other [cognition] too is non-conceptual, being incapable of convention. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.182 //
Words denote <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal), and conceptual construction too has that single meaning;
in the absence of <s>nirvikalpa</s> (non-conceptual cognition), how would apprehension of particulars [occur]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.183 //
If [you say] it exists and is non-conceptual, then something having the same cause,

children.text: sarva tathaiva hetorhi bhedād bhedaḥ phalātmanām // Pramāṇav_2.184 //
children.translated_text: everything would be just like that — for from difference of cause, there is difference in the nature of results. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.184 //
The application [of words] from the recollection of convention does not depend on external objects;
likewise, visual cognition, without depending on convention, [operates] solely through the power of the real thing. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.185 //
If the form in sense-cognition depended on the recollection of convention,

children.text: anapekṣya na cecchaktaṃ syāt smṛtāveva liṃgavat // Pramāṇav_2.186 //
children.translated_text: then, if it were incapable without depending [on convention], it would be like an inferential mark, [operative] only in memory. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.186 //
Since that [visual cognition] arises from contact with that [object], visual cognition would arise from memory or not;

children.text: tataḥ kālāntare 'pi syāt kvacid vyākṣepasambhavāt // Pramāṇav_2.187 //
children.translated_text: therefore it could [arise] even at another time, since distraction is possible in some cases. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.187 //
If both causes [operate] sequentially, then it should arise even earlier, due to non-difference;
if the cause of sense-cognition is something else, then memory is also purposeless regarding it. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.188 //
Just as the recollection of convention is accepted for the purpose of establishing what has not been established,
and the difference to be apprehended is [itself] unestablished — what purpose does memory serve there? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.189 //
In the apprehension of the mere universal, dependence on difference is not logical;

children.text: tasmāccakṣuśca rūpaṃ ca pratītyodeti netradhīḥ // Pramāṇav_2.190 //
children.translated_text: therefore, visual cognition arises dependent on the eye and form [alone]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.190 //
And the object is capable of directly generating cognition, just like the sense-faculty;

children.text: atha kasmād dvayādhīnajanma tat tena nocyate // Pramāṇav_2.191 //
children.translated_text: then why is it not called that [i.e., a sense], since its production depends on both? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.191 //
For designation is applied after examining the indicative function;
and that [indicative function] exists in the designation as 'sense-[cognition],' so let the property of that be applied. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.192 //
Therefore, let the nature of an inferential mark be applied in [this] designation;
[it] ceases with the cessation of the pervading nature. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.193 //

children.text: sañcitaḥ samudāyaḥ sa sāmānyaṃ tatra cākṣadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: That aggregate, assembled together — <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) is there, and visual cognition [apprehends] it;
and the cognition of universals is necessarily accompanied by <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction). // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.194 //
Those other atoms that arise from connection with a different object —

children.text: uktāste sañcitāste hi nimittaṃ jñānajanmanaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.195 //
children.translated_text: they have been described; for those assembled [atoms] are the cause of the arising of cognition. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.195 //
And that particularity of atoms [does not arise] without other atoms;
cognition that is not confined to one of them alone has been described as having <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) as its object. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.196 //
Now, even though [they share] a single sense-field, multiple [objects] are not perceived simultaneously;
what would be the appearance of simultaneous apprehension in the case of separate sesame seeds and the like? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.197 //
The lightness [of cognition] employed here [applies] only to those [atoms] falling in sequence;
why is there not a non-sequential apprehension, [since] all cognitions of this [perceiver] are simultaneous? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.198 //
Are some among those [cognitions] appearing without sequence, while others have sequence?
In the apprehension of all objects, therefore, this absence of sequence would follow absurdly. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.199 //

children.text: nai kaṃ citrapataṃgādi rūpaṃ vā dṛśyate katham /
children.translated_text: How is a single variegated form — such as a butterfly — perceived?

children.text: citraṃ tadekāmiti cedidaṃ citrataraṃ tataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.200 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] 'that variegated [form] is one,' then this is even more variegated than that. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.200 //

children.text: naikasvabhāvaṃ citraṃ hi maṇirūpaṃ yathaiva tat /
children.translated_text: For the variegated is not of a single nature — just as that which has the form of a jewel;
and the appearance of blue and so forth is the same in variegated cloths and the like. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.201 //
If there only the form of the parts is perceived as such,
then, setting aside blue and the like, if you perceive something else as 'variegated' — [what is] that variegated [thing]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.202 //
Of two [cognitions] characterized by having the same object-aspect and same time,
if one has sequence and [apprehends] many objects, why would the other, [apprehending] one object without sequence, [be different]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.203 //
It is precisely due to the manifold nature of cognitions that things have manifold nature;
if that [manifoldness of cognition] were not a component [of reality], by what would this establishment of difference be proved? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.204 //
Since dissimilar [elements] are not produced [together], there is no cognition of variegation in a painting and the like;
since [colour] is formless, there is no variegated conjunction, and it is not the basis of portions. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.205 //
Since each individually is not variegated, and when they are apprehended in sequence,
there is no combining into a cognition of variegation — because one [cognition] does not apprehend many [simultaneously]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.206 //
Therefore, a single [cognition] having many objects would be established as also non-conceptual;
[for] one who conceptually constructs a single object thereby also perceives another. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.207 //
Now, if oneness is not tenable in [cognitions with] variegated appearances,

children.text: saiva tāvat kathaṃ buddhirekā citrāvabhāsinī // Pramāṇav_2.208 //
children.translated_text: then how is that very cognition — a single one — appearing as variegated [possible]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.208 //
This is arrived at by the force of reality, as the wise declare:

children.text: yathā yathārthāścintyante viśīryante tathā tathā // Pramāṇav_2.209 //
children.translated_text: the more objects are analyzed, the more they disintegrate. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.209 //

children.text: kiṃ syāt sā citrataikasyām na syāt tasyāṃ matāvapi /
children.translated_text: Would that variegation exist in the one [cognition] or not, even on your view?

children.text: yadīdaṃ svayamarthānāṃ rocate tatra ke vayam // Pramāṇav_2.210 //
children.translated_text: If the objects themselves are pleased with this [arrangement], then who are we [to object]? // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.210 //
Therefore, neither in objects nor in cognition [is there] a gross appearance of that nature;

children.text: ekatra pratiṣiddhitvād bahuṣvapi na sambhavaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.211 //
children.translated_text: since it is refuted in one [case], it is also impossible in many. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.211 //
This internal determination is a portion [appearing] as if situated externally;

children.text: jñānasyābhedinau bhinnau pratibhāso h yupaplavaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.212 //
children.translated_text: the appearance of cognition — [seemingly] divided though undivided — is an error. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.212 //
There, by the absence of even one [of the pair], both are nullified;

children.text: tasmāt tadeva tasyāpi tattvaṃ yā dvayaśūnyatā // Pramāṇav_2.213 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the true nature of that [cognition] too is that very emptiness of the duality. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.213 //
And this establishment of the differentiation of things depends on the differentiation of that [cognition];
when that error ceases, the differentiation of those [things] too is an error [that ceases]. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.214 //
There is no characteristic that is external in the form of <s>grāhya</s> (apprehended) and <s>grāhaka</s> (apprehender);
therefore, being empty of characteristics, [all <s>dharmas</s>] are revealed as <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> (without own-nature). // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.215 //
All characteristics of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth in particular are conditioned by functional activity;

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ sa ca tattvaṃ na tenāpyete vilakṣaṇāḥ // Pramāṇav_2.216 //
children.translated_text: and that [activity] is not the ultimate truth — therefore these too are without [real] characteristics. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.216 //
Depending on their respective conditions, for those whose nature is afflicted by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),
<s>vijñapti</s> (representation/consciousness) arises with a false appearance, like [the visions of one with] an eye-disease. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.217 //
And that [representation], whose true nature is not known, by all other cognitions —
because [true cognition] is impossible without the errors of <s>grāhya</s> (apprehended) and <s>grāhaka</s> (apprehender) in them. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.218 //
Those who have disregarded the true nature of reality, performing the 'elephant-eye-closing' [i.e., willful ignorance],
elaborate the conception of the external merely through worldly understanding alone. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.219 //
Blue and the like, in variegated consciousness, are a condition of cognition and do not partake of anything else;

children.text: aśakyadarśanaḥ taṃ hi patatyarthe vivecayan // Pramāṇav_2.220 //
children.translated_text: being impossible to see [as separate], one who discriminates it falls into [the error of reifying] the object. // <s>Pramāṇav</s> 2.220 //

children.text: yad yathā bhāsate jñānaṃ tat tathaiva prakāśate /
children.translated_text: Whatever cognition appears in whatever manner, that is illuminated just as it is,
thus there would be no unity of name for the variegated aspect (<s>citrākāra</s>) in the mind. // Pramāṇav_2.221 //
If there were unity of form such as cloth and the like, there would likewise be non-discrimination;

children.text: vivekīni nirasyānyadā viveki ca nekṣate // Pramāṇav_2.222 //
children.translated_text: that which discriminates, having excluded the other, does not perceive while discriminating. // Pramāṇav_2.222 //

children.text: ko vā virodho bahavaḥ sañjātātiśayāḥ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Or what contradiction is there if many [causes], each having produced their respective excellence,
were to be the cause of cognition, just as the self, sense faculties, and so forth are not [contradictory]? // Pramāṇav_2.223 //

children.text: hetubhāvād ṛte nānyā grāhyatā nāma kācana /
children.translated_text: There is no so-called apprehensibility (<s>grāhyatā</s>) apart from being a cause;
that of whose aspect (<s>ākāra</s>) the cognition partakes — that is said to be apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.224 //

children.text: kathaṃ vāvayavī grāhyā sakṛt svāvayavaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: How can a whole (<s>avayavī</s>) be apprehended simultaneously with its parts?

children.text: na hi gopratyayo dṛṣṭaḥ sāsnādīnāmadarśane // Pramāṇav_2.225 //
children.translated_text: For a cognition of a cow is not observed when the dewlap and other [parts] are not perceived. // Pramāṇav_2.225 //
If the apprehension of the qualifier and the principal together is also accepted,

children.text: sampūrṇāṅgo na gṛhyeta sakṛnnāpi guṇādimān // Pramāṇav_2.226 //
children.translated_text: then one with complete limbs would never be apprehended at once, nor one possessing qualities and the like. // Pramāṇav_2.226 //
Since the qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>) and the qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>) depend on the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>),

children.text: yadṅgabhāvenopāttaṃ tat tenaiva hi gṛhyate // Pramāṇav_2.227 //
children.translated_text: that which is taken up as a subordinate part is apprehended precisely through that [intention]. // Pramāṇav_2.227 //
Due to the intrinsic non-difference from other entities, and due to the non-apprehension
of the differentiator such as quality and the like, there would be a single cognition even for one who sees successive [objects]. // Pramāṇav_2.228 //
If the apprehension of plurality is through grasping differences of quality and the like,

children.text: astu nāma tathāpyeṣāṃ bhavet sambandhisaṅkaraḥ // Pramāṇav_2.229 //
children.translated_text: let it be so; nevertheless, there would be a confusion of the relata of these. // Pramāṇav_2.229 //
Since sound and the like are multiple, the simultaneous apprehension of many is established,
because there is no possibility of apprehending the configuration when the configured [elements] are not apprehended. // Pramāṇav_2.230 //
The exclusion of that which is excluded from everything [else proceeds] from this and from that;
that manifoldness of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), whose distinctions are derived from those distinctions. // Pramāṇav_2.231 //
Those [distinctions] are conceptually constructed (<s>kalpita</s>) through difference of form, by the non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) mind;

children.text: na vicitrasya citrābhāḥ kādācitkasya gocaraḥ // Pramāṇav_2.232 //
children.translated_text: the domain of the occasional [cognition] is not the variegated appearances of the variegated [object]. // Pramāṇav_2.232 //
Although whiteness and the like exist as objects of the sense faculties of a certain kind,
they are not denoted by words; one should know [this] from the difference of form. // Pramāṇav_2.233 //
Even when cognitions have a single object, if [they differ] due to having different bases,
then how [can one say] that the auditory and other mental [cognitions] now have different objects? // Pramāṇav_2.234 //
Granted that the basis of cognitions is one thing and another for that entity;

children.text: ekasyaiva kuto rūpaṃ bhinnākārāvabhāsi tat // Pramāṇav_2.235 //
children.translated_text: how then does a single [object] have a form that manifests in different aspects (<s>ākāra</s>)? // Pramāṇav_2.235 //
Through the operation of reflective grasping of the visible, of verbal expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>) and conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>),
the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) of cows and the like is refuted from observation. // Pramāṇav_2.236 //
And whatever inference through positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of verbal expression and conceptual construction
regarding universal (<s>jāti</s>) and the like in the visible [object] such as a cow — that too is refuted by this [argument]. // Pramāṇav_2.237 //
Perceptions themselves, though different, produce a single conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>),
enumerated as recognition — this has been explained as being by their own nature. // Pramāṇav_2.238 //
If the mental [cognition] apprehends what was previously experienced, it would lack validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>);
if it apprehends what was not seen, then even a blind person and the like would have perception of objects. // Pramāṇav_2.239 //
Because [cognition] is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), there is no possibility of a past perception [continuing];
if [things] were non-momentary, then the definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) together with its qualifier would need to be stated. // Pramāṇav_2.240 //
When the action has been accomplished, if [something] does not produce any further distinction,
why is another instrument posited for that action, whether sensory or otherwise? // Pramāṇav_2.241 //
And the simultaneous arising of all cognitions born from that [cause],
because there is no contradiction in the dependence of that whose effect-distinction is not produced by others. // Pramāṇav_2.242 //
Therefore, the mental [cognition], arising as the immediately succeeding condition (<s>anantarapratyaya</s>) from sensory cognition,

children.text: mano 'nyameva gṛhṇāti viṣayaṃ nāndhadṛk tataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.243 //
children.translated_text: apprehends a different object — hence one who is blind does not [perceive] from that [mental cognition alone]. // Pramāṇav_2.243 //
The sense-born cognition is the cause insofar as it requires positive concomitance with its own object;
therefore, when it apprehends something else, its having a determined object of apprehension is maintained. // Pramāṇav_2.244 //
If [one asks] how the object, whose action-time is not equal to that [of cognition], can be a cooperating condition
simultaneous with its own cognition — [we reply regarding] sense cognition: // Pramāṇav_2.245 //
Because of the incapacity of what is non-existent beforehand, and the uselessness [of what exists] afterwards,

children.text: prāgbhāvaḥ sarvahetūnāṃ nāti 'rtha svadhiyā saha // Pramāṇav_2.246 //
children.translated_text: the prior existence of all causes does not exceed [the requirement of being together] with their own cognition. // Pramāṇav_2.246 //

children.text: bhinnakālaṃ kathaṃ grāhyamiti ced grāhyātāṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: If [one asks] how can what belongs to a different time be apprehended — those who know reasoning understand apprehensibility
to be nothing but causal efficacy (<s>hetutva</s>), the capacity to impart its aspect (<s>ākāra</s>) to cognition. // Pramāṇav_2.247 //
For even when an effect has multiple causes, that which arises conforming [to a particular cause],

children.text: tat tenāpyatra tadrūpaṃ gṛhītamiti cocyate // Pramāṇav_2.248 //
children.translated_text: is said to have been apprehended by that [cause] as bearing its form, even in this case. // Pramāṇav_2.248 //
For the self (<s>ātman</s>), whose convention cannot be established [externally], being inseparable from desire (<s>rāga</s>) and the like,
therefore their self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>) is not accompanied by verbal designation (<s>abhijalpa</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.249 //

children.text: avedakāḥ parasyāpi te svarūpaṃ kathaṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: If they do not cognize the other, how do they know their own nature?
Some [say]: they are known by a cognition residing in the same object. // Pramāṇav_2.250 //
Entities that are of that or not-that form, born from causes of that or not-that form —
is that pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like unknowing? [No,] for it is born from a cause not different from cognition. // Pramāṇav_2.251 //
When the object exists, the sense faculty is fit, and the mind is in its proper [state],

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ janma sukhādīnāṃ tat tulyaṃ manasāmapi // Pramāṇav_2.252 //
children.translated_text: the arising of pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like is observed — the same holds for mental [cognitions] as well. // Pramāṇav_2.252 //

children.text: asatsu satsu caiteṣu na janmājanma vā kvacit /
children.translated_text: When these [conditions] are absent or present, neither the arising nor the non-arising

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ sukhāderbuddhervā tat tato nānyaśca te // Pramāṇav_2.253 //
children.translated_text: of pleasure and the like, or of cognition, is observed [independently] — and they are not from anything else. // Pramāṇav_2.253 //
The differentiation into pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), and the like is due to the particular [conditions]
of those very [cognitions], just as the dullness and sharpness of that very cognition depend on [conditions]. // Pramāṇav_2.254 //
Through the encounter with which object cognition, pleasure, and the like arise —

children.text: multvā taṃ pratipadyeta sukhādīneva sā kathan // Pramāṇav_2.255 //
children.translated_text: how could that [cognition], abandoning that [object], apprehend pleasure and the like alone? // Pramāṇav_2.255 //
If [awareness] were uninterrupted, its self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>) would not appear in sequential apprehension;
if [you say it is] due to the subtlety of that — then why not equally [say] there is no awareness [of the object]? // Pramāṇav_2.256 //
And there is no knowledge of two by a single [cognition], because of the restriction of sense-cognition;
and even in the absence of pleasure and the like, [cognition] arises from the object, because the capacity of that [to produce pleasure] is not established. // Pramāṇav_2.257 //

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak ca sāmarthye dvayornīlādivat sukham /
children.translated_text: If each of the two has a separate capacity, like blue and the like, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>)
would be apprehended in isolation — but for one who does not apprehend the object that is its cause. // Pramāṇav_2.258 //

children.text: na hi saṃvedanaṃ yuktam arthenaiva saha grahe /
children.translated_text: For awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) is not logically possible only when there is apprehension together with the object;

children.text: kiṃ sāmarthya sukhādīnāṃ neṣṭā dhīryat tadudbhavā // Pramāṇav_2.259 //
children.translated_text: what capacity do pleasure and the like have? Is the cognition born from that not accepted? // Pramāṇav_2.259 //
If pleasure and the like were cognized without the object, by the eye and other [senses],

children.text: rūpādiḥ stryādibhedo 'kṣraṇā na gṛhyeta kadācana // Pramāṇav_2.260 //
children.translated_text: then the difference of form and the like, [and of] women and the like, would never be apprehended by the senses. // Pramāṇav_2.260 //
For when a truly internal object exists and [cognition] is capable, the cognition that is outward-seeing —
in its apprehension of the object, there would be non-awareness of the pleasure and the like born from it. // Pramāṇav_2.261 //
If two cognitions arise simultaneously, since each has its own object as its [sufficient] ground,
there would be cognition of pleasure and pain at the same time as [cognition of] the object arises. // Pramāṇav_2.262 //
Even if there is another material cause (<s>upādāna</s>), there is the arising of pain and the like in cognition;
if [you say] the material cause of what is contrary to that is one — that is not our position. // Pramāṇav_2.263 //
By what is the consciousness that does not know that [object] a material cause?

children.text: ādhipatyaṃ tu kurvīta tadvirudve 'pi dṛśyate // Pramāṇav_2.264 //
children.translated_text: But it may exercise dominance (<s>ādhipatya</s>) — [for] that is seen even in what is contrary. // Pramāṇav_2.264 //
Just as light, in the case of the two senses, for the nocturnal creature and the other,
produces simultaneously deficiency and non-deficiency in the seeing of form. // Pramāṇav_2.265 //
Therefore, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like, of the objects that appear as transferred to themselves,
are the experiencers of their own selves, and the arising of these from objects is merely [causal]. // Pramāṇav_2.266 //
For the object-nature, being of their own nature, is experienced by them through those [cognitions];
hence the designation 'experience of the object' (<s>arthānubhava</s>), while the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) is that which is brought by it. // Pramāṇav_2.267 //
Someone says that pleasure and the like, standing externally, are non-conscious,

children.text: grāhyānāha na tasyāpi sakṛd yukto dvayagrahaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.268 //
children.translated_text: [yet] apprehensible — but for him too, simultaneous apprehension of the two is not logical. // Pramāṇav_2.268 //
If there is simultaneous apprehension because pleasure and the like are of a form not different from blue and so forth,
[then] what is different in appearance — white, pain, and so forth — [and what is] not different — [are these matters of] cognition or experience?
If there is no distinction in the external [object], then due to the gradation of habitual cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
the gradation would be in the cognition, not in pleasure and distress. // Pramāṇav_2.270 //
Even if there is no contradiction in cognition having the nature of pleasure and the like,

children.text: sa idānīṃ kathaṃ bāhyāḥ sukhādyātmeti gamyate // Pramāṇav_2.271 //
children.translated_text: how then is it now understood that external [objects] have the nature of pleasure and the like? // Pramāṇav_2.271 //
If [you say it is] because what is unapprehensible cannot apprehend — [then] a person, being of a different class,

children.text: agrāhakaḥ syāt sarvasya tato hīyeta bhoktṛtā // Pramāṇav_2.272 //
children.translated_text: would be a non-apprehender of everything, and thereby experiencer-hood (<s>bhoktṛtā</s>) would be lost. // Pramāṇav_2.272 //
This [objection] is answered by the cause-effect relation; when there is no apprehensible-apprehender [relation] in cause and effect,
if it exists, that [relation] would exist elsewhere too. // Pramāṇav_2.273 //

children.text: tasmāt ta āntarā eva saṃvedyatvācca cetanāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, those [pleasure and the like] are internal indeed, and because they are experienced, they are conscious;

children.text: saṃvedanaṃ na yad rūpaṃ na hi tat tasya vedanam // Pramāṇav_2.274 //
children.translated_text: that which is not of the nature of awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) — that indeed is not the experience of it. // Pramāṇav_2.274 //
If [you say] experience whose nature is not that [of awareness] apprehends those cognitive [states] —
apart from direct perception and memory-shaped awareness (<s>saṃvitti</s>), what cognition is there here? // Pramāṇav_2.275 //
Taking up those various objects, the experience of pleasure, pain, and the like

children.text: ekamāvirbhavad dṛṣṭaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ tvanyadantarā // Pramāṇav_2.276 //
children.translated_text: is observed arising as one; but no other [experience] is observed in between. // Pramāṇav_2.276 //
If [you say] non-difference [arises] from contact — [then] just as with [the argument about] the non-conjunction [of atoms],
the determination of difference and non-difference would be destroyed in all entities. // Pramāṇav_2.277 //
The unity of undifferentiated experience — if that is not so, then with differentiation
it would be established; but if it [i.e., unity] is not an instrument of proof, the proof of difference is not established either. // Pramāṇav_2.278 //
What is different in appearance — white, pain, and the like — [and what is] not different in cognition and experience;

children.text: abhinnābhe vibhinne ced bhedābhedau kimāśrayau // Pramāṇav_2.279 //
children.translated_text: if the undifferentiated in appearance were differentiated — on what would difference and non-difference rest? // Pramāṇav_2.279 //
Because even for one with sharp [intellect], there is occasional perception of non-difference among the concealed [aspects],
the determination of difference in the stream of awareness-distinctions is established. // Pramāṇav_2.280 //

children.text: prāguktaṃ yogināṃ jñānaṃ teṣāṃ tad bhāvanāmayam /
children.translated_text: The cognition of <s>yogins</s> mentioned earlier — that [cognition] of theirs is born of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
having dispelled the net of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>), it manifests clearly indeed. // Pramāṇav_2.281 //
Those afflicted by desire (<s>kāma</s>), grief (<s>śoka</s>), fear (<s>bhaya</s>), madness (<s>unmāda</s>), theft, dreams, and the like
see even what is non-existent as though standing before them. // Pramāṇav_2.282 //
That which is accompanied by conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) does not have the manifestation of a clear object;

children.text: svapne 'pi smaryate smārta na ca tat tādṛgarthavat // Pramāṇav_2.283 //
children.translated_text: even in a dream, what is remembered is of the nature of memory (<s>smārta</s>), and that is not [endowed] with an object of such [clarity]. // Pramāṇav_2.283 //
The <s>aśubhā</s> (contemplation of impurity), <s>pṛthivīkṛtsna</s> (earth-totality meditation), and the like — though non-existent — are described as
having clear appearance and being non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), produced by the power of meditation (<s>bhāvanābala</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.284 //
Therefore, whether existent or non-existent, whatever is intensively meditated upon,
at the completion of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), that bears the fruit of clear, non-conceptual cognition. // Pramāṇav_2.285 //

children.text: tatra pramāṇaṃ saṃvādi yat prāṅ nirṇītavastuvat /
children.translated_text: Among those, that which is concordant [with reality] (<s>saṃvādi</s>), like a previously ascertained object,

children.text: tad bhāvānājaṃ pratyakṣamiṣṭam śeṣā upaplavāḥ // Pramāṇav_2.286 //
children.translated_text: that [cognition] born of meditation on real entities is accepted as <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception); the rest are disturbances (<s>upaplava</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.286 //

children.text: śabdārthagrāhi yad yatra tajjñānaṃ tatra kalpanā /
children.translated_text: Whatever cognition in whatever context apprehends the meaning of words (<s>śabdārtha</s>) — that cognition there is conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>);
and the own-form (<s>svarūpa</s>) is not the meaning of a word — therefore all of that is direct perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.287 //
The threefold conceptual [cognition]: ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), that arising from disturbance of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>),
and the one that is non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>) — [together these constitute] the fourfold [classification of] perception-like [cognition]. // Pramāṇav_2.288 //
In order to establish that [the first] two are not born from the senses, since they are seen to be erroneous,
the statement [that perception is] like established inference is for the purpose of proving the first two [to be non-perceptual]. // Pramāṇav_2.289 //
The conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) that depend on convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) and involve the superimposition of other meanings —
because they never follow upon direct perception, they are never a cause of error. // Pramāṇav_2.290 //
Just as this conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) of a non-present object, being of the nature of memory (<s>smaraṇa</s>),
requires convention and does not directly ascertain the object — // Pramāṇav_2.291 //
so too, without the remembrance of what was previously experienced, regarding pots and the like,
there is no cognition that follows [from conceptual construction] — and that falls away from <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). // Pramāṇav_2.292 //
The fourth [type] here is the exclusion (<s>apavāda</s>); hence it is said [to be] born from disturbance (<s>upaghāta</s>).
Merely, in that case, <s>timira</s> (visual defect) is an indicator of disturbance (<s>upaghāta</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.293 //
Some [say] that too is mental (<s>mānasa</s>) — their thesis is contradicted.
As for the argument that the senses are also the cause of cognitions of blue, two moons, and the like — 294 //
If the sense [is] an indirect cause through a chain [of causation], in the domain of sense-cognition,
when examined, what relevance does the mental [cognition] have here? // Pramāṇav_2.295 //
Is it rather a sense-cognition? If it follows the presence and absence of the senses,

children.text: tat tulyaṃ vikriyāvaccet saiveyaṃ kiṃ niṣidhyate // Pramāṇav_2.296 //
children.translated_text: if it is equally subject to modification — then what exactly is being denied about it? // Pramāṇav_2.296 //
Like the error of [seeing] snakes and the like, even with a defect of the senses,
its cessation would not cease even when the sensory disturbance has ceased. // Pramāṇav_2.297 //
Sometimes in another [mental] continuum (<s>santāna</s>), it would be implanted in just the same way by verbal [instruction];
it would depend on the memory of what was seen, and would not appear clearly manifest. // Pramāṇav_2.298 //

children.text: suptasya jāgrato vāpi yaiva dhīḥ sphuṭabhāsinī /
children.translated_text: Whether of one asleep or awake, that very cognition which manifests clearly —
that is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpa</s>) in both cases, whereas the conceptual (<s>vikalpikā</s>) is otherwise [i.e., not clear]. // Pramāṇav_2.299 //
Therefore, even though it is non-conceptual, its validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) is denied,

children.text: visaṃvādāt tadartha ca pratyakṣābhaṃ dvidhoditam // Pramāṇav_2.300 //
children.translated_text: because of discordance (<s>visaṃvāda</s>); and for that purpose, the perception-like [cognition] has been stated to be twofold. // Pramāṇav_2.300 //
The means of accomplishment (<s>sādhana</s>) of an action (<s>kriyā</s>) — this alone is the instrument (<s>sādhana</s>) for all of every action;

children.text: sādhanaṃ na hi tasya sādhanaṃ yā kriyā yataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.301 //
children.translated_text: for that is not the instrument of that whose action it is, because — // Pramāṇav_2.301 //
in that case, cognition, being of a nature conforming [to the object], is to be understood through mere experience (<s>anubhava</s>);

children.text: bhāvyaṃ tenātnamā yena pratikarma vibhajyate // Pramāṇav_2.302 //
children.translated_text: by that [aspect] which is its own nature (<s>ātman</s>), it is differentiated with respect to each object (<s>karman</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.302 //
A differentiation that is not part of its own nature (<s>ātman</s>), even though present in the causes (<s>hetu</s>),

children.text: bhinne karmaṇyabhinnasya na bhedena niyāmakaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.303 //
children.translated_text: does not determine a differentiation in something undifferentiated when the object is differentiated. // Pramāṇav_2.303 //
Therefore, since its apprehension arises from the differentiation of its own nature —

children.text: kriyāyāḥ karmaniyamaḥ siddhā sā tatprasādhanā // Pramāṇav_2.304 //
children.translated_text: this is the restriction of action to object; that [cognition] is established as accomplishing that [apprehension]. // Pramāṇav_2.304 //
The object connects it [cognition with apprehension]; for apart from the form of the object (<s>artharūpatā</s>),
there is no other differentiator of cognition apart from its own differentiation, in any way whatsoever. // Pramāṇav_2.305 //
Therefore, the bearing of the form of the object (<s>meyarūpatā</s>) is the instrument (<s>sādhana</s>) for apprehending the knowable (<s>prameya</s>);
in another instrument [apart from this], the relation of that [apprehension] to action is not established. // Pramāṇav_2.306 //

children.text: sā ca tasyātmabhūtaiva tena nārthāntaraṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: And that [object-form] is indeed the very nature (<s>ātmabhūta</s>) of that [cognition]; therefore the result (<s>phala</s>) is not something different,
and that [cognition], bearing that [form] within itself, [functions] through the nature of apprehending the object. // Pramāṇav_2.307 //
It appears as if endowed with activity (<s>vyāpāra</s>), through [its] operation upon its own object;
because of its determination by that [object], even though it is itself without agenthood (<s>akāraka</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.308 //
Just as, because the effect arises with a nature conforming to the causes,
the grasping of the form of the cause is spoken of in the world, even though [it] is without [real] action. // Pramāṇav_2.309 //
Of bare perception (<s>ālocana</s>), sense-contact, and qualifying cognitions — moreover —

children.text: neṣṭaṃ prāmāṇyameteṣāṃ vyavadhānāt kriyāṃ prati // Pramāṇav_2.310 //
children.translated_text: the status of being a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is not accepted for these, because of their separation from the action [of cognition]. // Pramāṇav_2.310 //
Although all the causal factors (<s>kāraka</s>) are useful for the action,

children.text: yadantyaṃ bhedakaṃ tasyāstat sādhakatamaṃ matam // Pramāṇav_2.311 //
children.translated_text: that which is the ultimate differentiator of it — that is regarded as the most effective instrument (<s>sādhaka</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.311 //
The senses, being causes in common [for all cognitions], do not have such [differentiating power];
for even when [the object] is differentiated, how can something not of that nature [determine] 'this is that'? // Pramāṇav_2.312 //
By this, the rest is also explained. As for the qualifying cognitions,

children.text: atādrū pye na bhedo 'pi tadvadanyadhiyo 'pi vā // Pramāṇav_2.313 //
children.translated_text: when there is no conformity [with the object], there is no differentiation either — or else other cognitions would also [qualify]. // Pramāṇav_2.313 //
A difference in object-domain between the two — the action (<s>kriyā</s>) and the instrument (<s>sādhana</s>) — is not accepted;

children.text: ekārthatve dvayaṃ vyartha na ca syāt kramabhāvitā // Pramāṇav_2.314 //
children.translated_text: if both had the same object, the pair would be redundant; nor would there be sequential arising (<s>kramabhāvitā</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.314 //
The absence of the relation of means and end when cognitions arise simultaneously in the mind —
the establishment of means and end is based on the determination of that [sequential relation]. // Pramāṇav_2.315 //
Even what is connected in every aspect is apprehended only through certain

children.text: dharmeḥ sa niyamo na syāt sambandhasyāviśeṣataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.316 //
children.translated_text: properties (<s>dharma</s>); that restriction would not exist given the non-particularity of the connection. // Pramāṇav_2.316 //
Since even without a difference in that, this differentiation [exists] — therefore its validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) —
if from a disposition (<s>saṃskāra</s>), then in the absence of conformity [with the object], even that [disposition] would be unstable. // Pramāṇav_2.317 //
If [one objects that] there is a contradiction in the identity of action and instrument — that is wrong,
because a difference of properties (<s>dharma</s>) is accepted, [while] the entity (<s>vastu</s>) is held to be non-different. // Pramāṇav_2.318 //
In this way, every establishment of action and causal factor
operates through superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) upon an entity that is undivided, even when [parts] are held to be distinct. // Pramāṇav_2.319 //
The awareness of the meaning of the object (<s>kārtha-saṃvid</s>) — which is this very apprehension of each particular —

children.text: tadarthavedanaṃ kena tādrū pyād vyabhicāri tat // Pramāṇav_2.320 //
children.translated_text: that knowledge of the object — by what [means] does it deviate from [its own] conformity [with the object]? // Pramāṇav_2.320 //
Now, where is that experience (<s>anubhava</s>) of it? This very [question] is being examined.

children.text: sarūpayanti tat kena sthūlābhāsaṃ ca te 'ṇavaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.321 //
children.translated_text: By what do those atoms make it conform? And [how do] those [atoms produce] the appearance of a gross [object]? // Pramāṇav_2.321 //
Therefore, the bearing of the form of the object is not [sufficient] for it; even when it exists, it is deviant (<s>vyabhicāriṇī</s>),
and it is incapable of establishing the nature of the awareness of that [object]. // Pramāṇav_2.322 //
If conformity with that and arising from that are the defining marks of what is cognized (<s>saṃvedya</s>),

children.text: saṃvedya syāt samānārtha vijñānaṃ samanantaram // Pramāṇav_2.323 //
children.translated_text: then the immediately succeeding cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) having the same object would also be what is cognized. // Pramāṇav_2.323 //

children.text: idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vedam iti yatrāvasāyadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This was seen, this was heard, this was known' — where there is a cognition of ascertainment (<s>avasāyadhī</s>),
that itself is not the experience of it; [rather,] the proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) is what is being examined. // Pramāṇav_2.324 //
By the one for whom the seeing of the seen and seeing [is established] — that is regarded as his perception;
relying upon the connection of those two, this is the ascertainment of the seer (<s>draṣṭṛ</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.325 //

children.text: ātmā sa tasyānubhavaḥ s ca nānyasya kasyacit /
children.translated_text: That [cognition] is the self (<s>ātman</s>) of that [seer]; that is his experience; and that belongs to no other whatsoever.
The fact of being apprehended by direct perception — that too is its identity [with the seer]. // Pramāṇav_2.326 //
There is no other [cognition] to be experienced by that; therefore there is no other experience of it.

children.text: tasyāpi tulyacodyatvāt svayaṃ saiva prakāśate // Pramāṇav_2.327 //
children.translated_text: Since the same objection would apply to that [further cognition] as well, it itself illuminates itself (<s>svayaṃ prakāśate</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.327 //
That nature of it, having the form of blue and so forth, is also the experience (<s>anubhava</s>) of it;
though known through the experience of blue and the like, it is also the experience of its own nature (<s>svarūpa</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.328 //
Being manifest, through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) [with its own nature], it illuminates its own nature;
just as light (<s>prakāśa</s>) is accepted [to be self-illuminating], so too cognition (<s>dhī</s>) is self-aware (<s>ātmavedinī</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.329 //
And when this [cognition's] object of knowledge is something external, the [roles of] known and knower are difficult to establish;
just as by those who are deluded, [cognition] is perceived as having the form of known and knower [while actually] devoid of [real] known and knower. // Pramāṇav_2.330 //
The error of the forms of apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) and apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) having distinct characteristics —
this determination is constructed [through error], like the differentiation of cognitions of [illusory] hair and the like. // Pramāṇav_2.331 //
When that is so, the characteristics of apprehended and apprehender are not to be challenged;
since there is no other awareness [apart from self-awareness], self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvit</s>) is accepted as the result (<s>phala</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.332 //

children.text: yadi bahyo 'nubhūyeta ko doṣo naiva kaścana /
children.translated_text: If an external [object] were experienced, what would be the fault? None whatsoever.

children.text: idameva kimuktaṃ syāt sa bāhyo 'rtho 'nubhūyate // Pramāṇav_2.333 //
children.translated_text: Would this alone have been said — that the external object is experienced? // Pramāṇav_2.333 //
If cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) bears its form, then it exists as qualified by [that] form;
whether that [form] is from something external or otherwise — this deserves examination. // Pramāṇav_2.334 //
Because of the non-apprehension of [an object] free from the condition of being seen, and because of apprehension only when that [condition obtains],

children.text: darśanaṃ nīlanirbhāsaṃ nārtho bāhyo 'sti kevalam // Pramāṇav_2.335 //
children.translated_text: the seeing that appears as blue [is all there is] — there is simply no external object. // Pramāṇav_2.335 //
For some [beings], something internal awakens from a latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>);

children.text: tato dhiyāṃ viniyamo na bāhyārthavyapekṣayā // Pramāṇav_2.336 //
children.translated_text: therefore the regulation of cognitions is not dependent on an external object. // Pramāṇav_2.336 //
Therefore, there exists a single [cognition] of dual form (<s>dvirūpa</s>) — that which is experienced in this way
and is also remembered — the awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) of both forms of this [cognition] is the result (<s>phala</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.337 //
When the other [i.e., external object] is accepted as one whose existence is produced by that [cognition], whether desired or undesired,
[it serves as] the cause of a representation (<s>vijñapti</s>), and the experience of that [representation] as well is the object. // Pramāṇav_2.338 //
When cognition has an object, and the object is established in the cognition-aspect,

children.text: tadā ya ātmānubhavaḥ sa evārthaviniścayaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.339 //
children.translated_text: then that which is the self-experience (<s>ātmānubhava</s>) — that itself is the ascertainment of the object. // Pramāṇav_2.339 //
Whether the desired form is [its] own nature or is experienced otherwise,

children.text: iṣṭo 'niṣṭo 'pi vā tena bhavatyarthaḥ praveditaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.340 //
children.translated_text: whether desired or undesired — through that, the object becomes known (<s>pravedita</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.340 //
Even when an external object exists, it is ascertained only as it is experienced,
in its own nature — not through the fault of it having multiple natures. // Pramāṇav_2.341 //

children.text: yadi bāhyaṃ na vidyeta ksya saṃvedanaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the external does not exist, of what would there be awareness?

children.text: yadyagatyā svarūpasya bāhyasyaiva na kiṃ matam // Pramāṇav_2.342 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] unavoidably of its own nature — then why is it not accepted as [awareness] of the external itself? // Pramāṇav_2.342 //
Even if [external objects] are accepted, with [their] difference, there would be no experience of the two [simultaneously];

children.text: adṛṣṭāvaraṇāt syāt cenna nāmārthāvaśo gatiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.343 //
children.translated_text: if [one says] it would be so because of an unseen obstruction (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) — no, for there is no cognition dependent merely on name and object. // Pramāṇav_2.343 //
That which shows a thing of manifold nature as though of a single nature —

children.text: tadadṛṣṭaṃ kathaṃ nāma bhavedarthasya darśakam // Pramāṇav_2.344 //
children.translated_text: how can that, which has not seen [the real nature], be a revealer of the object? // Pramāṇav_2.344 //
If conceptual constructions (<s>kalpanā</s>) that manifest as desired or undesired are not sense-cognition,
[still] the connection of minds with what is undesired is seen even in that [sense-cognition]. // Pramāṇav_2.345 //

children.text: tasmāt prameye bāhye 'pi yuktaṃ svānubhavaḥ phalam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even when the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is external, self-experience (<s>svānubhava</s>) as the result is proper,
because whatever is the nature of this [cognition] — just so is the ascertainment of the object. // Pramāṇav_2.346 //
