The manifestation as having the form of the object (<s>tadarthābhāsatā</s>) — that is its <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition); but even though [the object] exists,
the apprehender-nature (<s>grāhakātman</s>), being for its own purpose, does not depend on external objects. // Pramāṇav_2.347 //
Since however this [cognition] is established in the perception as having the nature of the object,
it is ascertained as 'this is so established' — through self-awareness (<s>ātmasaṃvid</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.348 //
Thus, the awareness of the object (<s>arthasaṃvit</s>) is accepted as just that [self-awareness], because the object-nature is not seen [independently];

children.text: tasmād buddhiniveśyārthaḥ sādhanaṃ tasya sā kriyā // Pramāṇav_2.349 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the object established in cognition is the instrument (<s>sādhana</s>), and that [self-awareness] is the action (<s>kriyā</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.349 //

children.text: yathā niviśate so 'rtho yataḥ sā prathate tathā /
children.translated_text: In whatever way the object is established, from that, it [cognition] manifests accordingly;
because of its identity with the state of the object (<s>arthasthiti</s>), self-awareness is also regarded as awareness of the object. // Pramāṇav_2.350 //
Therefore, even the difference of object-domain is not [a reason why] self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>) [cannot be] the result;
it has been stated in the investigation of [its] own nature that [self-awareness] is identical with the awareness of the object, due to identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.351 //
Of cognition that appears in a certain way — whether the object is of that same kind or of a different kind —
the object is also the cause of the cognition; thus the status of the object as the knowable (<s>prameya</s>) is established. // Pramāṇav_2.352 //
How can there be apprehension of the object for one that appears in whatever manner, apart from bearing the form of the object?

children.text: arthagrahaḥ katham satyaṃ na jāne 'hamapīdṛśam // Pramāṇav_2.353 //
children.translated_text: Truly, I too do not know such a [possibility]. // Pramāṇav_2.353 //
Though undivided (<s>avibhāga</s>), by those whose vision is distorted — having the nature of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) —
it is perceived as though having the divisions of apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>), apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>), and self-awareness (<s>saṃvitti</s>). // Pramāṇav_2.354 //
Just as for those whose eyes are afflicted by mantras and the like, clods of earth and potsherds and so forth
appear as something entirely different, even though devoid of that [apparent] form. // Pramāṇav_2.355 //
Similarly, from seeing them with unafflicted vision, [the truth becomes clear];

children.text: dūre yathā vā maruṣu mahānalpo 'pi dṛśyate // Pramāṇav_2.356 //
children.translated_text: just as in a desert, even a small [thing] is seen as large from a distance. // Pramāṇav_2.356 //
And this establishment of knowable (<s>meya</s>), means of knowing (<s>māna</s>), and result (<s>phala</s>), as it has been demonstrated,
is constructed even though non-existent [in reality], among the apprehended, apprehender, and awareness. // Pramāṇav_2.357 //
Otherwise, for a single entity that appears in multiple forms,
how could the forms be real? — since the unity of that would be destroyed. // Pramāṇav_2.358 //
And from the loss of otherness of something other, there is no non-difference [either], from the perception of form;

children.text: rūpābhedaṃ ca paśyanto dhīrabhedaṃ vyavasyati // Pramāṇav_2.359 //
children.translated_text: and those who see non-difference of form determine a non-difference of cognition. // Pramāṇav_2.359 //

children.text: bhāvā yena nirūpyante tadrūpaṃ nāsti tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The form by which entities are determined does not exist in reality,

children.text: yasmādekamanekaṃ ca rūpaṃ teṣāṃ na vidyate // Pramāṇav_2.360 //
children.translated_text: because neither a single nor a manifold form is found in them. // Pramāṇav_2.360 //
From the perception of similarity in the world, error (<s>bhrānti</s>) arises,
through the determination of identity in what is not [actually] identical — that does not apply here. // Pramāṇav_2.361 //
Because in this world, not even a single entity is seen as having that [identical] nature;
however, this [error] which arises from internal disturbance (<s>upaplava</s>) also exists — // Pramāṇav_2.362 //
born from defect (<s>doṣa</s>), by its very nature it produces false appearances (<s>vitathapratibhāsinī</s>),
like the vision of those with <s>timira</s> (visual defect) and the like, not depending on [external] similarity. // Pramāṇav_2.363 //
In that case, the delimitation of cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) is accepted as the apprehender-form (<s>grāhakākāra</s>);

children.text: tādātmyādātmavit tasya sa tasya sādhanaṃ tataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.364 //
children.translated_text: through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>), [cognition] is self-aware — that is the instrument (<s>sādhana</s>) of that [apprehension]. // Pramāṇav_2.364 //
Therein, when the means of knowing bears self-awareness as its domain — just as the feeling (<s>vedana</s>) of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like —
Therein too, because they are of the nature of experience, they are capable of self-awareness (<s>svātmasaṃvid</s>);

children.text: iti sā yogyatā mānamātmā meyaḥ phalaṃ svavit // Pramāṇav_2.366 //
children.translated_text: thus that capability is the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), the self is the object of cognition (<s>meya</s>), and the result (<s>phala</s>) is self-knowledge. // Pramāṇav 2.366 //
The delimitation (<s>pariccheda</s>) counted as the apprehender-aspect (<s>grāhakākāra</s>) in the self —

children.text: sā yogyateti ca proktaṃ pramāṇaṃ svātmavedanam // Pramāṇav_2.367 //
children.translated_text: that capability, it is said, is the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), and self-awareness is [its result]. // Pramāṇav 2.367 //
For every cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), arising from objects,
even when something else is also a cause, has in some way the form of the object (<s>viṣayākṛti</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.368 //
Just as, even when food, time, and the like are causes in the production of offspring,
[the offspring] bears the form of the parents alone, not of anything else. // Pramāṇav 2.369 //
Even though other [factors] are equally causes of that, objecthood (<s>viṣayatva</s>) is regarded as belonging to the object

children.text: viṣayatvaṃ tadaṃśena tadabhāve na tad bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.370 //
children.translated_text: by virtue of its specific aspect; in the absence of that, that [objecthood] would not obtain. // Pramāṇav 2.370 //
The suspicion that [cognition] lacks the form of an object might arise even in a cognition that has an object,
when the apprehension of a past object is established, and self-awareness has a twofold nature (<s>dvirūpatva</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.371 //
Because of differentiation through appearances such as blue and the like, the object is not a <s>jāti</s> (universal) possessing [those qualities];

children.text: sā cānityā na jātiḥ syānnityā cā janikā katham // Pramāṇav_2.372 //
children.translated_text: and that [appearance] is impermanent — it cannot be a <s>jāti</s>; and if eternal, how could it be produced? // Pramāṇav 2.372 //
Name and the like were previously refuted; this is not the procedure for things having meaning.
Because it merely follows [one's] wish, the power of the object is not established. // Pramāṇav 2.373 //
If memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is this kind of cognition, and its arising is from experience (<s>anubhava</s>),

children.text: sa cārthākārarahitaḥ sedānīṃ tadvatī katham // Pramāṇav_2.374 //
children.translated_text: and that [experience] is devoid of the form of an object — then how would [memory] now possess that [form]? // Pramāṇav 2.374 //
The arising is not from the object, since it is absent [at the time of memory]; even in the [original] experience it would be the same [problem].

children.text: ākāraḥ sa ca nārthasya spaṣṭakāravivekataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.375 //
children.translated_text: And that form is not of the object, because of the discrimination of the clearly appearing form. // Pramāṇav 2.375 //
Another [person] would then cognize that form as distinct [from the cognition];

children.text: nityamātmani sambandhe pratīyāt kathitaṃ ca na // Pramāṇav_2.376 //
children.translated_text: if there is an eternal connection to the self, it should be [always] cognized — but it has been stated [that it is] not. // Pramāṇav 2.376 //
When each [cognition] is connected to only one [object], the connection (<s>pratisandhi</s>) is not appropriate,
since the engagement with a single object is [only] in the minds of the speaker and listener. // Pramāṇav 2.377 //
If the single designation [is due to] similarity — then for things not identical to each other,
how would an object of different nature be grasped? Then the cognition would be objectless. // Pramāṇav 2.378 //
But that [connection] is bound through the experiential cognition (<s>anubhavavijñāna</s>) that encompasses both aspects,
by the subsequent cognition having a single form-particular. // Pramāṇav 2.379 //
For otherwise, how would what does not have that form ascend into cognition?

children.text: ekākārottaraṃ jñānaṃ tathā h yuktaramuktaram // Pramāṇav_2.380 //
children.translated_text: The subsequent cognition having a single form — thus the subsequent is indeed appropriate. // Pramāṇav 2.380 //
Of that [cognition], the aspects are: the form of the object (<s>arthākāra</s>) and a certain self-aspect (<s>ātmākāra</s>);

children.text: dvitīyasya tṛtīyena jñānena hi vivicyate // Pramāṇav_2.381 //
children.translated_text: the second [aspect] is distinguished by a third cognition. // Pramāṇav 2.381 //
If, in the memory of the cognition as an effect of the object, there is a conflation with the memory of the object

children.text: bhrāntyā saṅkalanaṃ jyotirmanaskāre ca sā bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.382 //
children.translated_text: due to error — that [error] would [also] arise in the mental attention toward light. // Pramāṇav 2.382 //

children.text: sarveṣāmapi kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇaiḥ syāt tathā grahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the apprehension of all effects through their causes would be the same;
and from that, a pot would not be remembered [distinctly] from [its cause, such as] the potter. // Pramāṇav 2.383 //
Since cognition, by virtue of a special quality, partakes of contact with the object,

children.text: sārūpyāttat kimanyat syād dṛṣṭeśca yamalādiṣu // Pramāṇav_2.384 //
children.translated_text: what else could that be due to besides resemblance (<s>sārūpya</s>)? And [this is] also [seen] in the case of twins and the like. // Pramāṇav 2.384 //
For if the initial [cognition] has a twofold nature, and the second is established in a single form,
the second would not be distinguished by the reflective cognition (<s>parāmarśacetas</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.385 //
The cognition that conflates the object grasps the second [aspect],
namely the cognition appearing in the form of blue and the like, which manifests before [the mind]. // Pramāṇav 2.386 //
Otherwise, if only the initial [cognition] were to be conjoined [with the object] because of the object's existence,
successive cognitions would have no observed connection with the prior object. // Pramāṇav 2.387 //
For an object that is cognized only once in necessary connection with a cognition,
by what aspect would its otherness from [the cognition] be established? // Pramāṇav 2.388 //
And difference would be seen through erroneous cognitions, as in the case of the [double] moon and the like;
there is no fixed rule of awareness for blue and yellow, which are distinct. // Pramāṇav 2.389 //
No one who does not cognize the object cognizes what is not an object;

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ saṃvedyamānaṃ tat tayornāsti vivekitā // Pramāṇav_2.390 //
children.translated_text: what is seen is what is being cognized — there is no discrimination between those two. // Pramāṇav 2.390 //
Therefore, the non-difference of the object that appears at the time of cognition from the cognition
is irresistible; there would be an inference from the difference of causes. // Pramāṇav 2.391 //
If, from the absence of momentary cognitions even when other causes are present,

children.text: niyamaṃ yadi na bru yāt pratyayāt samanantarāt // Pramāṇav_2.392 //
children.translated_text: one would not state the fixed rule [that the object is the cause], then [it would be] from the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.392 //
The [inference that] 'a sprout arises from a seed, smoke [proves] fire' — such
states of affairs involving agents and indicators rely on external objects; // Pramāṇav 2.393 //
but even those could be constructed by relying on cognitions that have the appearance of those forms

children.text: buddhīrāśritya kalpyeta yadi kiṃ vā virudhyate // Pramāṇav_2.394 //
children.translated_text: and are in fixed connection [with them] — if so, what would be contradicted? // Pramāṇav 2.394 //

children.text: anagnijanyo dhūmaḥ syāt tatkāryāt kāraṇe gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Smoke would arise without fire; the inference from the effect to the cause

children.text: na syāt kāraṇatāyāṃ vā kuta ekāntato gatiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.395 //
children.translated_text: would not hold; or regarding the state of being a cause, from where would there be certainty? // Pramāṇav 2.395 //
Even there, a cognition appearing as smoke would lead to a cognition appearing as fire
through an imprint (<s>vāsanā</s>) ready for awakening — not to fire [itself]. // Pramāṇav 2.396 //
Only a mental continuum (<s>cittasantāna</s>) pregnant with an imprint capable of that [fire-appearance]
manifests the cognition appearing as smoke — smoke is therefore not introduced from elsewhere. // Pramāṇav 2.397 //

children.text: astyeṣa viduṣāṃ vādo bāhyāṃ tvāśritya varṇyate /
children.translated_text: This is the position of the learned; but [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] explains it by relying on the external [object].
The twofold nature (<s>dvairūpya</s>) is established from the fixed rule of self-awareness — and that [too] is established. // Pramāṇav 2.398 //
Cognition, through the difference of the sense faculties (<s>indriya</s>), bearing differentiation in its appearances with respect to the object —
sharp, dull, unclear, and so forth — is seen in one and the same [object]. // Pramāṇav 2.399 //
If the object has an undifferentiated form, the mind should be of one form;

children.text: sarvai tadarthamarthāccet tasya nāsti tadābhatā // Pramāṇav_2.400 //
children.translated_text: if all [cognitions] are for that object, and [the variety comes] from the object — then that [uniformity] would not belong to it. // Pramāṇav 2.400 //
For [cognition], which arises relying on the object and imitates its form,

children.text: tasya kenacidaṃśena parato 'pi bhidā bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.401 //
children.translated_text: there could be difference from something else by some aspect. // Pramāṇav 2.401 //

children.text: tathā hyāśritya pitaraṃ tadrūpo 'pi sutaḥ pituḥ /
children.translated_text: For just as a son, relying on the father and having the father's form,
[yet] in some aspect derives difference from somewhere [else]. // Pramāṇav 2.402 //
Those with weak vision see the disc of a lamp and the like
in the form of a peacock-tail, shining with blue and red. // Pramāṇav 2.403 //
If that [appearance] is the form of the external [object], what incapacity [would there be] for one with clear vision?

children.text: bhūtaṃ paśyaṃśca taddarśī kathaṃ copahatendriyaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.404 //
children.translated_text: And one who sees the reality is a perceiver of that — how could one with impaired faculties [see the same]? // Pramāṇav 2.404 //
When one whose eye has been cleansed of cataract (<s>timira</s>) clearly sees a supersensory object,
how would that [same object] be unclear for one seeing it with another faculty? // Pramāṇav 2.405 //
The capacity of a single [object] is understood from light, the eye, and mental attention —
from something other than these [three], it is not a cause; and how then is the object [a cause]? // Pramāṇav 2.406 //

children.text: sa eva yadi dhīhetuḥ ki pradīpamapekṣate /
children.translated_text: If that very [object] is the cause of cognition, why does it require a lamp?
Since cognition arises from the lamp alone, neither [object nor both] is a cause. // Pramāṇav 2.407 //
Due to differences of distance, proximity, and so forth, being manifest and unmanifest is not appropriate [for the external object];
if it would be so due to differences in illumination — then [the same problem applies] for heating and covering. // Pramāṇav 2.408 //
For something subtle, either there is equal vision and non-vision, or some [partial vision];

children.text: ālokana na mandena dṛśyate 'to bhidā yadi // Pramāṇav_2.409 //
children.translated_text: if it is not seen by dim illumination, then, if there is difference [in illumination], [it should be seen]. // Pramāṇav 2.409 //
If the external object is one, whence the difference of being seen and not-seen?
If it is many, being divided atom by atom, whence the non-difference of being seen and not-seen? // Pramāṇav 2.410 //
If the differentiation in appearance is due to differences in dullness and sharpness of cognition,
how would the undifferentiated appear with differentiation when something else is differentiated? // Pramāṇav 2.411 //

children.text: mandaṃ tadapi tejaḥ kimāvṛteriha sā na kim /
children.translated_text: Is that [dim] light also dim? Or is there not also obstruction here?
This thinness of light also exists elsewhere where there is no thinness. // Pramāṇav 2.412 //
And when very close, the light being well-manifest would be very clear;
if even there, relying on the unseen, another form would arise — // Pramāṇav 2.413 //
from their mutual obstruction there would be impairment of light; therefore
only one would be seen there; and when unobstructed, one would at once // Pramāṇav 2.414 //
see a clear and unclear form — one [sees] through obstruction by the unseen;

children.text: arthānarthau na yena stastadadṛṣṭaṃ karoti kim // Pramāṇav_2.415 //
children.translated_text: that which cannot [produce] either an object or a non-object — what does that unseen [factor] do? // Pramāṇav 2.415 //
Therefore, awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), arising in dependence on its causes from the object,
bears differentiation in its appearances; the rest are the false theories of those of poor understanding. // Pramāṇav 2.416 //
Of cognition, words, and lamps — whether [they are causes] of perception or of something else —
since the prior [causes] are momentary and perish, // Pramāṇav 2.417 //
whence is manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) from what is non-existent? For [the object,] being other than cognition, does not assist [it].
If manifestation is [accepted], every object would be manifested — if there is a fixed rule regarding its cause. // Pramāṇav 2.418 //
Nor is this conceptualization in cognition; but cognition, because of the appearance of the object,

children.text: taṃ vyanaktīti kathyeta tadabhāve 'pi tatkṛtam // Pramāṇav_2.419 //
children.translated_text: is said to 'manifest' it — even in its absence, that [manifestation] would be effected [by cognition]. // Pramāṇav 2.419 //
And another object, arising simultaneously, does not shape [cognition], since it does not assist.

children.text: vyakto 'nākārayan jñānaṃ svākāreṇa kathaṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.420 //
children.translated_text: If manifested yet not shaping the cognition — how would [the cognition] have its own form? // Pramāṇav 2.420 //
Even an object like a diamond or stone, being stable, because it does not depend on others,

children.text: sakṛt sarvasya janayejjñānāni jagataḥ samam // Pramāṇav_2.421 //
children.translated_text: would produce cognitions of everything in the world simultaneously and at once. // Pramāṇav 2.421 //
They [cognitions] arise sequentially because of the assistance of cooperating conditions [of that object].

children.text: āhuḥ pratikṣaṇaṃ bhedaṃ sa doṣo 'trāpi pūrvavat // Pramāṇav_2.422 //
children.translated_text: They say [the object] differs at each moment — [but] the same fault [applies] here too, as before. // Pramāṇav 2.422 //
Regarding the identity of cognition with awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>), there is no dispute with anyone;
and its having the form of the object is established — and that too is established from memory (<s>saṃsmṛti</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.423 //
When this [cognition] has not been experienced as different, [and is] not distinguished by its own objects,

children.text: evametanna khalvevamiti sā syānna bhedinī // Pramāṇav_2.424 //
children.translated_text: [one might think] 'it is thus' or 'it is not thus' — but that [doubt] would not be discriminative. // Pramāṇav 2.424 //
And no difference whatsoever is a discriminator by mere experience;
nor is cognition discriminative when the difference is indistinct, as in the case of twins and the like. // Pramāṇav 2.425 //
Even through the proof of the twofold nature (<s>dvairūpya</s>), self-awareness (<s>svavedana</s>) is mostly established,
since at the time of awareness, the appearance that is the self-nature [of cognition] is observed. // Pramāṇav 2.426 //
When cognition is blocked by a cognition not having that form, how would there be experience?

children.text: svaṃ ca rūpaṃ na sā vettītyutsanno 'nubhavo 'khilaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.427 //
children.translated_text: And that [cognition] does not know its own form — [thus] all experience would be destroyed. // Pramāṇav 2.427 //
That cognition appears as if outward-directed, like the appearance of an object;
but the apprehending awareness (<s>vitti</s>) of the intellect is always inward-directed in the self. // Pramāṇav 2.428 //

children.text: yo yasya viṣayābhāsastaṃ vetti na tadipyapi /
children.translated_text: Whatever has the appearance of an object of another — that [other] knows it, but not vice versa.
Mutual awareness of all similar [cognitions] would follow;

children.text: buddhiḥ sarūpā tadviccet nedānīṃ vit sarūpikā // Pramāṇav_2.430 //
children.translated_text: if a cognition of similar form were to know that — then even now, the awareness would be of similar form. // Pramāṇav 2.430 //
That experience is itself its own [self-awareness]; it is not the cause of similarity.
It would be the basis for the conventional distinction of action and object. // Pramāṇav 2.431 //
Because of the collapse of superimposing awareness of [external] form onto what is intrinsically of that nature,
the designation 'experienced' belongs to blue and the like — not [through] experience from another self. // Pramāṇav 2.432 //
If cognition has the form of blue and the like, the [external] object is sublated — by what means of valid cognition [is it established]?
If cognition does not have the form of blue and the like, how is that its experience? // Pramāṇav 2.433 //
Since the nature of being awareness (<s>saṃvedanātmatva</s>) is not grounded in resemblance,

children.text: siddhaṃ tat svat evāsya kimarthenopanīyate // Pramāṇav_2.434 //
children.translated_text: that [self-awareness] is established from itself alone — why is the object brought in? // Pramāṇav 2.434 //
And there is not complete identity, because of the absurd consequence of non-cognition;

children.text: na ca kenacidaṃśena sarva sarvasya vedanam // Pramāṇav_2.435 //
children.translated_text: nor is there partial [identity], for [then] everything would be the cognition of everything. // Pramāṇav 2.435 //
Just as the experience of blue and the like is accepted because of having the form of blue and the like,
so too there would be experience of that [experience itself], because of having the form of experience. // Pramāṇav 2.436 //
'Experience is not experienced' — this is indeed a definitive determination having meaning.

children.text: tasmādadoṣa iti cet nārthe 'pyastyeṣa sarvadā // Pramāṇav_2.437 //
children.translated_text: Therefore [there is] no fault — if you say so, [then] that [problem] always exists even regarding the object. // Pramāṇav 2.437 //
Why would experience not exist when being (<s>sattā</s>) is the ground of being?

children.text: api cedaṃ yadābhāti dṛśyamāne sitādike // Pramāṇav_2.438 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, this which appears when white and the like are being seen — // Pramāṇav 2.438 //
A person's cognition of the form manifested by white and so forth is clear.
Is that [cognition] of the form of the other, namely the manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) of white and so forth, or of its own nature? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.439]
If the manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) is of the form of the other and is itself non-luminous, how is white manifested?

children.text: jñānaṃ vyaktirna sā vyaktetyavyaktamakhilaṃ jagat // Pramāṇav_2.440 //
children.translated_text: If cognition is the manifestation, and that [manifestation] is not [itself] manifest, then the entire world would be unmanifest. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.440]
Because the same fault would follow even if manifestation were manifested by another manifestation,

children.text: dṛṣṭyā vājñātasambandhaṃ viśinaṣṭi tayā katham // Pramāṇav_2.441 //
children.translated_text: how does sight, whose connection [with the object] is unknown, distinguish by means of that [manifestation]? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.441]
Since when both [cognition and object] share a single locus, the second is not seen,

children.text: dvayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭayordṛṣṭau syād dṛṣṭamiti niścayaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.442 //
children.translated_text: when both are seen in conjunction, there would be the determination 'it has been seen.' [Pramāṇavārttika 2.442]
That whose cognition, having the same form [as the object], is seen by another mind —

children.text: dṛṣṭākhyā tatra cet siddhaṃ sārūpyesya svavedanam // Pramāṇav_2.443 //
children.translated_text: if it is called 'seen' on that account, then <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) is established through that very similarity of form. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.443]

children.text: athātmarūpaṃ no vetti pararūpasya vit katham /
children.translated_text: But if it does not know its own form, how can it know the form of another?

children.text: sārūpyād vedanākhyā ca prāgeva prativarṇitā // Pramāṇav_2.444 //
children.translated_text: And the designation 'cognition' based on similarity of form has already been refuted earlier. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.444]
The apprehension of similarity of form occurs only between two things that are [both] seen, and the object has not been seen [independently].

children.text: prāk kathaṃ darśanenāsya sārūpyaṃ so 'dhyavasyati // Pramāṇav_2.445 //
children.translated_text: How then could one ascertain its similarity of form with the cognition prior [to seeing it]? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.445]
One who does not even desire similarity — for that person there is no seeing of both.

children.text: tadārtho jñānamiti ca jñāte ceti gatā kathā // Pramāṇav_2.446 //
children.translated_text: And when it is known that 'the object is cognition,' the discussion is concluded. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.446]

children.text: atha svarūpam sā tarhi svayameva prakāśate /
children.translated_text: If [you say manifestation] is of its own form, then it is self-luminous.
Because if it were non-luminous, the object would remain unilluminated. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.447]
By this, those who, on the view that [cognition] does not know itself, declare cognition to be non-perceptual because all objects would be unseen —
they too have been answered. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.448]
Differing in their operations due to differences in basis (<s>āśraya</s>), object-support (<s>ālambana</s>), and habituation (<s>abhyāsa</s>),
those are indeed cognitions differentiated as pleasure, pain, desire, and so forth. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.449]
They are perceptual, and nothing else distinct from them is discerned.

children.text: yattajjñānaṃ paro 'pyetān bhuñjītānyena vid yadi // Pramāṇav_2.450 //
children.translated_text: That cognition — even another could experience these [pleasure, etc.] if it knew them by another [cognition]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.450]

children.text: tajjā tatpratibhāsā va yadi dhīrvetti nāparā /
children.translated_text: If a cognition that is born from that or that has that as its appearance knows [it], no other [cognition is needed].
Even for another that apprehends [it], this pair [of conditions] necessarily obtains. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.451]
But if [the cognition] does not arise from that [object] and does not have that as its appearance,

children.text: sā dhīrnirviṣayā prāptā sāmānyaṃ ca tadagrahe // Pramāṇav_2.452 //
children.translated_text: that cognition would be without an object, and a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) would [result] if it fails to apprehend that [particular]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.452]

children.text: na gṛhyat iti proktam na ca tadvastu kiñcana /
children.translated_text: It has been stated that [the universal] is not apprehended, and there is no such real entity.
Therefore, that appearance of the object is not other than that cognition. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.453]
If [someone says]: 'When the perceptual nature of cognition is established as self-aware, it apprehends those [objects] again,

children.text: nādhyakṣamiti cedeṣa kuto bhedaḥ samārthayoḥ // Pramāṇav_2.454 //
children.translated_text: but not perceptually' — then whence comes this distinction between two things of equal capacity? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.454]
If the restriction of awareness is due to an unseen connection with a single object and so forth,
then another could never apprehend [it] at all, and the difference of awareness is also refuted. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.455]
And for those who hold that <s>yogins</s> (contemplatives) perceive the pleasure and so forth of others directly —
having equal experience, they too would become afflicted [by others' suffering]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.456]
If [you say] their suffering born from that does not arise due to the absence of contact between object and sense faculty —

children.text: nodeti duḥkhamiti cet na vai duḥkhasamudbhavaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.457 //
children.translated_text: well, it is not the arising of suffering [that is at issue]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.457]
Rather, the awareness of suffering — the arising of the cognition of suffering [is the issue].
For indeed, suffering and the like, when not experienced, are not the cause of affliction or benefit. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.458]

children.text: bhāsamānaṃ svarūpeṇa pīḍā duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ yadā /
children.translated_text: When suffering itself is the affliction appearing in its own form,

children.text: na tadālambanaṃ jñānaṃ na tadaivaṃ prayujyate // Pramāṇav_2.459 //
children.translated_text: a cognition that has that as its object is not applied in that way [i.e., does not produce affliction in another]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.459]
Since all cognition is distinct from that [object], in the awareness that has that as its object-support,

children.text: arthasārūpyamālamba ātmā vittiḥ svayaṃ sfuṭā // Pramāṇav_2.460 //
children.translated_text: similarity to the object is the object-support; the self is awareness (<s>vitti</s>), self-luminous. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.460]
Moreover, in the absence of direct perceptibility of cognition, there would be [only] inferential knowledge of the mind.

children.text: taccākṣamartho dhīḥ pūrvo manaskāro 'pi vā bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.461 //
children.translated_text: And the inferential sign (<s>liṅga</s>) would be the sense-object, or the cognition, or the previous mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>). [Pramāṇavārttika 2.461]
In this causal complex, nothing else is related [to cognition],
because no capacity [of the sense faculty] is observed there, due to deviation. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.462]

children.text: tathārtho dhīmanaskārau jñānaṃ tau ca na sidhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the object, cognition, and mental attention — [as signs for] cognition — these two are not established.
What is not established cannot serve as an inferential sign. The manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) of the object would be its cognition-nature. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.463]

children.text: liṅgaṃ saiva nanu jñānaṃ vyakto 'rtho 'nena varṇitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Surely that very manifestation is the inferential sign for cognition — [but] the object is described as manifested by this [cognition].
Since when manifestation is not experienced, there is no certainty of its being manifested by that. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.464]
If some particular quality of the object itself is accepted as manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>),
[we say:] there is no particular quality of an object that does not undergo production and decay. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.465]
Or if that [production and decay] is accepted, momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) follows from each successive cognition.

children.text: sa ca jñāto 'tha vājñāto bhavejjñātasya liṅgatā // Pramāṇav_2.466 //
children.translated_text: And is that [momentary particular] known or unknown? If known, it has the status of an inferential sign. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.466]
If cognition is not ascertained, then whence [the determination] 'this is known'?
And how can that which is not ascertained as known serve as an indicator? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.467]

children.text: adṛṣṭadṛṣṭayo 'nyena draṣṭrā dṛṣṭā na hi kvacit /
children.translated_text: Those whose vision is unseen are never seen by another perceiver.
If [you say] the distinction 'it exists even when seen by another' — that would [require] knowledge of one's own cognition. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.468]
Therefore, inference of cognition, independent of cognition's own properties,
from the properties of the object alone — what other own-property of one's own cognition [could serve]? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.469]
The inferential sign apprehended by perception — for [cognitions] born from the same causal basis,

children.text: tasya bhedaḥ kuto buddhe rvyabhicāryanyajaśca saḥ // Pramāṇav_2.470 //
children.translated_text: whence is there a difference of that [sign] from cognition? And that [sign] is deviant and produced by another. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.470]
Apart from the five objects — form and so forth — the sense faculties, and apprehension,

children.text: muktvā na kāryamaparaṃ tasyāḥ samupalabhyate // Pramāṇav_2.471 //
children.translated_text: no other effect of that [cognition] is observed. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.471]
Of these, the pair [sense faculties and apprehension] is beyond direct perception; even a single one among the five sense-objects is not observed
that, having arisen from the seeing of form, could exist separately in another way. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.472]
That which is thus not cognized — to call it an inferential sign is extraordinary.

children.text: vidyamāne 'pi liṅge tāṃ tena sārdhamapaśyataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.473 //
children.translated_text: Even when an inferential sign is present, for one who does not see it together with that [cognition], [Pramāṇavārttika 2.473]
how can there be ascertainment? For an inferential sign does not illuminate what has not been seen.

children.text: tata evāsya liṅgāt prāk prasiddherupavarṇane // Pramāṇav_2.474 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, regarding the establishment [of cognition] from that inferential sign prior to [direct] apprehension, [Pramāṇavārttika 2.474]
it would require proof by another example, and that too [leads to] infinite regress.

children.text: ityarthasya dhiyaḥ siddhiḥ nārthāt tasyāḥ kathañcana // Pramāṇav_2.475 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the establishment of cognition from the object is not possible in any way [through inference]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.475]
When that [cognition] is not established, the object itself is not established,

children.text: pratyakṣāṃ ca dhiyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyāśceṣṭābhidhādikam // Pramāṇav_2.476 //
children.translated_text: and having seen cognition as perceptual, [one observes] its behavior, speech, and so forth. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.476]
The inference of others' minds too would be impossible, since [cognition] is not seen in oneself [on your view],
and due to the non-establishment of the connection between mind, cognition, object, and inferential sign. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.477]

children.text: prakāśitā kathaṃ vā syāt buddhirbuddh yantareṇa vaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or how could cognition be illuminated by another cognition, according to you?
Since both are equally non-luminous in nature, whence the relation of manifested and manifestor? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.478]
How is there manifestation of the object in a light through the transfer of form?

children.text: sa ca prakāśastadrūpaḥ svayameva prakāśate // Pramāṇav_2.479 //
children.translated_text: And that light, having the form of that [object], is itself self-luminous. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.479]
If that is accepted, then cognition in cognition is self-aware (<s>svavedikā</s>),

children.text: siddhānyathā tulyadharmā viṣayo 'pi dhiyā saha // Pramāṇav_2.480 //
children.translated_text: which is [what we wished to be] established. Otherwise, the object too, having equal properties, [would need illumination] along with cognition. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.480]

children.text: iti prakāśarūpā naḥ svayaṃ dhīḥ samprakāśate /
children.translated_text: Thus, for us, cognition, being of the nature of luminosity, is self-luminous.

children.text: anyo 'syāṃ rūpasaṃkrāntyā prakāśaḥ san prakāśate // Pramāṇav_2.481 //
children.translated_text: Another [entity] appears in it as luminous through the transfer of form [into cognition]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.481]

children.text: sādṛśye 'pi hi dhīranyā prakāśyā na tayā matā /
children.translated_text: For even with similarity, another cognition is not regarded as that which is to be illuminated by it.
The object, being self-luminous [within cognition], appears in that form. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.482]
Just as between two lamps, or between a lamp and a pot, dependent on that [relation],
the conventional distinction of manifested and manifestor is extended. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.483]
The determination 'it is not seen' [cannot arise] from the mere contact of object and sense faculty alone.

children.text: tasmād yato 'yaṃ tasyāpi vācyamanyasya daśanam // Pramāṇav_2.484 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, since this [determination arises] from that [self-awareness], for that [cognition] too, one must state the seeing by another. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.484]
From memory too, <s>svasaṃvedana</s> (self-awareness) of cognition is established. If cognition were known by another [cognition],
the apprehension of long [vowels] and the like would be impossible, due to the instability of multiple units (<s>mātrā</s>). [Pramāṇavārttika 2.485]
If [the phoneme] were stable and non-sequential, then since in cognition there is only a single appearance,
the phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>) would be non-sequential and not long. How could what has sequence [Pramāṇavārttika 2.486]
assist a part of a phoneme that does not conjoin with another part?
The sound, increasing beyond what is established in the prior [moment], would become the final [part]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.487]
Since apprehension is non-sequential, cognition at the end would not be as if sequential.

children.text: dhiyaḥ svayaṃ ca na sthānaṃ tadūrdhvaviṣayāsthiteḥ // Pramāṇav_2.488 //
children.translated_text: And cognition itself has no abiding, because it does not persist regarding objects beyond that [moment]. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.488]

children.text: sthāne svayaṃ na naśyet sā paścādapyaviśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: If [cognition] had stability, it would not perish in its own state, nor later, since there is no difference [between the two moments].
This fault applies even to the view that the non-sequential phoneme arises and persists all at once. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.489]
Since [the phoneme] arises from a single effort, each successive effort would be purposeless.
This fault regarding phonemes follows even on the [theory of] manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>). [Pramāṇavārttika 2.490]
When there is apprehension of that [long vowel] through multiple [cognitions], the final cognition is experienced,

children.text: na dīrghagrāhikā sā ca tanna syād dīrghadhīsmṛtiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.491 //
children.translated_text: but that is not the cognition that grasps the long [vowel]; hence there would be no memory of a long-vowel cognition. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.491]

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak ca buddhīnāṃ saṃvittau taddhvaniśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: And when cognitions are individually aware of themselves, from hearing the sounds of those [phonemes],

children.text: avicchinnābhatā na syād ghaṭanaṃ ca nirākṛtam // Pramāṇav_2.492 //
children.translated_text: there would be no appearance of continuity, and the combining [of phonemes] is refuted. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.492]
If even for one who hears [them as] discontinuous there is the illusion of continuity,
then even in the utterance of two short [vowels] there would be the illusion of continuity. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.493]
And if upon discontinuous sense-perception there is superimposition of continuity,
then [this superimposition would apply] not [only] from the senses — all sense-cognitions would be false, as a consequence. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.494]
For even the last phoneme in its entirety has a duration equal to the blink of an eye,
and it persists through sequential connection with multiple atoms. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.495]
And the time of the passing of a single atom is considered the briefest duration — a <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment).

children.text: buddhiśca kṣaṇikā tasmāt kramād varṇān prapadyate // Pramāṇav_2.496 //
children.translated_text: And since cognition is momentary, it apprehends phonemes sequentially. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.496]
Thus, even with regard to phonemes as well as form and the like, [cognition] appears as continuous

children.text: vicchinnāpyanyathā buddhiḥ sarvā syād vitathārthikā // Pramāṇav_2.497 //
children.translated_text: though [it is actually] discontinuous — otherwise all cognition would be of false objects. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.497]
And the combining of entities [that appear unified] — apart from sensory error,
that memory, confused about the non-apprehension of difference, is conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>). [Pramāṇavārttika 2.498]
How can there be clear appearance for that which is associated with verbal expression?
It has been determined that there is no application of words to what is grasped by the senses. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.499]
If conceptual construction could combine [what is perceived as] discontinuous by the senses,
[then] both the object and the awareness of it, which appear continuously, [Pramāṇavārttika 2.500]

children.text: bādhake sati sannyāye vicchinna iti tat kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: when there is a defeating reason and a valid proof, whence [the claim] 'it is discontinuous'?

children.text: buddhīnāṃ śaktiniyamāditi cet sa kuto bhataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.501 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] due to the restriction of the capacity of cognitions — whence is that restriction established? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.501]
If [you say] because cognitions are not seen simultaneously — that is exactly what is being examined here.
There would be a restriction of capacity among those of the same class. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.502]
For indeed, conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>) are correctly observed as arising sequentially.
By this, one who would construct a recognition-based conceptual construction (<s>pratyabhijñāna-kalpanā</s>) regarding an object present before the eyes — [Pramāṇavārttika 2.503]
and would make it perceptual because of its vivid appearance — that [view] too is refuted,
since even in [the perception of] hair-nets, floating spots, and lamps, there is vivid appearance. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.504]
Even when difference is cognized, how could such a cognition be direct perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>)?
Therefore, the ascertainment of the unity of phonemes and the like does not follow from recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>). [Pramāṇavārttika 2.505]
Without the recollection of what was previously experienced and the superimposition of its properties,

children.text: sa evāyamiti jñānaṃ nāsti tacchakṣaje kutaḥ // Pramāṇav_2.506 //
children.translated_text: there is no cognition of the form 'this is that very same [thing].' How then could that [arise] in sense-born [cognition]? [Pramāṇavārttika 2.506]
And since the awareness of the object and the awareness of cognition are not simultaneous,

children.text: lakṣyete pratibhāso dau nārthārthajñānayoḥ pṛthak // Pramāṇav_2.507 //
children.translated_text: two appearances are observed — not separately of the object and the cognition of the object. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.507]

children.text: na hyarthābhāsi ca jñānamartho bāhyaśca kevalaḥ /
children.translated_text: For cognition that appears as the object, and the external object alone,
are not [two distinct things] to be grasped in cognition as having a single form, because duality of aspects would follow. [Pramāṇavārttika 2.508]

children.text: sūpalakṣeṇa bhedena yau saṃvittau na lakṣitau /
children.translated_text: Two [cognitions] that are not distinguished by a well-marked difference,

children.text: arthārthapratyayo paścāt smaryete tau pṛthak katham // Pramāṇav_2.509 //
children.translated_text: how could the cognition of object and [cognition of] object subsequently be remembered as distinct? // Pramāṇav 2.509 //
Even if there is sequential arising of experience, this [objection concerning] the object and the mental [cognition] of the object —
the difficulty of the manifoldness of appearance is hard to overcome. // Pramāṇav 2.510 //
First there is the cognition of the object, then the cognition of the appearance of the object;

children.text: na hi saṃvedanaṃ śuddhaṃ bhavedarthasya vedanam // Pramāṇav_2.511 //
children.translated_text: for pure self-awareness (<s>saṃvedana</s>) cannot be the cognition of the object. // Pramāṇav 2.511 //

children.text: tathā hi nīlādyākāra eka ekaṃ ca vedanam /
children.translated_text: For thus: the form of blue and so forth is one, and the cognition is one;

children.text: lakṣyate na tu nīlābhe vedane vedanaṃ param // Pramāṇav_2.512 //
children.translated_text: but in the cognition that has the appearance of blue, another cognition [of it] is not observed. // Pramāṇav 2.512 //
If the experience were through another cognition, then there would be memory of that too;

children.text: dṛṣṭā tadvedanaṃ kena tasyāpyanyena ced imām // Pramāṇav_2.513 //
children.translated_text: by what is that [other cognition] cognized? If by yet another — this // Pramāṇav 2.513 //
endless chain of cognitions — who produces it?

children.text: pūrvā dhīḥ saiva cenna syāt sañcāro viṣayāntare // Pramāṇav_2.514 //
children.translated_text: If [you say] the previous cognition itself [cognizes], then there would be no transition to another object. // Pramāṇav 2.514 //
Without apprehending that proximate generating cognition, which has attained the status of being apprehensible (<s>grāhya</s>),
how could a subsequent cognition apprehend something else? // Pramāṇav 2.515 //

children.text: ātmani jñānajanane svabhāve niyatāṃ ca tām /
children.translated_text: Who else could obstruct that [cognition], which is fixed in its own nature
as the cause of self-cognition, [being] intrinsic with respect to what is extrinsic? // Pramāṇav 2.516 //

children.text: bāhyāḥ sannihito 'pyarthastāṃ vibadhnan hi na prabhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Even an external object that is present, obstructing that [cognition], is not capable [of doing so];
for no one would fail to experience a cognition when the object is present. // Pramāṇav 2.517 //
And there is no state of cognition in which the object is not present; therefore
even memory, whose root has been pulled out, would cease — this is the brilliant [consequence of this] view. // Pramāṇav 2.518 //
For those conceptualizations of past [objects] and so forth, for which the object is not present —
due to the absence of a cause for transition, thinking about other [matters] would cease. // Pramāṇav 2.519 //
If the transition to another object [occurs] gradually through the exhaustion of the capacity
for self-cognition, then how is it the same cognition of the object? // Pramāṇav 2.520 //

children.text: śaktikṣaye pūrvādhiyo na hi dhīḥ prāgdhiyā vinā /
children.translated_text: Upon the exhaustion of the capacity of the previous cognition, there would be no cognition without the prior cognition;
in a cognition that is deficient due to engagement with another object, there is no arising of [further] cognition. // Pramāṇav 2.521 //
Even when something of a dissimilar kind has once arisen, due to the deficiency imposed
by a single more powerful mind, there is no possibility of another [cognition arising] from the repository (<s>ālaya</s>). // Pramāṇav 2.522 //
Otherwise, a mental activity would not require the equality of another mind;
even the sequential arising of mental cognitions would be a justifying requirement. // Pramāṇav 2.523 //
Since the mind is one, if, while engaged in one [object], the arrival of another [cognition occurs],
then the non-arising of another cognition would never [occur], since [both] arise simultaneously. // Pramāṇav 2.524 //
And if there were equal functioning, then transition to another [object] would always occur;
for those [cognitions] born solely from the conjunction of self and mind, arising would occur only once. // Pramāṇav 2.525 //

children.text: ekaiva cet kriyaikaḥ syāt kiṃ dīpo 'nekadarśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: If there is a single [cognition], there should be a single action — why then does a lamp [produce] multiple perceptions?

children.text: krameṇāpi na śaktaṃ syāt paścādapyaviśeṣataḥ // Pramāṇav_2.526 //
children.translated_text: Even sequentially it would not be capable, nor would it be [capable] afterwards, since there is no distinction. // Pramāṇav 2.526 //
By this [argument]: if the restriction regarding the enjoyment of body and person is due to latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>),

children.text: niyamaḥ sa kutaḥ paścāt buddheścedastu sammatam // Pramāṇav_2.527 //
children.translated_text: then whence [does the restriction come] afterwards? If [you say] from the intellect — let that be accepted. // Pramāṇav 2.527 //
Apprehensibility (<s>grāhyatā</s>) is nothing other than the capacity to generate [cognition]; generation is the defining mark of the apprehensible.

children.text: agrāhyaṃ na hi tejo 'sti na ca saukṣamyādyanaṃśake // Pramāṇav_2.528 //
children.translated_text: For there is no luminosity (<s>tejas</s>) that is not apprehensible, nor [is there non-apprehensibility] due to subtlety in what is partless. // Pramāṇav 2.528 //
Loss of the capacity for apprehensibility could occur, but not [the loss] of the generating nature itself;
for there is no other generation of apprehensibility apart from the defining mark of being apprehensible. // Pramāṇav 2.529 //
For directly, not otherwise, form and so forth cause the form-aspect in cognition;
what restriction is there on the occurrence of [something] other than the defining mark of apprehensibility? // Pramāṇav 2.530 //
That [apprehensibility] also belongs to cognition; that too is established in [its] existence.
The apprehension of the apprehensible, the material cause, and self-awareness — [this is] the defining mark of the apprehensible for the mind. // Pramāṇav 2.531 //
Thus, regarding form and so forth as well as mind, for one of purified cognition,
contemplation of the defining mark of the apprehensible — the course of <s>yogins</s> is inconceivable. // Pramāṇav 2.532 //
There, through subtlety and so forth, the apprehensible may become non-apprehensible;

children.text: rūpādi buddheḥ kiṃ jātaṃ paścād yat prāṅ na vidyate // Pramāṇav_2.533 //
children.translated_text: what has arisen in cognition from form and so forth — [that is,] that which did not exist before? // Pramāṇav 2.533 //
Therefore, given that there is self-apprehension by one's own cognition, whatever is the immediately preceding cause

children.text: cetaso grāhyatā saiva tato nārthāntare gatiḥ // Pramāṇav_2.534 //
children.translated_text: of the mind — that itself is the apprehensibility [of the mind]; hence there is no transition to another object. // Pramāṇav 2.534 //
Even in the absence of multiple capacities, an entity does not produce multiple effects;

children.text: prakṛtyaiveti gaditam nānekasmānna ced bhavet // Pramāṇav_2.535 //
children.translated_text: it is said [to do so] by its very nature — [but] not if it does not arise from multiple [causes]. // Pramāṇav 2.535 //
Nothing [arises] from a single [cause alone]; everything arises from a totality of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>).
Even one [thing] may belong to [different] totalities — thus it is said [to be] a producer of many [effects]. // Pramāṇav 2.536 //

children.text: artha pūrvañca vijñānaṃ gṛhṇīyad yadi dhīḥ parā /
children.translated_text: If a subsequent cognition were to apprehend a prior cognition and its object,
there would always be a double verbal expression — one corresponding to the observed sequence and one not. // Pramāṇav 2.537 //
Because of appearing as prior and subsequent objects, in a single mind engaged in thought and so forth,
each [thing] would appear twice, due to the appearance in both the self and the cognition of it. // Pramāṇav 2.538 //
If, in the transition to another object, the final [cognition] is not experienced,
then the non-experience of all [cognitions] follows, just as with what is experienced by others. // Pramāṇav 2.539 //
If what is experienced by oneself is perception, but what is not experienced by others [is not],

children.text: ātmānubhūtiḥ sā siddhā kuto yenaivamucyate // Pramāṇav_2.540 //
children.translated_text: then that self-experience is [already] established — whence [comes the one] by whom it is stated thus? // Pramāṇav 2.540 //
There would be non-establishment of the cause of manifestation, for one who desires the manifest from the manifest;

children.text: vyaktyasiddhavapi vyaktaṃ yadi vyaktamidaṃ jagat // Pramāṇav_2.541 //
children.translated_text: even if the manifest is not established, if the manifest is [desired] — this world is manifest. // Pramāṇav 2.541 //

body.translated_text: Chapter Three: The Section on Inference for Oneself (<s>Svārthānumāna</s>), together with the auto-commentary.

children.translated_text: A property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), pervaded by a portion of that — the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is of three kinds only.
Due to the restriction of inseparability (<s>avinābhāva</s>), the pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) are the others [that lack this]. // Pramāṇav 3.1 //
Through effect (<s>kārya</s>) and own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — by as many [aspects] as are inseparable from the cause —
the reason [operates]: the [reason based on] own-nature is [the case where] mere existence [of the reason] corresponds [to the probandum]. // Pramāṇav 3.2 //
The non-functioning of the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), when the result of non-functioning is absent,
[yields] a certain [non-apprehension] whose result is the cognition of non-existence, depending on the distinction of reasons. // Pramāṇav 3.3 //
The establishment [of the probandum] through the effects of contradictories, and the non-establishment of the status of reason —
non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), [which proves] the non-existence of what is observable and [what has] the nature of the self, is fourfold. // Pramāṇav 3.4 //
That apprehension of the cause of what is contradictory to it, which is employed [as a reason] —
in the absence of the contradictoriness of the two causes, that [apprehension] is inconclusive (<s>vyabhicāriṇī</s>). // Pramāṇav 3.5 //
The consideration of place, time, and so forth is required even in [the apprehension of] the effect of a contradictory;
otherwise it would be inconclusive — like ashes in proving coldness. // Pramāṇav 3.6 //
That which is inferred from an effect produced by a complete reason (<s>hetu</s>) —
since it does not depend on anything else, that is described as [the reason based on] own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). // Pramāṇav 3.7 //
Due to the possibility of a restriction (<s>pratibandha</s>) that follows the transformation
of the capacities [and] the results of the totality of conditions, inconclusiveness may arise regarding the effect. // Pramāṇav 3.8 //
The transition from form and so forth, which depend on a single totality [of conditions], to taste and so forth
[is known] through the inference of the property of the reason — like the transformation of smoke [from] fuel. // Pramāṇav 3.9 //
Without the operation of [its] capacity, there is no taste; that very [capacity] is another cause.
Thus the cognition of things past and simultaneous arises from the mark of their effect. // Pramāṇav 3.10 //
The production of an effect that is inferred from an incomplete reason —
[is known] through the capacity of what is residual, like the inference of passion from the body. // Pramāṇav 3.11 //
Through mere non-observation in the dissimilar instance, and the observation of the generality of the effect,
the knowledge of the reason has the appearance of a valid cognition — like [the inference of] passion and so forth from verbal statement. // Pramāṇav 3.12 //
But merely through non-observation in the dissimilar instance, there is no non-deviation (<s>avyabhicāritā</s>),
because deviation is conceivable — like cooking rice in a pot. // Pramāṇav 3.13 //
That whose negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is shown merely through non-observation —
since that is a cause of doubt, it is cited as [merely] residual. // Pramāṇav 3.14 //
Therefore, certainty regarding the reason in all three aspects has been described:

[reasons may be flawed as] unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), having a contradictory meaning (<s>viparītārtha</s>), or inconclusive (<s>vyabhicāri</s>) with respect to the dissimilar instance. // Pramāṇav 3.15 //
And that statement of the similar example (<s>vadharmya</s>) which [functions] through the inconclusive dissimilar instance,
and that which has non-observation as its result — even when that is not stated, it is understood. // Pramāṇav 3.16 //

children.text: na ca nāstīti vacanāt tannāstyeva yathā yadi /
children.translated_text: And it is not the case that from the mere statement 'it does not exist,' that thing does not exist; just as,

children.text: nāsti sa khyāpyate nyāyastadā nāstīti gamyate // Pramāṇav_3.17 //
children.translated_text: when the principle 'it does not exist' is declared, then 'it does not exist' is understood. // Pramāṇav 3.17 //
If cessation occurs upon non-observation — is what is residual inconclusive?
Even the negative concomitant would be a reason — the objection of non-establishment need not be stated. // Pramāṇav 3.18 //
There would be exclusion of the particular as the basis of the reason, through non-observation;
if [you say] there is obstruction by another means of valid cognition — at present there is no such [obstruction]. // Pramāṇav 3.19 //
Likewise, in other cases too, obstruction by another means of valid cognition may be conceivable;
the reasoning based on observation is non-contradictory even regarding the unobserved, as in the case of touch. // Pramāṇav 3.20 //
Due to differences of place and so forth, different capacities (<s>śaktis</s>) are seen in substances;
certainty of the existence of that [capacity] elsewhere is not justified from observation in one [case] alone. // Pramāṇav 3.21 //
That same non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) which does not prove the non-existence

children.text: sa evānupalambhaḥ kiṃ hetvabhāvasya sādhakaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.22 //
children.translated_text: of the self, atoms, consciousness, and so forth — how can it prove the non-existence of the reason? // Pramāṇav 3.22 //
Therefore, [a reason] connected with that alone, [based on] own-nature, would establish either existence
or a cause or an effect, without deviation. // Pramāṇav 3.23 //
How could the cessation of one thing bring about the cessation of another?

children.text: nāścavāniti martyena na bhāvyaṃ gomatāpi kim // Pramāṇav_3.24 //
children.translated_text: A mortal should not think 'there are no horses' — would there also be [no] cows? // Pramāṇav 3.24 //
How does the presence of one [thing] entail the presence of another?
A mortal should think 'there are cows' — would there also be horses? // Pramāṇav 3.25 //
Therefore, in the dissimilar example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>), dependence [on it] is not required here;

children.text: tadabhāve ca tanneti vacanādapi tadgatiḥ // Pramāṇav_3.26 //
children.translated_text: and from the statement 'in its absence, that [does not exist]' too, that [conclusion] is understood. // Pramāṇav 3.26 //
For the relations of existence-of-that and reason-status are, in the example, for one who does not know them,

children.text: khyāpyete viduṣāṃ vācyo hetureva hi kevalaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.27 //
children.translated_text: made known; but for those who know, only the reason alone need be stated. // Pramāṇav 3.27 //
When the connection is known through that very [reason], from the statement of either one of the two,
by implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>), the recollection of the second too arises. // Pramāṇav 3.28 //
Therefore, the non-existence of the nature of the reason is also a reason for the negation of something;
and the non-apprehension of that which should be apprehendable [is a valid reason]. // Pramāṇav 3.29 //
Thus, this non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), though said to be threefold, is of many kinds,
through the distinction of application according to the [various] contradictories and so forth. // Pramāṇav 3.30 //
The restriction of inseparability (<s>avinābhāva</s>) [is established] from the relation of cause and effect, or from own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) which is the determiner;
[it is established] not from non-observation [alone], but from observation. // Pramāṇav 3.31 //
What is the restriction of necessary occurrence of another [thing] that [can be established] by others otherwise?

children.text: arthāntaranimitte vā dharme vāsasi rāgavat // Pramāṇav_3.32 //
children.translated_text: If a property is caused by something else, or [the property resides] in a substrate — like passion [in a red cloth]. // Pramāṇav 3.32 //

children.text: arthāntaranimitto hi dharmaḥ syādanya eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: For a property caused by something else would be an entirely different [thing];

children.text: paśyād bhāvānna hetutvaṃ phale 'pyekāntatā kutaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.33 //
children.translated_text: from the observation of [mere] entities, there is no reason-status; whence would there be certainty regarding the effect? // Pramāṇav 3.33 //
Smoke is an effect of fire, because of its conformity with the properties of the cause;

children.text: tasyābhāve tu sa bhavan hetumatāṃ vilaṅghayet // Pramāṇav_3.34 //
children.translated_text: but if [smoke] were to exist in the absence of that [fire], it would transgress [the rule regarding] things that have causes. // Pramāṇav 3.34 //
Either the reason would permanently exist or permanently not exist, since it does not depend on anything else;
and from [its] dependence, the occasional occurrence of entities is possible. // Pramāṇav 3.35 //
If [<s>Indra's</s>] thunderbolt is of the nature of fire, [and] its head is indeed fire,
but if it is not of the nature of fire — how could smoke exist there? // Pramāṇav 3.36 //
For fire is of the nature of being the cause of smoke, having distinct capacities for that;
if smoke were to exist from what is not the cause of smoke, then that [smoke] would be causeless. // Pramāṇav 3.37 //
That which is observed to be a concomitant of that, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>),
is the own-nature of that [thing] — that is its cause; hence [the effect] cannot arise from what is different [from it]. // Pramāṇav 3.38 //
Even in [the reason based on] own-nature, inseparability [holds] when [the reason] corresponds to mere existence;
in its existence, the non-existence of its own nature would [follow] due to non-difference. // Pramāṇav 3.39 //
All entities are established in their respective own-natures through [their] own-nature;
Since [things] partake of exclusion through both their own nature and the nature of others, // Pramāṇav 3.40 //
therefore, from whatever [aspects] the exclusions of objects [arise], dependent on those,
distinctions of <s>jāti</s> (universal class) are conceptually constructed, penetrating into the particularities of those [objects]. // Pramāṇav 3.41 //

children.text: tasmād viśeṣo yo yena dharmeṇa sampratīyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, a particular that is cognized through a certain property

children.text: na da śakyastato 'nyena tena bhinnā vyavasthitiḥ // Pramāṇav_3.42 //
children.translated_text: cannot be differentiated by anything other than that; hence the distinction [of classes] is established [only] thereby. // Pramāṇav 3.42 //
Of a single entity whose nature is self-evident to direct perception,

children.text: ko 'nyo bhāgo na dṛṣṭaḥ syād yaḥ pramāṇaiḥ parīkṣyate // Pramāṇav_3.43 //
children.translated_text: what other aspect could remain unseen that would need to be examined by <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid cognition)? // Pramāṇav 3.43 //
Unless, due to a cause of error, an additional quality were to be superimposed—
like the appearance of silver in a shell, from seeing a similarity of form. // Pramāṇav 3.44 //

children.text: tasmād dṛṣṭasya bhāvasya dṛṣṭa evākhilo guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, every quality of a perceived entity is itself perceived;
it is through error that one ascertains 'this is not [so],' and [then] a means of proof is set in motion. // Pramāṇav 3.45 //
In grasping a real thing, and from inference in ascertaining a single property,

children.text: sarvagraho hyapohe tu nāyaṃ doṣaḥ prasajyate // Pramāṇav_3.46 //
children.translated_text: there is apprehension of the whole; but in <s>apoha</s> (exclusion), this fault does not arise. // Pramāṇav 3.46 //
Therefore, the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is declared to have <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) as its object;

children.text: anyathā dharmiṇaḥ siddhavasiddhaṃ kimataḥ param // Pramāṇav_3.47 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, what further [remains] beyond the established or unestablished [nature] of the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>)? // Pramāṇav 3.47 //
In some cases, cognition having a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object, when [the particular] is perceived, is not born from a logical mark;
how then is it an object of <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other)—having as its scope the exclusion of that alone? // Pramāṇav 3.48 //
From the relation of what is to be sublated and what sublates, [we understand that] ascertainments and superimposing cognitions
operate through the discrimination of superimposition—thus it is understood. // Pramāṇav 3.49 //
As many as are the superimpositions of [erroneous] aspects, so many are the ascertainments [that negate them],

children.text: tāvanta eva śabdāśca tena te bhinnagocarāḥ // Pramāṇav_3.50 //
children.translated_text: and equally many are the words; therefore they have distinct domains. // Pramāṇav 3.50 //
Otherwise, with a single word pervading a single object,

children.text: buddh yā vā nānyavisaya iti paryāyatā bhavet // Pramāṇav_3.51 //
children.translated_text: or with a cognition having no other object, there would be synonymity. // Pramāṇav 3.51 //
Even for one whose cognition, through diverse limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>), apprehends a differentiated object—
in apprehending [an entity] whose nature is undifferentiated from the capacity that is a component of the benefit of diverse limiting conditions, // Pramāṇav 3.52 //
what unascertained difference could there be of that which is benefited in its entirety?
Due to the connection of both in a single nature, there is apprehension of both in a single cognition. // Pramāṇav 3.53 //
If the capacities that benefit properties are different, what if they do not benefit that [entity]?
Then there would be no stable determination of those [capacities]. // Pramāṇav 3.54 //
When what is apprehended has a single benefiting [capacity], the other [capacities] do not benefit [it]; hence
when that is perceived, the unseen [capacities] too—in apprehending that, [there would be] apprehension of all. // Pramāṇav 3.55 //
If, for the purpose of removing error, even when [something] is apprehended, another [aspect] is desired,
then it is established that [cognition] has the exclusion of that as its object; and similarly for what is beyond that. // Pramāṇav 3.56 //
Even when ascertainments operate regarding an object not [yet] superimposed upon,

children.text: yanna niścīyate rūpaṃ tat teṣāṃ viṣayaḥ katham // Pramāṇav_3.57 //
children.translated_text: the form that is not ascertained [by them]—how can that be their object? // Pramāṇav 3.57 //
Even when a particular is apprehended by direct perception, free of [erroneous] aspects,
there is a cognition for the ascertainment of that particular—and that [cognition] is what is experienced. // Pramāṇav 3.58 //
Even there, 'exclusion from others' and 'that which is excluded from others'—
both words and ascertainments follow [their respective] causes. // Pramāṇav 3.59 //
Even when two [things] are denoted by a single expression, the case-ending that differentiates
follows as if [indicating] a different meaning, by virtue of a distinguishing trace of what is to be expressed. // Pramāṇav 3.60 //
The non-rejection and rejection of another difference in the case of those two
is the basis for the difference of convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), which follows the desire of the knower. // Pramāṇav 3.61 //
This very difference [applies] everywhere between two words denoting substance and quality;
there is no [real] distinction whatsoever in their referent; hence [the difference lies in convention]. // Pramāṇav 3.62 //

children.text: jijñāpayiṣurartha taṃ taddhitena taṃ taddhitena kṛtāpi vā /
children.translated_text: One wishing to communicate that meaning, whether through a <s>taddhita</s> (secondary derivative suffix)

children.text: antena vā yadi brū yāt bhedo nāsti tataḥ paraḥ // Pramāṇav_3.63 //
children.translated_text: or through a <s>kṛt</s> (primary derivative suffix), or by [another] ending—if one were to speak, there is no difference beyond that. // Pramāṇav 3.63 //
Therefore, describing the <s>tadvatpakṣa</s> (possessor thesis) regarding what has <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) as its object

children.text: pratyākhyātaṃ pṛthaktve hi syād doṣo jātitadvatoḥ // Pramāṇav_3.64 //
children.translated_text: has been rejected; for if [universals were] separate, there would be the fault [of the relation] between <s>jāti</s> (universal) and its possessor. // Pramāṇav 3.64 //
For those who [hold that] words depend on the nature of real things and do not depend on the speaker's intention—

children.text: ṣaṣṭhīvacanabhedādi codyaṃ tān prati yuktimat // Pramāṇav_3.65 //
children.translated_text: the objection concerning the difference of genitive expressions and the like is appropriate against them. // Pramāṇav 3.65 //
Whatever is conventionally assigned as an expression by speakers in whatever manner,

children.text: anapekṣitavāhyārtha tat tathā vācakaṃ vacaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.66 //
children.translated_text: that speech is expressive in just that way, without regard to external objects. // Pramāṇav 3.66 //
In expressions like '<s>dārāḥ</s>' (wives, [plural for singular]) and '<s>ṣaḍ nagarī</s>' (six cities [for one city]), where unity and plurality are conventionally fixed—

children.text: khasya svabhāvaḥ khatvaṃ cetyatra vā kiṃ nibandhanam // Pramāṇav_3.67 //
children.translated_text: or in '<s>khasya svabhāvaḥ khatvam</s>' (the nature of space is space-ness)—what is the basis [for insisting on real reference]? // Pramāṇav 3.67 //
By that cognition which conceals the distinct nature [of things] through its own form,
appearing as a single object, relying upon entities that are [in fact] different— // Pramāṇav 3.68 //
by that, [entities] whose multiplicity is concealed by <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional cognition), being themselves different,

children.text: abhedina ivābhānti bhāvā rūpeṇa kenacit // Pramāṇav_3.69 //
children.translated_text: appear as if non-different through some [common] form. // Pramāṇav 3.69 //
Due to the intention of that [cognition], a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is declared to exist [only] conventionally;

children.text: tadasat paramārthena yathā saṅkalpitaṃ tayā // Pramāṇav_3.70 //
children.translated_text: it is unreal in the ultimate sense, [existing] just as it is imagined by that [cognition]. // Pramāṇav 3.70 //
Particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>) do not follow another [i.e., a universal]; what follows [them] does not appear [as separate];
or, if it is not different from cognition, how could it go to another object? // Pramāṇav 3.71 //
Therefore, this is a false conceptual construction (<s>mithyāvikalpa</s>)—the apprehension of a single nature in [diverse] objects;
the mutual difference of these [objects] is the seed [of this construction], and the conventional name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is what serves the purpose. // Pramāṇav 3.72 //
From the cognition whose purpose is a single reflective judgment, those that serve the same end—
even though different, certain [things] are fixed by their own nature, like sense faculties and the like. // Pramāṇav 3.73 //
Just as certain medicines are seen to cure fever and the like, either together or individually,

children.text: dṛṣṭā yathā vauṣadhayo nānātve 'pi na cāparāḥ // Pramāṇav_3.74 //
children.translated_text: and yet others [that are different] are not [effective]— // Pramāṇav 3.74 //
[One should] not [infer] a universal from [mere] non-difference, because of the absurd consequence of [everything being] non-different;

and because of the constancy [of the universal's presence] even when there is difference in location and so forth, [there would be] no [specific] beneficial effect of those [medicines]. // Pramāṇav 3.75 //
The cognition that arises from grasping the nature of that [object], or is purposeless regarding that object,
being of the nature of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), is produced as resting on the distinction of effects and non-effects of that. // Pramāṇav 3.76 //
In that [cognition], the form that appears as if a single external [entity] excluded from others
is devoid of real essence, because [such analysis] does not form part of [practical] examination. // Pramāṇav 3.77 //
Objects established in cognition, having the form of being excluded [from others],

children.text: abhinnā iva cābhānti vyāvṛttāḥ punaranyataḥ // Pramāṇav_3.78 //
children.translated_text: appear as if non-different, [while being] further excluded from other [things]. // Pramāṇav 3.78 //
Those very [exclusions], through cognitions and expressions that range over a common substratum as [if they were] universals—
conventional discourse (<s>vyavahāra</s>) with false content is extended. // Pramāṇav 3.79 //
And all of that [discourse] depends on the mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>) of things;
therefore it has <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) as its object, and depends on an appearance of a [non-existent] real thing. // Pramāṇav 3.80 //
Where there is a connection with a real thing, as in the inference described above,

children.text: nānyatra bhrāntisāmye 'pi dīpatejo maṇau yathā // Pramāṇav_3.81 //
children.translated_text: [it is effective]; not elsewhere, even when the error is equal—just as lamplight [is not present] in a gem [that merely resembles it]. // Pramāṇav 3.81 //
Therein, even though many [things] produce the same effect, [conventional discourse] based on the otherness of what does not produce that effect
is extended through expressions and cognitions [that treat them] as one. // Pramāṇav 3.82 //
Hence, even one [thing] that produces many [effects], in illuminating its [particular] nature,
is cognized as having diverse properties, through the distinction of effects not produced by it [versus those produced by it]. // Pramāṇav 3.83 //
The meaning of words has been stated according to how [things] are cognized, even though it is not real;

children.text: samānādhikaraṇyaṃ ca vastunyasya na sambhavaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.84 //
children.translated_text: and co-reference (<s>samānādhikaraṇya</s>) does not [truly] obtain in a real thing. // Pramāṇav 3.84 //
The distinction of property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), and such difference and non-difference
as is cognized in the world without examining the true nature of things— // Pramāṇav 3.85 //
relying on just that, the arrangement of what is to be proved and the means of proof
is devised by the learned for the purpose of arriving at ultimate truth. // Pramāṇav 3.86 //
Ultimate real things are neither combined nor differentiated by themselves;
the [appearance of] one form and many forms in them is an error of the intellect. // Pramāṇav 3.87 //
Therefore, this difference is [only] in the intellectually constructed object; [what appears as] a universal is also [merely] a difference;
and through the exclusion of that very [object] from others, the differentiation of properties is conceptually constructed. // Pramāṇav 3.88 //
In the conceptual construction of what is to be proved and the means of proof, due to the loss of seeing the real thing,

children.text: bhedaḥ sāmānyasaṃsṛṣṭo grāhyo nātra svalakṣaṇam // Pramāṇav_3.89 //
children.translated_text: what is to be apprehended is difference conjoined with a universal—not the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular) here. // Pramāṇav 3.89 //
That [particular] cannot be apprehended in any way through forms such as 'same,' 'different,' and so forth,
because of the impossibility of [all] those many differences [residing] in that single [particular]. // Pramāṇav 3.90 //

children.text: tadrū paṃ sarvato bhinnaṃ tathā tatpratipādikā /
children.translated_text: Its form, being completely different from everything, likewise cannot be conveyed by

children.text: na śrutiḥ kalpanā vāsti samānyenaiva vṛttitaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.91 //
children.translated_text: verbal testimony (<s>śruti</s>) or conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>), since these operate only through universals. // Pramāṇav 3.91 //
Words express what has been conventionally designated (<s>saṃketita</s>), and that [designation] is remembered for the sake of practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>);

children.text: tadā svalakṣaṇaṃ nāsti saṃketastena tatra na // Pramāṇav_3.92 //
children.translated_text: there is no convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) for a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular) as such; therefore there is no [verbal designation] of it. // Pramāṇav 3.92 //
A person would act [only] upon knowing things capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākṣama</s>);
for the accomplishment of that [purpose], acts of verbal designation are connected with objects. // Pramāṇav 3.93 //
Therein, a <s>jāti</s> (universal) is incapable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), and its possessor is not sufficient [as referent]; and that [possessor]
is not directly connected—because of [its] infinity? If so, the same [problem arises for you]. // Pramāṇav 3.94 //
When there is sameness of the difference between what produces that [effect] and what does not, why has [a universal] been posited?
If [you say] because of the sameness of the fault in [our position] as in yours—then let the <s>jāti</s> (universal) be; it is superfluous. // Pramāṇav 3.95 //
And the implication is that [a person] acts by excluding others [i.e., through <s>apoha</s>];

children.text: ucyate tena tebhyo 'syāvyavacchede kathaṃ ca saḥ // Pramāṇav_3.96 //
