children.translated_text: it is said: how then [could there be] non-exclusion of those from it? // Pramāṇav 3.96 //
If there is exclusion of this [from others], is not this much alone the purpose

children.text: śabdānāmiti kiṃ tatra sāmānyenāpareṇa vaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.97 //
children.translated_text: of words—what then is the need for yet another universal for you? // Pramāṇav 3.97 //

children.text: jñānādyarthakriyāṃ tāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhede 'pi kuvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen that [objects], though different, produce this or that causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) from cognition and so forth,
those objects, together with sounds that have as their domain the separation from what is other than that— // Pramāṇav 3.98 //
connecting [them], one would produce recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) even upon seeing another [instance];

children.text: parasyāpi na sā buddhiḥ sāmānyādeva kevalāt // Pramāṇav_3.99 //
children.translated_text: but even for the other [party], that cognition does not arise from the universal alone as such. // Pramāṇav 3.99 //
Because, if there were always cognition of that [universal] alone, there would be the absurd consequence of non-cognition of particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>);
then, of a possessor [of the universal] that was at some point connected [with it] but not [previously] apprehended, // Pramāṇav 3.100 //
there would be no ascertainment that it possesses that [universal]—how then could there be practical activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>)?
If [you say that] particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>) together with one [associated] entity are the cause of cognition— // Pramāṇav 3.101 //

children.text: tadekaṃ vastu kiṃ tāsāṃ nānātvaṃ samapohati /
children.translated_text: does that one entity remove their multiplicity?
Because of their multiplicity, causation of a single cognition is not accepted in them. // Pramāṇav 3.102 //
If, even though many, they produce a non-different cognition in dependence on one [entity]—

children.text: tābhirvināpi pratyakaṃ kriyamāṇāṃ dhiyaṃ prati // Pramāṇav_3.103 //
children.translated_text: even without those [particulars], with respect to the cognition that is individually produced, // Pramāṇav 3.103 //
by that one [entity] alone there would be capacity—the apprehension that those [particulars] are 'not [the cause]' by the intellect,
from the observation of independent capacity in visual cognition of blue and the like. // Pramāṇav 3.104 //
The establishment of capacity is in the aggregate, not at all in the particular (<s>vyakti</s>) [alone];
if it is capable [only] in dependence on the otherness of those, then it is not [capable] alone. // Pramāṇav 3.105 //
How would they assist that one [entity], and [how would they] not [produce] a single cognition?

children.text: kārya ca tāsāṃ prāpto 'sau jananaṃ yadupakriyā // Pramāṇav_3.106 //
children.translated_text: And the production [of cognition] is the effect of those [particulars]; that assistance has [already] been obtained. // Pramāṇav 3.106 //
If the view is that a cognition with a non-different appearance does not [arise] regarding different [things]—

children.text: pratibhāso dhiyā bhinnaḥ samānā iti tadgrahāt // Pramāṇav_3.107 //
children.translated_text: [we reply:] the appearance is different from the cognition; from the apprehension that [they are] 'the same,' // Pramāṇav 3.107 //
how can they, apprehended by different cognitions, be the same? If [you say they are] the same, there would be single-effect-ness;

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ nanu dhīḥ kārya tāsāṃ sā ca vibhidyate // Pramāṇav_3.108 //
children.translated_text: but surely the cognition that is the effect of those [particulars] is the similarity, and that too is differentiated. // Pramāṇav 3.108 //
Because it is the cause of a single reflective judgment, the cognition is non-differentiating;
[but] by being the cause of a single cognition, even of the particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>) there would be non-difference. // Pramāṇav 3.109 //
And that [non-difference] is [nothing but] the separation from what does not produce that effect; since an invariable concomitant other than that
is not observed—and because of [its] negation—the convention (<s>saṃketa</s>) serves the purpose of [knowing] that [exclusion]. // Pramāṇav 3.110 //
Verbal testimony (<s>śruti</s>), having as its purpose activity through the exclusion of what does not produce that effect,
even though it produces a cognition that manifests a form similar to what produces that effect [yet is itself] not a producer of the effect— // Pramāṇav 3.111 //
a cognition whose seed is merely the separateness from real things, [and which is] purposeless [in itself]—
nevertheless, because it functions as a component of the exclusion of what does not produce that effect, [it serves practical activity]. // Pramāṇav 3.112 //
And because [the cognition] is based on real distinctions in the object, it is not considered misleading,
therefore it has <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) as its object, because it depends on the nature established by that [real distinction]. // Pramāṇav_3.113 //
In apprehending the meaning of 'tree' through exclusion of non-tree, both [the word and the cognition]
involve mutual dependence — thus, in the absence of grasping one, neither is grasped. // Pramāṇav_3.114 //
Therefore some declare that <s>saṅketa</s> (linguistic convention) is impossible.

children.text: teṣāmavṛkṣāḥ saṃṅkete vyavacchinnā na vā yadi // Pramāṇav_3.115 //
children.translated_text: For them [we ask]: in the convention, are non-trees excluded or not? // Pramāṇav_3.115 //
If excluded, how are they known prior to and apart from grasping 'tree'?
If those [non-trees] are not excluded in the convention, then for those who engage in ordinary usage, // Pramāṇav_3.116 //
there would be no activity through the avoidance of those [non-trees], just as with the varieties of trees.

children.text: avidhāya niṣidhyānyat pradarśyaikaṃ puraḥ sthitam // Pramāṇav_3.117 //
children.translated_text: Without [first] establishing [the meaning], by negating what is other, and showing the one [thing] present before [the learner], // Pramāṇav_3.117 //
the convention is made: 'This is a tree' — one accepts that.

children.text: vyavahāre 'pi tenāyamadoṣa iti cet taruḥ // Pramāṇav_3.118 //
children.translated_text: If [one says] there is no fault in ordinary usage either through this [method], then [consider]: the tree — // Pramāṇav_3.118 //
the unwanted consequence that 'this one too is just this one' does not cease,

children.text: ekapratyavamarśākhye jñāne ekatra hi sthitaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.119 //
children.translated_text: for it is established in a single cognition called recognition (<s>pratyavamarśa</s>) directed at one [object]. // Pramāṇav_3.119 //
The one who accepts [this] discriminates for himself the objects that are causes of being that and not-that;

children.text: tadbuddhivartino bhāvān bhāto hetutayā dhiyaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.120 //
children.translated_text: things that conform to that cognition, appearing as causes of the cognition, // Pramāṇav_3.120 //
lacking the form of non-cause, [yet appearing] as if having many forms of their own —
the statement that one apprehends [them] as distinct applies [only] to [real] distinction. // Pramāṇav_3.121 //

children.text: taṃ tasyā pratiyatī dhīḥ bhrāntyaikaṃ vastvivekṣate /
children.translated_text: The cognition apprehends that [object] of that [convention]; through error it regards [many] as a single entity.
For the purpose of applying [a word] to a certain object, having excluded [it] from certain [others], // Pramāṇav_3.122 //
a word is employed for [directing] the cognition, because it determines that meaning.
Otherwise its usage would be purposeless — this applies also to words like 'that which is to be known' (<s>jñeya</s>) and so on. // Pramāṇav_3.123 //
Among things brought into conventional usage, there is something to be excluded,

children.text: niveśanaṃ ca yo yasmād bhidyate vinivartya tam // Pramāṇav_3.124 //
children.translated_text: and the application [of a word] is to that which differs from that [excluded thing], having excluded it. // Pramāṇav_3.124 //
Among those that are differentiated by the distinction of that, appearing with a common form,

children.text: sa cāyamanyavyāvṛttyā gamyate tasya vastunaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.125 //
children.translated_text: and this [common form] is understood through the exclusion of others (<s>anyavyāvṛtti</s>) — of that entity, // Pramāṇav_3.125 //

children.text: kaścid bhāga iti prokto rūpaṃ nāsyāpi kiñcina /
children.translated_text: it is said to be some part. But there is no [real] form of this either;
it is only in their apprehension that the exclusion of others is understood from words. // Pramāṇav_3.126 //

children.text: na tatra gamyate kaścid viśiṣṭaḥ kenacit paraḥ /
children.translated_text: No particular [entity] distinguished by something else is apprehended therein,

children.text: na cāpi śabdo dvayakṛdanyonyābhāva ityasau // Pramāṇav_3.127 //
children.translated_text: nor does the word produce a duality — this [exclusion] is [merely] the mutual absence. // Pramāṇav_3.127 //
The perception of what is formless as having form is a distortion of cognition.
Therefore this [universal] is not ultimately real; for otherwise, of a real entity, // Pramāṇav_3.128 //
exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) would be a real thing, [meaning] its distinction from this [other thing] through elimination.
A single sound operates to sever the connection with one meaning. // Pramāṇav_3.129 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ vā tatra vicchinnaṃ vācyaṃ vastu na kiñcana /
children.translated_text: Or it is a sign (<s>liṅga</s>) separated therein — no real entity is the object of denotation,
[for the word] from whose denotation, by the power of the real entity, there is understanding of the whole [class]. // Pramāṇav_3.130 //
A word with multiple results comes to have a single basis; therefore,
indicating the separation [from others], it operates without rejecting the one [particular]. // Pramāṇav_3.131 //

children.text: yadānyat tena sa vyāpta ekatvena ca bhāsate /
children.translated_text: When something else is pervaded by that and appears as one [with it],
then there would be co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), due to conformity with the cognition. // Pramāṇav_3.132 //
The contact of the property of a real entity in making the word effect a separation

children.text: syāt satyaṃ sa hi tatreti naikavastvabhidhāyini // Pramāṇav_3.133 //
children.translated_text: would indeed be [real] — for it is there [in the thing]. But [the word] does not denote a single entity. // Pramāṇav_3.133 //
Because of the ascertainment of the absence of the visible [universal] that appears in cognition,
therefore [words and cognitions] are said to have <s>anyāpoha</s> (exclusion of the other) as their domain, having <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) as [merely apparent] scope. // Pramāṇav_3.134 //
Both words and cognitions [cannot pertain to] the real entity, because of the impossibility of these [universals] in [real] things.

children.text: ekatvād vasturūpasya bhinnarūpā matiḥ kutaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.135 //
children.translated_text: Since the nature of a real entity is one, how could there be a cognition of diverse forms? // Pramāṇav_3.135 //
Moreover, <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) of a single [entity] cannot have a single object as their scope,
and conventions of non-difference would be groundless where there is [actual] difference. // Pramāṇav_3.136 //
Since exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) is present everywhere, these faults do not follow;
in prompting the effect of that [common causal capacity] among entities that have a common effect, // Pramāṇav_3.137 //
because of the cumbersomeness, incapacity, and futility of expressing [each] difference, an equivalent verbal expression
has been made by the wise, based on the exclusion of what does not produce that effect. // Pramāṇav_3.138 //
This is not [a universal] existing in [all] things, because each entity is established in its own nature.

children.text: yad rūpaṃ śābaleyasya bāhuleyasya nāsti tat // Pramāṇav_3.139 //
children.translated_text: The form that belongs to <s>Śābaleya</s> (one particular cow) does not exist in <s>Bāhuleya</s> (another cow). // Pramāṇav_3.139 //
And the turning away from what does not produce that effect exists in both [cows];

children.text: arthābhedena ca vinā śabdābhedo na yujyate // Pramāṇav_3.140 //
children.translated_text: and without identity of meaning, identity of word is not justified. // Pramāṇav_3.140 //
Therefore, the capacity to produce that effect is also accepted; the distinction is [determined] only from the [distinct] effect of that.

children.text: cakṣu rādau yathā rūpavijñānaikaphale kvacit // Pramāṇav_3.141 //
children.translated_text: Just as with the eye and so forth, in some case where there is a single result of visual cognition, // Pramāṇav_3.141 //
when it is possible to indicate that [common] effect without distinction,

children.text: sakṛt sarvapratītyartha kaścit sāṃketikīṃ śrutim // Pramāṇav_3.142 //
children.translated_text: someone would make a conventional expression for the purpose of communicating everything at once, // Pramāṇav_3.142 //
even without a real universal that differs from those forms.
Even if many [things] belonging to a single class were to have a single verbal expression, // Pramāṇav_3.143 //
occurrence, being a substrate, and manifestation — these do not apply to that [universal],
for [the universal] being eternal cannot be helped [by anything], hence there is no substrate for what extends [everywhere]. // Pramāṇav_3.144 //
The power [of the universal to manifest] would be birth in that place, like <s>kuṇḍa</s>-berries (jujube) and <s>badara</s>-berries (plums) and so on,
but that [power] too is impossible here, because [the universal] persists even in the absence of that [manifestor]. // Pramāṇav_3.145 //
That persistence too is simply unjustified, upon examination of difference and non-difference.
That which depends on others in itself, for the purpose of fitness to produce cognition, // Pramāṇav_3.146 //

children.text: tad vyaṅgyaṃ yogyatāyāśca kāraṇaṃ kārakaṃ matam /
children.translated_text: that is what is to be manifested (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), and the cause of that fitness is considered the manifestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>).

children.text: prāgevāsya ca yogyatve tadapekṣā na yujyate // Pramāṇav_3.147 //
children.translated_text: But if [the universal] already has fitness prior [to the manifestor], then dependence on that [manifestor] is not justified. // Pramāṇav_3.147 //
How could there be a refinement of the sense-faculty for the unchangeable universal, just as there is

children.text: añjanāderiva vyakteḥ saṃskāro nendriyasya ca // Pramāṇav_3.148 //
children.translated_text: for a manifest [object] through collyrium and the like — there is no such refinement of the sense-organ [for perceiving universals]. // Pramāṇav_3.148 //
Because cognition is the same in the times of presence and absence of that [universal],

children.text: vyañjakasya ca jātīnāṃ jātimattā yadīṣyate // Pramāṇav_3.149 //
children.translated_text: and if it is accepted that <s>jātis</s> (universals) possess <s>jāti</s> (a universal of their own), // Pramāṇav_3.149 //
then one possessing that [higher universal], such as <s>gotva</s> (cowness) and so on, would be a revealer — like a lamp and so forth.

children.text: vyakteranyātha vānanyā yeṣāṃ jātistu vidyate // Pramāṇav_3.150 //
children.translated_text: Or those for whom there exists a <s>jāti</s> that is neither different nor non-different from the individual (<s>vyakti</s>), // Pramāṇav_3.150 //
for them, how can there be cognitions of the universal in previously unencountered individuals?
Because [the universal] existing in one [individual] cannot be seen in another where it exists [as well]. // Pramāṇav_3.151 //
If non-different [from the individual], there is no positive concomitance; if different, [the universal] has no support.

children.text: na yāti na ca tatrāsīdasti paścānna cāṃśavat // Pramāṇav_3.152 //
children.translated_text: It does not go [to another locus], nor was it there [before]; it exists afterwards — but not as a part. // Pramāṇav_3.152 //
It does not leave its prior substrate — what a succession of absurdities!
When [something] existing elsewhere comes into being in another place, // Pramāṇav_3.153 //
that it occurs without moving from its own place — this is exceedingly unreasonable.

children.text: yatrāsau varttate bhāvastena sambadhyate 'pi na // Pramāṇav_3.154 //
children.translated_text: And the entity that exists there is not even connected with that [locus], // Pramāṇav_3.154 //
yet pervades what is in that place — what an extraordinary wonder this is!

children.text: vyaktyaivaikatra sā vyaktāabhedāt sarvatragā yadi // Pramāṇav_3.155 //
children.translated_text: If [the universal], being manifested by an individual in one [locus], is omnipresent due to non-difference [from individuals], // Pramāṇav_3.155 //
it should be perceived everywhere due to non-difference; and it [the universal] would not depend on a manifestor.

children.text: byañjakasyāpratītau na vyaṅgyaṃ samyak pratīyate // Pramāṇav_3.156 //
children.translated_text: When the manifestor (<s>vyañjaka</s>) is not cognized, the manifestable (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is not properly cognized [either]. // Pramāṇav_3.156 //
Why then is the reverse accepted for the universal and its possessor?
In [cases like] 'cook' (<s>pācaka</s>) and so on, [a word] is expressive even without an undifferentiated [universal] entity. // Pramāṇav_3.157 //

children.text: bhedānna hetuḥ karmāsya na jātiḥ karmasaṃśrayāt /
children.translated_text: [The basis of the word 'cook'] is not <s>karma</s> (action), due to difference, nor is it <s>jāti</s> (universal), because it depends on action.
Because [the word arises] from another cause [than universal], and because action has no permanence, // Pramāṇav_3.158 //
the universal [is not the cause] due to lack of connection; nor is something unjustified the cause of the word.
Due to over-extension, action too — [if] non-existent — cannot be [the basis] of cognition and denotation, // Pramāṇav_3.159 //
because the consequence of causelessness [would follow]; nor is it a power (<s>śakti</s>), due to lack of positive concomitance.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ pācakatvādi yadi prāgeva tad bhavet // Pramāṇav_3.160 //
children.translated_text: If <s>pācakatva</s> (being a cook) and the like were a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), then that would exist even before [the action], // Pramāṇav_3.160 //
manifestly, like <s>sattā</s> (existence) — if not, then afterwards [it would exist] without any distinction.
For that which is unchangeable, if [the universal] is the manifestor depending on the assistance of action, // Pramāṇav_3.161 //
even if there were an excess of dependence, whence would action [arise], since [it is] momentary?

children.text: tulye bhede yayā jāti pratyāsattyā prasarpati // Pramāṇav_3.162 //
children.translated_text: Whatever proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>) by which the <s>jāti</s> extends to some [individuals], when difference is equal, // Pramāṇav_3.162 //
let that alone, and not another, be the basis of the word and cognition.

children.text: na nivṛttiṃ vihāyāsti yadi bhāvānvayo 'paraḥ // Pramāṇav_3.163 //
children.translated_text: If there is no other positive relation to entities apart from exclusion (<s>nivṛtti</s>), // Pramāṇav_3.163 //
the effect of one cannot be [the effect] of another, due to absolute difference.
If many [things] are causes of a single effect by virtue of having a single nature, // Pramāṇav_3.164 //

children.text: ātmaikatrāpi vā so 'stīti vyarthāḥ syuḥ sahakāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: or if that [nature] exists in even one [of them], then the co-operating conditions would be purposeless.

children.text: napaityabhinnaṃ tad rūpaṃ viśeṣāḥ khalvapāyinaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.165 //
children.translated_text: That form which is undifferentiated does not depart; the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars) indeed are what perish. // Pramāṇav_3.165 //
Since the effect ceases when one [particular] ceases, the arising of that [effect] is from the <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars).

children.text: sa pāramārthiko bhāvo ya evārthakriyākṣamaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.166 //
children.translated_text: That which is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) — that alone is the ultimately real entity. // Pramāṇav_3.166 //

children.text: sa ca nānveti yonveti na tasmāt kāryasambhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that [ultimately real] does not persist; what persists — from that, no effect is possible.

children.text: tenātmanāpi bhede hi hetuḥ kaścinna cāparaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.167 //
children.translated_text: For even in [the case of] difference, some [particular] by that very nature is a cause, and nothing else [is]. // Pramāṇav_3.167 //
This is its <s>svabhāva</s> (own nature); but if there were non-difference, origination and destruction would occur simultaneously.

children.text: bhedo 'pi tena naivaṃ cet ya ekasmin vinaśyati // Pramāṇav_3.168 //
children.translated_text: If difference too [is denied], then in that case — that which perishes in one [locus], // Pramāṇav_3.168 //

children.text: tiṣṭhatyātmā na tasyāto na syāt sāmānyabhedadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: its essence persists [in another] — therefore there could be no cognition of the universal and the particular.
Because <s>nivṛtti</s> (exclusion) has no intrinsic nature of its own, no construction of [its] having a locus or not having a locus [is needed]. // Pramāṇav_3.169 //
And [if there is] a disruption of the cognition of the universal, even by that, there is no fault,

children.text: yat tasya janakaṃ rūpaṃ tato 'nyo janakaḥ katham // Pramāṇav_3.170 //
children.translated_text: for the form that generates that [cognition] — how could something other than it be a generator? // Pramāṇav_3.170 //

children.text: bhinnā viśeṣā janakāḥ astyabhedo 'pi teṣu cet /
children.translated_text: The distinct <s>viśeṣas</s> (particulars) are the generators; if there is also non-difference in them,

children.text: tena te 'janakāḥ proktāḥ pratibhāso 'pi bhedakaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.171 //
children.translated_text: by that [non-difference] they are declared to be non-generators — and even the appearance [of universals] differentiates [things]. // Pramāṇav_3.171 //
That which partakes of nothing else is the real entity itself; the exclusions of others are its [aspects].

children.text: tat kāryakāraṇaṃ coktaṃ tat svalakṣaṇamiṣyate // Pramāṇav_3.172 //
children.translated_text: And that which is the cause of its effect is declared to be the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (unique particular) — that is what is accepted. // Pramāṇav_3.172 //
All activities of persons have as their fruit the abandonment or attainment of that [<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>].

children.text: yathā bhedāviśeṣe 'pi na sarva sarvasādhanam // Pramāṇav_3.173 //
children.translated_text: Just as, even when difference is not distinct, not everything is the means to everything, // Pramāṇav_3.173 //
so too, even when difference is not distinct, not everything is the means to everything.

children.text: bhede hi kārakaṃ kiñcid vastudharmatayā bhavet // Pramāṇav_3.174 //
children.translated_text: For in [the case of] difference, something functions as a cause by virtue of the nature of the real entity, // Pramāṇav_3.174 //
but in non-difference, the activity and non-activity of that single [entity] would be contradictory.
If there is also difference [such that] non-activity [results], then the co-operating conditions would not produce [the effect]. // Pramāṇav_3.175 //

children.text: paryāyeṇātha kartṛtvaṃ sa kiṃ tasyaiva vastunaḥ /
children.translated_text: If [they produce] alternately, then is that [alternation a property] of that very entity?

children.text: atyantabhedābhedau tu syātāṃ tadvati vastuni // Pramāṇav_3.176 //
children.translated_text: Absolute difference and non-difference would [both] exist in the entity that possesses that [universal]. // Pramāṇav_3.176 //
Or there would be a difference between those two [difference and non-difference] themselves, which have dissimilar and similar natures.

children.text: tayorapi bhaved bhedo yadi yenātmanā tayoḥ // Pramāṇav_3.177 //
children.translated_text: If there were also a difference of those two, then by what nature would there be // Pramāṇav_3.177 //
a difference [that is also] a universal? If the difference is by that very nature

children.text: bheda eva tathā ca syānniḥsāmānyaviśeṣatā // Pramāṇav_3.178 //
children.translated_text: simply difference, then there would be [entities] devoid of universal and particular. // Pramāṇav_3.178 //
Just as [there is] between difference and universal, so [there would be] among pots and so forth mutually.
Whatever nature it is, keeping which in view, this person engages [in action], // Pramāṇav_3.179 //
desiring the fruit to be accomplished by that — difference and non-difference are dependent on that.

children.text: cintyete svātmanā bhedo vyāvṛttyā ca samānatā // Pramāṇav_3.180 //
children.translated_text: By its own nature, difference is conceived; and by exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), sameness. // Pramāṇav_3.180 //
A real entity certainly exists [and] does not persist — because of the consequence regarding activity and so forth.
By this very [reasoning], whatever shameless [opponents] — some confused, unworthy [thing] — // Pramāṇav_3.181 //
babble, that too is refuted, because of the impossibility of absolute [identity].
If everything had a dual nature, the distinction of that would be negated. // Pramāṇav_3.182 //
When told 'Eat yogurt!', why does one not rush toward a camel?

children.text: athāstyatiśayaḥ kaścid yena bhedena varttate // Pramāṇav_3.183 //
children.translated_text: If there is some distinguishing feature by virtue of which difference obtains, // Pramāṇav_3.183 //

children.text: sa eva dadhi so 'nyatra nāstītyanubhayaṃ param /
children.translated_text: that alone is the yogurt; that [distinguishing feature] does not exist elsewhere — [the entity is] neither both nor supreme.

children.text: sarvātmatve ca sarveṣāṃ bhinnau syātāṃ na dhīdhvanī // Pramāṇav_3.184 //
children.translated_text: And if everything had the nature of all, cognition and words would not differ [for any pair]. // Pramāṇav_3.184 //
For the doctrine of the aggregation of differences (<s>bhedasaṃhāravāda</s>), there is the impossibility of that non-difference;
since absence has no form, and words denote [things with] form — // Pramāṇav_3.185 //
they are established without any doubt; therefore they express exclusion (<s>vyavaccheda</s>).

children.text: upādhibhedāpekṣo vā svabhāvaḥ kevalo 'tha vā // Pramāṇav_3.186 //
children.translated_text: Either the own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) depends on the distinction of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>), or [it is] bare [nature] alone — // Pramāṇav_3.186 //
it is said: the meaning is [already] established as the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) — like the properties of being an effect (<s>kāryatva</s>) and existence (<s>sattva</s>) upon destruction;

children.text: sattāsvabhāvo hetuścet sā sattā sādhyate katham // Pramāṇav_3.187 //
children.translated_text: if the reason (<s>hetu</s>) has existence (<s>sattā</s>) as its own-nature, how then is that existence to be proved? // Pramāṇav_3.187 //
For there is no positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of differences, [and this] contradicts the [relation of] reason and probandum;
but when the probandum is merely the taking up of existence (<s>bhāvopādānamātra</s>), with a universal subject (<s>sāmānyadharmin</s>) — // Pramāṇav_3.188 //

children.text: na kaścidarthaḥ siddhaḥ syādaniṣiddhaṃ ca tādṛśam /
children.translated_text: no meaning whatsoever would be established, and such [a probandum] is not [even] contested;
when the probandum involves an assumed difference, the reason would lack positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.189 //

children.text: sattāyāṃ tena sādhyāyāṃ viśeṣaḥ sādhito bhavet /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when existence (<s>sattā</s>) is the probandum, a particular (<s>viśeṣa</s>) would be proved;
but when the proof concerns mere reality (<s>vastumātra</s>), without touching upon its [specific] differences — // Pramāṇav_3.190 //
the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) of the probandum that pervades that mere [reality] is not obstructed.
There is no property of existence (<s>bhāvadharma</s>) in what is unestablished; [such a reason] depending on both [pakṣa and sapakṣa] is deviant (<s>vyabhicārin</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.191 //

children.text: dharmo viruddho 'bhāvasya sā sattā sādhyate katham /
children.translated_text: A property contradictory to absence — how can that existence (<s>sattā</s>) be proved?

children.text: siddhaḥ svabhāvo gamako vyāpakastasya niścitaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.192 //
children.translated_text: The own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) that is established [and] ascertained as pervading it is the indicator (<s>gamaka</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.192 //
The own-nature that is to be indicated (<s>gamya</s>) by this [reason], or [the reason] that effects cessation upon [the probandum's] cessation —
just as an effect (<s>kārya</s>) [proves] impermanence, or the absence of an effect [proves] the non-perishable. // Pramāṇav_3.193 //
Because destruction has no [external] cause, the invariable connection (<s>anubandha</s>) is from the own-nature [itself];
for things that depend [on conditions], necessary occurrence is not observed. // Pramāṇav_3.194 //
For even when there is abundance of its cause, there may sometimes be non-occurrence;
by this, deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is stated, due to the non-fixity of effects (<s>kāryāvyavasthiti</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.195 //
For those who maintain that destruction has a cause, [there would be required] causes of destruction for all [things];
and due to the incapacity of that cause, [destruction] occurs precisely from [the thing's] own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.196 //
Wherever indeed [an effect] arises from this [cause], elsewhere too [it arises] from [its] own-nature;
whatever inference concerns an existent entity (<s>bhāvaviṣaya</s>) — that is of two kinds only. // Pramāṇav_3.197 //
Because of the restriction of the relation of those two — by effect (<s>kārya</s>) and own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — to their respective probanda;
since engagement [in action] is preceded by cognition, when there is non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) of that [object's] existence — // Pramāṇav_3.198 //
it is said that one should not engage [in affirming its existence] — this is the validity (<s>pramāṇatā</s>) of non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>).
In the domain of [authoritative] treatises, many objects are unconnected [to perception] and supersensible (<s>atīndriya</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.199 //
And [they are] without inferential marks (<s>aliṅga</s>) — how then [can] their absence [be established] through non-apprehension?
[Objection:] its result is the ascertainment of existent and non-existent — [answer:] no, [for then] there would be invalidity [of the means of knowledge]. // Pramāṇav_3.200 //
Some [non-apprehension] may indeed be a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), being [one] that possesses a superior inferential mark (<s>liṅgātiśaya</s>).
This rule has been set forth for the non-cognition of what reveals the own-nature (<s>svabhāvajñāpaka</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.201 //
But regarding an effect (<s>kārya</s>), the non-cognition of the cause is a proof of [the cause's] very existence;
and the non-apprehension of the own-nature (<s>svabhāvānupalambha</s>) [is a proof] regarding the own-nature of the object that is the inferential mark (<s>liṅgin</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.202 //
Its absence would be cognized if by some reason [it could be established];
when it is impossible that conditions for the non-perception of a perceptible [object] obtain — // Pramāṇav_3.203 //
the absence of an existing thing that is not apprehended is cognized;

children.text: viruddhasya ca bhāvasya bhāve tadbhāvabādhanāt // Pramāṇav_3.204 //
children.translated_text: and when a contradictory entity exists, because it obstructs the existence of that [other entity] — // Pramāṇav_3.204 //
upon the apprehension of what is contradictory (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>), there would be the ascertainment of non-existence.
Established through conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>) arising from beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — // Pramāṇav_3.205 //
the meaning of a word (<s>śabdārtha</s>) [as] the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is threefold, having its basis in existence, absence, or both.
When existence is not taken up in the probandum regarding that [subject], there is its non-apprehension; // Pramāṇav_3.206 //
likewise the reason — and the absence of that [subject] is [established] through the use of words.
If words were bound exclusively to ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), // Pramāṇav_3.207 //
there could be no application [of words] to objects that differ according to other viewpoints;
nor could there be falsity of meaning in any statement regarding the past and the yet-to-be-born. // Pramāṇav_3.208 //
Therefore this [word-meaning relation] is considered to have conceptual content (<s>buddhyartha</s>) as its object.
When the probandum is the denial of word-meaning (<s>śabdārthāpahnava</s>), due to the negation of the substratum of properties — // Pramāṇav_3.209 //

children.text: na sādhyaḥ samudāyaḥ syāt siddhau dharmaśca kevalaḥ /
children.translated_text: the aggregate should not be the probandum; and upon establishment, the property alone [remains];
by those who do not deny word-meaning, through the division into the existent and non-existent positions (<s>pakṣa</s>) — // Pramāṇav_3.210 //

children.text: vastveva cityate h yatra pratibaddhaḥ phalodayaḥ /
children.translated_text: it is reality (<s>vastu</s>) alone that is cognized, where the arising of the result is invariably connected.
For that which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>), what [need is there] of examination through analyses? // Pramāṇav_3.211 //

children.text: ṣaṇḍhasya rūpe vairūpye kāminyāḥ kiṃ parīkṣayā /
children.translated_text: What [need] of examining the beauty or ugliness of a woman for a eunuch (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>)?
The meaning of a word (<s>śabdārtha</s>) is constructed as the object of conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanājñāna</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.212 //
The property (<s>dharma</s>) [has] the defect of unestablished substratum (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) in reality — thus it is stated by the <s>Naiyāyika</s>;
because there is no necessary connection (<s>āntarīyakatā</s>) of words with real things — // Pramāṇav_3.213 //
there is no establishment of meaning [directly]; for those [words] are indicators of the speaker's intention.
From the general non-deviation of the statements of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>), [verbal testimony has] the status of inference (<s>anumānatā</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.214 //
A statement that indicates a connected and suitable means [and] declares a human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>),
is [a statement] subject to examination — beyond that, [it is] not subject [to examination]. // Pramāṇav_3.215 //
Non-contradiction by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and by the two kinds of inference (<s>anumāna</s>);
non-deviation regarding its seen and unseen purposes — that is the [criterion of] non-deceptiveness regarding those meanings. // Pramāṇav_3.216 //
From the general non-deviation of the statements of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>), [there is] the status of inference;
[this] has been stated due to the lack of any other recourse for the intellect, even though [inference] is [normally] precluded in its [scripture's] domain. // Pramāṇav_3.217 //
From the establishment of the reality of what is to be abandoned and adopted (<s>heyopādeya</s>), together with its means,
through non-deviation regarding the principal meaning, [there is] inference regarding the rest as well. // Pramāṇav_3.218 //
Others understand [scripture] as veridical, dependent on a person's extraordinary [qualities] (<s>puruṣātiśaya</s>);

children.text: iṣṭo 'yamarthaḥ pratyetuṃ śakyaḥ so 'tiśayo yadi // Pramāṇav_3.219 //
children.translated_text: this meaning is accepted — [but] that extraordinary [quality] can be cognized [only] if — // Pramāṇav_3.219 //
[one can determine] 'this is thus' or 'not thus' — [whether there are] faults of the other [kind] or faultlessness;
others hold that [this is] difficult to ascertain, due to the rarity of [adequate] means of knowledge. // Pramāṇav_3.220 //
Since all [persons] have opposing tendencies (<s>savipakṣatva</s>), [the extraordinary qualities] that depend on the diminution [of faults] and increase [of virtues] —
through assimilation (<s>sātmībhāva</s>) and repeated practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of that, the impurity-free [qualities] (<s>anāsrava</s>) may be attained at some point. // Pramāṇav_3.221 //
For one whose nature has become free from affliction and beneficial, by contrary [qualities] —
there is no obstruction even with effort, due to the impartiality (<s>apakṣapāta</s>) of the intellect. // Pramāṇav_3.222 //
Of all classes of faults (<s>doṣajāti</s>), the [entire] class [arises] from the view of a [real] self-entity (<s>satkāyadarśana</s>);
that is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); therein [arises] attachment to that [self]; from that, the arising of hatred and so forth. // Pramāṇav_3.223 //
Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is stated to be the root cause of the defilements (<s>doṣa</s>) precisely for this reason;
the view of a [real] self-entity (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) [extends] to other [lives]; upon its abandonment, [all faults are] abandoned. // Pramāṇav_3.224 //
Because the faults that cause the falsity of speech are dependent on a person (<s>puruṣāśraya</s>),
some declare [the <s>Veda</s> to be] authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>) [and hence] having true meaning. // Pramāṇav_3.225 //
Since the virtues that cause the truth of speech are [also] dependent on a person,

children.text: apauruṣeyaṃ mithyārtha kiṃ netyanye pracakṣate // Pramāṇav_3.226 //
children.translated_text: why do others not declare [it to be] authorless [and hence] having false meaning? // Pramāṇav_3.226 //
For convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), which is the cause of knowledge of meaning, is dependent on a person;
even if speech were authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), therefore the possibility of falsity [remains]. // Pramāṇav_3.227 //
If the relation [between word and meaning] were authorless, there would be cognition without [prior] awareness (<s>asaṃvid</s>);
[but] a conceptual construction other [than convention] is incapable of manifesting that [relation] — [hence it is] from convention (<s>saṃketa</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.228 //
If words were restricted to a single meaning, there could be no access to other meanings;
[and] if connected with multiple meanings, there would be the occurrence of contradictory instances (<s>viruddhavyakti</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.229 //
And the postulation of authorlessness (<s>apauruṣeyatā</s>) would be pointless;
and [conventional] speech is the reason for the establishment of the relations of distinct [word-meaning pairs]. // Pramāṇav_3.230 //
Being entirely unrefinable (<s>asaṃskārya</s>) by persons, [the words] would be completely meaningless;
[and] upon admitting refinement (<s>saṃskāra</s>), this would become a principal case of 'elephant-bathing' (<s>gajasnāna</s>) [i.e., a futile effort]. // Pramāṇav_3.231 //
Because the relata are impermanent, there is no permanence in the relation;
since what is permanent cannot be benefited, and what does not act is not a basis (<s>āśraya</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.232 //
Therefore that [relation] of words with meanings is to be refined (<s>saṃskārya</s>) by persons through cognition;
[if words] arise simultaneously with [their] meanings, there is no reversal of [their] own-nature. // Pramāṇav_3.233 //

children.text: śabdeṣu yuktaḥ sambandhe nāyaṃ doṣo vikalpite /
children.translated_text: This defect is appropriate regarding [an actual] relation in words, [but] not regarding one that is conceptually constructed (<s>vikalpita</s>);
if [words were] permanent, there would be perpetual apprehension, since there could be no obstruction. // Pramāṇav_3.234 //
What capacity of a substratum [could there be] for permanent [entities]? And by what [means] is that substratum accepted?
Due to the relation of auxiliary causes (<s>sahakārin</s>) that are causes of the production of cognition — // Pramāṇav_3.235 //
origination through fitness for producing that [cognition] is accepted as manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>);
[but] those who know reasoning [reply:] in pots and the like too, [the same applies] when there is no difference for non-modifiable [entities]. // Pramāṇav_3.236 //

children.text: vyañjakaiḥ svaiḥ kṛtaḥ ko 'rtho vyaktāstaiste yato matāḥ /
children.translated_text: What purpose is served by [the entity's] own manifestors (<s>vyañjaka</s>)? For those [entities] are considered manifested by them.

children.text: sambandhasya ca vastutve syād bhedād buddhicitratā // Pramāṇav_3.237 //
children.translated_text: And if the relation were a real thing (<s>vastu</s>), there would be diversity in cognition due to [its] difference; // Pramāṇav_3.237 //
if [the relation were] non-different from those two [relata], then those two alone [would exist] — hence no other access to the real thing.
Because the nature of a real thing is distinct, the relation is a product of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.238 //

children.text: sad dravyaṃ syāt parādhīnaṃ sambandho 'nyasya vā katham /
children.translated_text: If an existent substance (<s>dravya</s>) were dependent on another, how [could there be] a relation of another [with it]?

children.text: varṇā nirarthakāḥ santaḥ padādi parikalpitam // Pramāṇav_3.239 //
children.translated_text: The phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>), being meaningless in themselves — word [units] and the like are conceptually constructed. // Pramāṇav_3.239 //
How can this relation, which is a real thing, have its locus in what is not a real thing?
Authorlessness (<s>apauruṣeyatā</s>) too is accepted [merely] because the authors are not remembered, it is said. // Pramāṇav_3.240 //
There exist transmitters (<s>anuvaktṛ</s>) of this [Veda] too — alas for this all-pervading darkness [of ignorance]!
Just as this [person], without having heard from another, [could not produce] this sequence of phonemes and words — // Pramāṇav_3.241 //
a person is [not] capable [of composing] a text [independently]; likewise, [some say,] another too [could not];

children.text: anyo vā racito granthaḥ sampradāyād ṛte paraiḥ // Pramāṇav_3.242 //
children.translated_text: or [they ask:] has any other text been composed by others without a tradition (<s>sampradāya</s>)? // Pramāṇav_3.242 //
What [text] has been seen [to be composed independently]? — stated by whom? — that one too is not inferred in this way.
Whatever is of a certain type, from whatever [source] it is established — that is no different [in kind], like fire and wood. // Pramāṇav_3.243 //
Even another [text] whose cause is unseen is understood to be of that kind [i.e., person-made];
therein, without demonstrating a difference, from the observation of the commonality of effects — // Pramāṇav_3.244 //
all those reasons that are extended [to prove authorlessness] are deviant (<s>vyabhicārin</s>).
In this way, beginninglessness (<s>anāditā</s>) would be proved [for everything] — not [just] non-dependence on a person. // Pramāṇav_3.245 //
Therefore, if authorlessness [were established], there would be another [consequence:] even what is not dependent on humans —
the speech practices of barbarians (<s>mleccha</s>) and even the words of nihilists (<s>nāstikya</s>) — // Pramāṇav_3.246 //
would have the same status due to beginninglessness, through the continuity of prior impressions (<s>pūrvasaṃskārasantati</s>).

children.text: tādṛśe 'pauruṣeyatve kaḥ siddhe 'pi guṇo bhavet // Pramāṇav_3.247 //
children.translated_text: Even if such authorlessness were established, what virtue (<s>guṇa</s>) would there be [in it]? // Pramāṇav_3.247 //
Moreover, from the observation of differences in the refinement of meanings, there is doubt;

children.text: anyāviśeṣād varṇānāṃ sādhane ki phalaṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_3.248 //
children.translated_text: given the non-difference of phonemes from others, what fruit would there be in [this] proof? // Pramāṇav_3.248 //
A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) distinct from phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) does not exist, due to non-apprehension;
when [a sentence] has the nature of multiple parts, those [parts] individually are meaningless. // Pramāṇav_3.249 //
And [attributing] that form to what does not have that form is a construction, like [the figure of] a lion and so forth;
even if each [phoneme] individually has meaning, the postulation of [their] multiplicity is false. // Pramāṇav_3.250 //
And through the cognition of a single component, comprehension of the sentence-meaning would occur;

children.text: sakṛcchrutau ca sarveṣā kālabhedo na yujyate // Pramāṇav_3.251 //
children.translated_text: and upon a single hearing, temporal difference of all [phonemes] would not be logical. // Pramāṇav_3.251 //
For even if [a word were] unitary, since sequential apprehension of what is undivided is impossible,

children.text: anityaṃ yatnasambhūtaṃ pauruṣeyaṃ kathaṃ na tat // Pramāṇav_3.252 //
children.translated_text: [words are] impermanent, produced by effort — how are they not person-made (<s>pauruṣeya</s>)? // Pramāṇav_3.252 //
If [words were] permanent, there would be perpetual apprehension, since there could be no obstruction;
[if one says] non-hearing is due to the deficiency of some auxiliary cause (<s>sahakārin</s>) — // Pramāṇav_3.253 //
granted, let [the word] depend on other [factors]; but the restriction [to particular occasions] is contradicted.
If those [auxiliary causes] did not pervade [all locations], there would be non-apprehension everywhere; // Pramāṇav_3.254 //
if they pervaded [all locations], there would be apprehension of all [words] simultaneously.
And upon the apprehension of what is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), who is the conditioner of the non-modifiable [eternal word]? // Pramāṇav_3.255 //

children.text: indriyasya syāt saṃskāraḥ śrṛṇuyānnikhilaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: The conditioning would be of the sense faculty (<s>indriya</s>) — [but then] one would hear all of that [at once];
if the restriction to a single meaning [is maintained] because of the distinctness of conditionings — // Pramāṇav_3.256 //
In a cacophony of multiple sounds, how can hearing occur?

children.text: dhvanathaḥ kevalaṃ tatra śrū yante cenna vācakāḥ // Pramāṇav_3.257 //
children.translated_text: If only <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) are heard there, then they are not <s>vācakas</s> (signifiers). // Pramāṇav_3.257 //
That there exists something distinct from <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) — this is a matter requiring much faith.

children.text: sthiteṣvanyeṣu śabdeṣu śrūyate vācakaḥ katham // Pramāṇav_3.258 //
children.translated_text: When other sounds persist, how is the <s>vācaka</s> (signifier) heard? // Pramāṇav_3.258 //
Or how could there be apprehension of distinct <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) due to a fixed capacity?

children.text: dhvanayaḥ sammatā yaiste doṣaiḥ kairapyavācakāḥ // Pramāṇav_3.259 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds) acknowledged by you — by what defects are they non-signifying? // Pramāṇav_3.259 //
Even when this <s>vācaka</s> (signifier) is being manifested by the <s>dhvanis</s> (sounds), how are they not
a sequence of phonemes (<s>varṇānupūrvī</s>) and a sentence? If not, because of the non-difference of the phonemes. // Pramāṇav_3.260 //
And there is no fixed arrangement of those, because of conflict with alternative sequences.
The absence of spatial and temporal sequence follows from the description of pervasion and eternality. // Pramāṇav_3.261 //
And when pervasion is non-eternal, the defect has already been stated previously.
Even the sequence of manifestations is not a sentence, because eternal manifestation has been refuted. // Pramāṇav_3.262 //
If that is established only through the operation of causes, then the causes have the nature of effects.
That which produces cognition of another through cognition of itself is regarded as a manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>), when the object is already established. // Pramāṇav_3.263 //

children.text: yathā dīpo 'nyathā vāpi ko viśeṣo 'sya kārakāt /
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp, or in some other way — what is the difference between this and a producer?
Since apprehension arises from the operation of the complete set of instruments. // Pramāṇav_3.264 //
And the nature of being an effect necessarily belongs to the manifester, since that is impossible otherwise.

children.text: tadrū pāvaraṇānāṃ ca vyaktiste vigamo yadi // Pramāṇav_3.265 //
children.translated_text: If the manifestation of those that obstruct its form is their removal, // Pramāṇav_3.265 //
in the absence [of obstruction], what would be the capacity of the aggregate of instruments?
From the particularity of sound, manifestation of others would also follow. // Pramāṇav_3.266 //
If such is accepted, all causes become purposeless.
That recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) is the proof, along with correct usage and so forth — such is the view. // Pramāṇav_3.267 //
This has no supporting example, since all entities are momentary (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>).
Any other fallacious reason is also to be rejected, when cognition does not depend on a person. // Pramāṇav_3.268 //
Together with what is perceived by perception that is accepted despite being contradicted, and with what is inferred,

children.text: ānupūrvyāśca varṇebhyo bhedaḥ sfoṭena cintitaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.269 //
children.translated_text: the difference of the sequence (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) from the phonemes has been conceived through <s>sphoṭa</s>. // Pramāṇav_3.269 //
That would be superimposed by conceptual construction; how could it not depend on a person?
The impermanence of <s>dhvani</s> (sound) follows from the fact that destruction is connected with mere existence. // Pramāṇav_3.270 //
If, when fire produces something else, the wood would be seen,

children.text: avināśāt sa evāsya vināśa iti cet katham // Pramāṇav_3.271 //
children.translated_text: and if it is said 'because of non-destruction, that very thing is its destruction' — how so? // Pramāṇav_3.271 //
Let the destruction of one be by another — why is the wood not seen?
If not, because of being encompassed by that — then because of that there is no obstruction. // Pramāṇav_3.272 //
The destructibility of destruction would follow, and then again from production
the wood would be seen; and upon the death of the killer, <s>Caitra</s> would not be reborn. // Pramāṇav_3.273 //
If it is said 'it is the same here too' — because the killer does not have the nature of not dying.

children.text: ananyatve vināśasya syānnāśaḥ kāṣṭhameva tu // Pramāṇav_3.274 //
children.translated_text: If destruction is non-different [from the entity], then destruction would just be the wood itself. // Pramāṇav_3.274 //
Since it is identical with that, it has no cause; there is no other possibility than this.
Even if destruction has no cause, because of the eternality of both entity and destruction, // Pramāṇav_3.275 //
there would be the absurd consequence of their coexistence — and how could what is non-existent be eternal?
If it is non-existent, the absurd consequence that the entity would not be destroyed is also untenable. // Pramāṇav_3.276 //
Because by destruction of an entity, annihilation is not intended;

children.text: naśyan bhāvo 'parāpekṣa iti tajjñāpanāya sā // Pramāṇav_3.277 //
children.translated_text: the perishing entity requires nothing else — that [statement about destruction] is for the purpose of making this known. // Pramāṇav_3.277 //
The state [of destruction] has been called the cause of this, by mentally superimposing a difference.
If this conceptual construction applies even when non-existence arises from the entity itself, then this is the same [problem]. // Pramāṇav_3.278 //

children.text: na tasya kiñcid bhavati na bhavatyeva kevalam /
children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever belongs to that [non-existent]; it simply does not exist, nothing more.

children.text: bhāve hyeṣa vikalpaḥ syād vidyervastvanuridhataḥ // Pramāṇav_3.279 //
children.translated_text: For this conceptual construction would apply to an existent; let the real thing be in accordance with itself. // Pramāṇav_3.279 //
It has been said that the entity does not come into being [as destruction]; it is not that non-existence comes into being.

children.text: apekṣyeta paraḥ kārya yadi vidyeta kiñcana // Pramāṇav_3.280 //
children.translated_text: Another [cause] would be required for an effect only if something [further] existed. // Pramāṇav_3.280 //
A thing that produces nothing — why would it be required by anything?
By this, even though [destruction] has no cause, since destruction occurs after not having existed, // Pramāṇav_3.281 //
the objection that existence would be destroyed has been refuted.

children.text: yathā keṣāñcideveṣṭaḥ pratigho janmināṃ yathā // Pramāṇav_3.282 //
children.translated_text: Just as for some, obstruction is accepted as the nature of produced things, // Pramāṇav_3.282 //
so destruction is the inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of entities — but not of those that are unproduced.
From the fixed nature of the cause, there is a fixed nature in the effect. // Pramāṇav_3.283 //
In what is non-eternal, there is no difference of form, because of the absence of differentiators.
Therefore, the eternality of the relation of these [words and meanings] is also to be rejected. // Pramāṇav_3.284 //
By the defects of the relation stated earlier, the power of words (<s>śabdaśakti</s>) has also been refuted.
Therefore, [the Veda] being <s>apauruṣeya</s> (authorless) is not a means of establishing true knowledge. // Pramāṇav_3.285 //
Fire and the like are seen to function otherwise too, uncontaminated by human fault.

children.text: na jñānahetutaiva syāt tasminnakṛtake mate // Pramāṇav_3.286 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, mere causation of knowledge would not exist if that [word] is regarded as uncreated (<s>akṛtaka</s>). // Pramāṇav_3.286 //

children.text: nityebhyo vastusāmarthyāt na hi janmāsti kasyacit /
children.translated_text: For from eternal things, no production of anything is possible due to the [fixed] capacity of real things.
Cognitions that arise from the impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of conceptual construction, having superimposed objects, // Pramāṇav_3.287 //
are produced there — they do not have real objects as their domain.
Falsity is seen only in what is created — therefore uncreated speech // Pramāṇav_3.288 //
[is true]? If because the exclusion from true objects pervades what is contradictory,
when the impossibility in the reason has not been stated, the existence of that [falsity] too may be suspected. // Pramāṇav_3.289 //
Because pervasion is seen even among contradictory things.
It has been said that non-existence is not established, because of non-apprehension in all cases. // Pramāṇav_3.290 //
When non-existence is unestablished, the negative concomitance is doubtful.

children.text: anvayo vyatireko vā sattvaṃ vā sādhyadharmiṇi // Pramāṇav_3.291 //
children.translated_text: Whether positive concomitance, negative concomitance, or existence in the subject of the proof — // Pramāṇav_3.291 //
if these are established by cognitions whose fruit is the ascertainment of those, then the proof [is valid].
Where the negative concomitance with the opposite of what is to be proved is described, // Pramāṇav_3.292 //

children.text: sa evāsya sapakṣaḥ syāt sarvo heturatonvayī /
children.translated_text: that itself would be the similar instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>); hence every reason would have positive concomitance.

children.text: samayatve hi mantrāṇāṃ kasyacit kāryasādhanam // Pramāṇav_3.293 //
children.translated_text: For if <s>mantras</s> are conventional, some [particular mantra] would be a means of producing an effect. // Pramāṇav_3.293 //
Even if there were an inherent power of entities, there would be no distinction otherwise.
And that the sequence is something different has already been refuted. // Pramāṇav_3.294 //
If that is eternal, the accomplishment of the purpose would always obtain; dependence [on conditions] would indicate incapacity.
All [mantras] would be your means of accomplishment, if the inherent power of entities is of this kind. // Pramāṇav_3.295 //
And dependence on differences of the user is not tenable for what cannot be refined.

children.text: saṃskāryasyāpi bhāvasya vastubhedo hi bhedakaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.296 //
children.translated_text: Even for an entity that can be refined, a real difference is what makes a difference. // Pramāṇav_3.296 //
The restriction in power would come from the difference of the user, not from convention.
For things upon which no qualification can be imposed, what does the user do as an impeller? // Pramāṇav_3.297 //
If usage is manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>), that has already been refuted.

children.text: vyaktiśca buddhiḥ sā yasmāt sa phalairyadi yujjate // Pramāṇav_3.298 //
children.translated_text: And manifestation is cognition; since that [cognition] — if it is connected with results, // Pramāṇav_3.298 //
the connection with the result would belong to the hearer, for the speaker is the cause of manifestation.
The purpose of the instruments that are unmanifested words, // Pramāṇav_3.299 //

children.text: manojapo vā vyarthaḥ syācchabdo hi śrotragocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: or mental recitation would be pointless, for sound is the object of the ear.

children.text: pāramparyeṇa tajjatvāt tadv yaktiḥ sāpi cenmatiḥ // Pramāṇav_3.300 //
children.translated_text: If, because of being produced from that indirectly, that manifestation too is cognition, // Pramāṇav_3.300 //
those too would be likewise; if they serve that purpose — this is unestablished, due to following from mere conceptual construction.
By the intention of regarding as one what has the nature of its own universal, // Pramāṇav_3.301 //
the statements of those who make conventions are non-contradictory — but not in reality.

children.text: ānupūrvyāmasatyāṃ syāt saro rasa iti śruto // Pramāṇav_3.302 //
children.translated_text: If the sequence (<s>ānupūrvī</s>) did not exist, 'sara' and 'rasa' would be heard [as the same]. // Pramāṇav_3.302 //

children.text: na kāryabheda iti ced asti sā puruṣāśrayā /
children.translated_text: If it is said there is no difference in effect — that [sequence] exists and depends on a person.
The sound that arises from the cognition born of the arising of a particular phoneme, // Pramāṇav_3.303 //

children.text: jāyate tadupādhiḥ sa śru tyā samavasīyate /
children.translated_text: that is its qualifying condition, and is ascertained through hearing.
One whose cognition is generated by cognition of that, who has heard with imperfect hearing — // Pramāṇav_3.304 //
relying on that memory, afterwards establishes memory in himself.
Thus this [sequence] is indeed person-dependent (<s>pauruṣeyī</s>), for those whose minds grasp its cause. // Pramāṇav_3.305 //
The causal relation among phonemes is called <s>ānupūrvī</s> (sequence).

children.text: anyadeva tato rūpaṃ tadvarṇānāṃ pade pade // Pramāṇav_3.306 //
children.translated_text: The form of those phonemes is something different in each word, // Pramāṇav_3.306 //
differing due to the maker's conditioning, and when combined, producing a difference in effect.

children.text: sā cānupūrvī varṇānāṃ pravṛttā racanākṛtaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.307 //
children.translated_text: And that sequence of phonemes has arisen from the act of composition;
because of the conflict with the established sequence of those whose desired results are contradictory. // Pramāṇav_3.307 //
Because the causal relation of the phoneme-sequence is established from persons,
every phoneme-sequence comes from persons, like the combination of fire and fuel. // Pramāṇav_3.308 //
The uncommon nature of those who produce the sequence called <s>mantra</s> is established
through the knowledge and power of [particular] persons, and through the absence of that in others. // Pramāṇav_3.309 //

children.text: ye 'pi tantravidaḥ kecid mantrān kāṃścana kuvaṃte // Pramāṇav_3.310 //
children.translated_text: Even those who are knowers of <s>tantra</s> who employ certain <s>mantras</s>, // Pramāṇav_3.310 //
their [efficacy] is the power of the Lord, operating according to the principles taught by him.

children.text: kṛtakāḥ pauruṣeyāśca mantrā vācyāḥ phalepsunā // Pramāṇav_3.311 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mantras</s> are created and person-made — this should be stated by one desiring results. // Pramāṇav_3.311 //
The proof of the incapacity of persons has been refuted by this very [argument].
As for the proof that is described regarding intellect, sense-organs, speech, persons, and so forth — // Pramāṇav_3.312 //

children.text: pramāṇābhaṃ yathārthāsti na hi śeṣavato gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: it has the semblance of a valid means of knowledge; there is a true object — for there is no access to what has a remainder.

children.text: artho 'yaṃ nāyamartho na iti śabdā vadanti na // Pramāṇav_3.313 //
children.translated_text: 'This is the meaning' or 'this is not the meaning' — words do not state. // Pramāṇav_3.313 //
The meaning must be construed by persons, and those [persons] are affected by passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like.
Among them, one knows reality and another does not — and what causes this difference? // Pramāṇav_3.314 //

children.text: tadvt puṃstve kathamapi jñānī kaścit katha na vaḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, how is it that among persons some knower [exists] and not according to you?

children.text: yasya pramāṇamavisaṃvādi vacanaṃ so 'rthavid yadi // Pramāṇav_3.315 //
children.translated_text: If one whose speech is a non-deceptive means of knowledge is a knower of objects, // Pramāṇav_3.315 //
for there is no possibility of validity regarding what is entirely beyond perception.

children.text: yasya prāmāṇasaṃvādi vacanaṃ tatkṛtaṃ vacaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.316 //
children.translated_text: One whose speech accords with valid means of knowledge — that speech is person-made. // Pramāṇav_3.316 //
That is <s>āgama</s> (authoritative tradition) — this follows; the authorlessness [of the Veda] is purposeless.
If regarding an entirely supersensible object, knowledge is not possible without <s>āgama</s>, // Pramāṇav_3.317 //
then it would follow that someone who knows supersensible objects exists.

children.text: svayaṃ rāgādimānnārtha vetti vedasya nānyataḥ // Pramāṇav_3.318 //
children.translated_text: One who himself has passion and the like does not know the meaning; nor [does he know it] from the <s>Veda</s> independently.

children.text: na vedayati vado 'pi vedārthasya kuto gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor does the <s>Veda</s> itself communicate — so whence is access to the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>? // Pramāṇav_3.318 //

children.text: tenāgnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāma iti śrutau // Pramāṇav_3.319 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) 'One who desires heaven should perform <s>agnihotra</s>' —

children.text: khādet śvamāṃsamityeṣa nārtha ityatra kā pramā /
children.translated_text: 'One should eat dog-meat' — that this is not the meaning — what is the evidence here? // Pramāṇav_3.319 //
If it is said to be well-known common speech — then who there perceives supersensible objects?
Among words with multiple meanings, who has discerned this particular meaning? // Pramāṇav_3.320 //
And words like <s>svarga</s> (heaven) and <s>vaśya</s> (subjugation) are seen to signify non-established meanings.
In other similar words, let the same kind of construction apply. // Pramāṇav_3.321 //

children.text: prasiddhiśca nṛṇāṃ vādaḥ pramāṇaṃ sa ca neṣyate // Pramāṇav_3.322 //
children.translated_text: And convention is the speech of people — and that is not accepted [as a valid means of knowledge by you].
Then how is further access to the meaning obtained? What is this desire [placed] in two positions? // Pramāṇav_3.322 //

children.text: atha prasiddhimullaṃdhya kalpane na nibandhanam // Pramāṇav_3.323 //
children.translated_text: Now, if overstepping convention there is no basis for construction,
since convention is not a valid means of knowledge, what is the basis for its acceptance? // Pramāṇav_3.323 //
The doubt in the ascertainment of word-meaning has been generated by convention itself,
since the non-occurrence of words in [only] one meaning is not seen there. // Pramāṇav_3.324 //
Because the impossibility of it being otherwise does not exist, and because sound itself has multiple capacities,
one must necessarily entertain doubt, for those who do not see a determining factor. // Pramāṇav_3.325 //

children.text: eṣa sthāṇurayaṃ mārga iti vaktīti kaścana // Pramāṇav_3.326 //
children.translated_text: Someone says 'This is a post, this is the road' — so someone [else] speaks.
Another [says] 'I myself declare' — let the difference between the two be examined. // Pramāṇav_3.326 //
Whence comes the restriction that what is applicable everywhere illuminates a single meaning? // Pramāṇav_3.327 //
Or by whom are supersensible things known, apart from the statement of intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>)?
The cause of restriction in the intention to express is convention (<s>saṃketa</s>), which reveals that [intention]. // Pramāṇav_3.328 //

children.text: apauruṣeyai sā nāsti tasya saikārthatā kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: For what is authorless (<s>apauruṣeya</s>), that [convention] does not exist — whence then its univocality?

children.text: svabhāvaniyame 'nyatra na yojyeta tayā punaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.329 //
children.translated_text: If [words] are restricted by [their own] nature, they should not be applied elsewhere; but by that [convention] again — // Pramāṇav_3.329 //

children.text: saṃketaśca nirarthaḥ syād vyaktau ca niyamaḥ kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: convention would be purposeless; and whence the restriction regarding individuals?

children.text: yatra svātantryamicchāyā niyamo nāma tatra kaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.330 //
children.translated_text: Where there is autonomy of will, what restriction can there be? // Pramāṇav_3.330 //
Therefore, convention would illuminate only the desired capacity of that [word],

children.text: yasmāt kiledṛśaṃ satyaṃ yathāgniḥ śītanodanaḥ // Pramāṇav_3.331 //
children.translated_text: because such is the truth — just as fire is what dispels cold. // Pramāṇav_3.331 //
Another [opponent] said: a sentence, being a part of the <s>Veda</s>, even another [sentence too],
like flavor — due to having the same form, like cooking in one vessel. // Pramāṇav_3.332 //
Like a remainder — due to deviation, such [reasoning] is dismissed by one who knows logic.

children.text: nityasya puṃsaḥ kartṛtvaṃ nityān bhāvānatīndriyān // Pramāṇav_3.333 //
children.translated_text: Agency of an eternal person, eternal entities beyond the senses, // Pramāṇav_3.333 //

children.text: ebnriyān viṣamaṃ hetuṃ bhāvānāṃ viṣamāṃ sthitim /
children.translated_text: sense objects, the unequal cause of entities, the unequal persistence of things,

children.text: nivṛttiṃ ca pramāṇābhyāmanyad vā vyastagocaram // Pramāṇav_3.334 //
children.translated_text: and cessation — [all of which are] beyond the scope of the two <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid cognitions), or anything else with distinct domains — // Pramāṇav_3.334 //
let him state [these] through scripture-dependent inference or otherwise,
without resolving the contradiction and without demonstrating the meaning of the treatise — // Pramāṇav_3.335 //
claiming the truth of [his] meaning, he would win a courtesan by sheer audacity.

children.text: sidhyet pramāṇaṃ yadyevam apramāṇamatheha kim // Pramāṇav_3.336 //
children.translated_text: If <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) were established thus, what then would be <s>apramāṇa</s> (invalid cognition)? // Pramāṇav_3.336 //

children.text: na hyokaṃ nāsti satyārtha puruṣe bahubhāṣīṇi /
children.translated_text: For it is not the case that there is no true meaning in a person who speaks much.

children.text: nāyaṃ svabhāvaḥ kārya vā vastūnāṃ vaktari dhvaniḥ // Pramāṇav_3.337 //
children.translated_text: But this [truth] is not the nature or the effect of things [residing] in the speaker's utterance. // Pramāṇav_3.337 //
And there is no invariable concomitance with anything distinct from that.
If [you say] the operation of signifying words is based on seeing the signified — // Pramāṇav_3.338 //
how could that [operation] apply to a single [word] which has mutually contradictory meanings?
Therefore, scriptures are not necessitated by things, nor are they indispensable for actions. // Pramāṇav_3.339 //
They are not established for the cognizer — whence then certainty about objects from them?
Therefore, even from the cessation of those, the existence or non-existence of things is not established. // Pramāṇav_3.340 //

body.translated_text: Hence, non-apprehension whose result is non-certainty is not established.

children.translated_text: Because the other is to be instructed, even what is not seen by oneself,
[if] seen by others, has [valid] proof — so some say; to refute that, a statement based on one's own perception [is given]. // Pramāṇav_4.1 //
In the domain of inference, [the authority of] words is not accepted, because one accepts what has been examined.

children.text: vācaḥ prāmāṇyamasmin hi nānumānaṃ pravartate // Pramāṇav_4.2 //
children.translated_text: For in this [domain], inference does not operate [based on words alone]. // Pramāṇav_4.2 //
Since the proof stated for the other is for the purpose of refuting scripture,
if that [scripture] is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then that [proof] is unestablished; if that [scripture] is established, then everything [follows] from it. // Pramāṇav_4.3 //

children.text: tadāgamavataḥ siddhaṃ yadi kasya ka āgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: If it is established for one who possesses scripture, then whose scripture is what?

children.text: bādhyamānaḥ pramāṇena sa siddhaḥ kathāmāgamaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.4 //
children.translated_text: That [scripture] which is contradicted by a <s>pramāṇa</s> — how is it an established scripture? // Pramāṇav_4.4 //
How could acceptance of what contradicts that be [consistent] with that very [scripture]?
If one accepts something else, the abandonment of that [scripture] would [result in] its being non-authoritative. // Pramāṇav_4.5 //
Why then is the proof not stated as that from which one's own cognition arises?

children.text: yuktyā yayāgamo grāhyaḥ parasyāpi ca sā na kim // Pramāṇav_4.6 //
children.translated_text: The reasoning by which scripture is to be accepted — does that not apply to the other [party] as well? // Pramāṇav_4.6 //
For one who is ordinary, existing prior [to instruction], the means by which the arising of cognitive perception [occurs] —
those proofs are sufficient for knowledge of the capacity of objects. // Pramāṇav_4.7 //
Even those whose [inferential] connection is broken, being beyond the scope even of generality,
there is no deliberation about proof and what is to be proved regarding those objects. // Pramāṇav_4.8 //
Due to the will of persons, in the determination of truth and untruth,
the reason and its semblance are lost, because of that [reason's] not being grounded in reality. // Pramāṇav_4.9 //
An existing object, dependent on cognition, is not a prover through cognition when non-existent.
Even for an existing thing, due to disconnection from reality, the understanding is similar [to that of a non-existent thing]. // Pramāṇav_4.10 //

children.text: liṅgaṃ svabhāvaḥ kārya vā dṛśyādarśanameva vā /
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark) is either <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature), <s>kārya</s> (effect), or non-apprehension of the perceptible.
That which is connected and established through reality — if that is unestablished, what [belongs] to itself? // Pramāṇav_4.11 //
It is improper even for the other to proceed from something else by means of what is imagined by another.
Due to the connection of the two, the <s>prasaṅga</s> (undesired consequence) [is]: when one is removed, the other is destroyed. // Pramāṇav_4.12 //
The apprehension of the meaning of that, for things whose nature is imposed through verbal conceptualization —
for the purpose of establishing their non-mark character — [is] from the establishment of one object from another object. // Pramāṇav_4.13 //
Due to the mere conformity with the wish of the maker of conceptual construction and scripture,
and due to the alteration of reality, those produced by that are deviant. // Pramāṇav_4.14 //
The capacity for proceeding from object to object [lies] in the statement of the thesis and the reason.

children.text: nārthe tena tayornāsti svataḥ sādhanasaṃsthitiḥ // Pramāṇav_4.15 //
children.translated_text: Not in the object — therefore those [thesis and reason] do not have an intrinsic establishment as proof. // Pramāṇav_4.15 //
Therefore, the statement of the thesis is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for communicating the speaker's intention.
Since doubt arises from that, it is not directly a proof. // Pramāṇav_4.16 //
Even indirectly, it is not sufficient merely by stating what is to be proved.
The statement of the reason, which indicates what is capable, is itself incapable. // Pramāṇav_4.17 //
The utterance of one incapable [of proving] is set forth as having the meaning of the reason as its object.
If even that [statement of the reason] has the capacity, since it sets in motion the statement of the reason — // Pramāṇav_4.18 //
for the inquirer, through doubt about that, there would be reliance on the context.
If the opponent accepts [the same argument], this is equally [applicable] — thus there is no stable conclusion. // Pramāṇav_4.19 //

children.text: antaraṅgaṃ tu sāmarthya triṣu rūpeṣu saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: But the intrinsic capacity, established in the three characteristics [of a valid reason],
the bringing to mind therein — that too is established in that alone. // Pramāṇav_4.20 //
For when the domain is not made known, the occurrence of the reason is impossible.

children.text: viṣayakhyāpanādeva siddhau cet tasya śaktatā // Pramāṇav_4.21 //
children.translated_text: If [the reason] is capable merely by making the domain known, then [it proves] in the establishment [itself]. // Pramāṇav_4.21 //
Even without stating this here — 'Sound is produced' — [things] of this kind,
even when stated as 'All are impermanent,' the cognition of their destruction would arise from the meaning [itself]. // Pramāṇav_4.22 //
Even when the thesis is not stated, because of the invariable connection with establishment,
the non-statement of any one of the three forms is declared as a deficiency. // Pramāṇav_4.23 //

children.text: sādhyoktiṃ vā pratijñāṃ sa vadan doṣairna yujyate /
children.translated_text: One who states the assertion (<s>pratijñā</s>), that is, the statement of what is to be proved, is not subject to faults,
because of the impossibility of pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) arising from the very undertaking of proof. // Pramāṇav_4.24 //
Even a general statement, when there is a single class, gives rise to doubt.
Otherwise, the statement of every [thing] to be proved would amount to being an assertion. // Pramāṇav_4.25 //
And since the statement of what is established serves as proof for the other party too, it is not faulty.
Now, how is the specification of what is to be proved a component of the proof? // Pramāṇav_4.26 //
The mockery of introducing and resolving [objections] together with the statement of semblances —

children.text: asambaddhā tathā hyeṣa na nyāyya iti varṇitam // Pramāṇav_4.27 //
children.translated_text: is unconnected, for thus it has been described as not logical. // Pramāṇav_4.27 //
Even though the meaning of the statement of what is to be proved is understood, a definition [is given] to prevent confusion.
That [definition] has four characteristics, [expressed] by its own words in the case of the particles and forms. // Pramāṇav_4.28 //
The acceptance of what is unestablished, what is not a proof, what is stated as the meaning, and what the proponent accepts —
even if not stated, what is pervaded by the wish [of the proponent] is considered to be proved and meaningful. // Pramāṇav_4.29 //
Even when all other accepted [positions] are removed, the prevention of grounds for doubt [remains].

children.text: vṛtto svayaṃśrutenāha kṛtā caiṣā tadarthikā // Pramāṇav_4.30 //
children.translated_text: He states through what is heard by itself as having occurred, and this [statement] is made for that purpose. // Pramāṇav_4.30 //
The specification of <s>dharma</s> (property) and <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) is stated because of their mutual dependence.

children.text: anuktāvapi vāñchāyā bhavet prakaraṇād gatiḥ // Pramāṇav_4.31 //
children.translated_text: Even when the wish is not stated, it can be understood from the context. // Pramāṇav_4.31 //
Even the absence of positive concomitance in the example is a fault of that, as stated.

children.text: ātmā paraścet so 'siddhaḥ iti tatreṣṭaghātakṛt // Pramāṇav_4.32 //
children.translated_text: If the self is the other [party's thesis], that is unestablished — thus it destroys what is accepted therein. // Pramāṇav_4.32 //

children.text: sādhanaṃ yadvivāde na nyastaṃ taccenna sādhyate /
children.translated_text: If the proof is not presented in the debate, then that is not proved.

children.text: kiṃ sādhyamanyathāniṣṭaṃ bhaved vaiphalyameva vā // Pramāṇav_4.33 //
children.translated_text: What is to be proved? Otherwise, it would be undesired, or there would be mere futility. // Pramāṇav_4.33 //
In arguments with a second [component], the faults of absence of positive concomitance and contradiction [arise].

children.text: etena kathite sādhyaṃ sāmānyenātha sammatam // Pramāṇav_4.34 //
children.translated_text: By this, what is to be proved is stated generally, or [it is] as agreed upon. // Pramāṇav_4.34 //
That very thing, due to the absence of a different meaning, is not established when the body is not obtained.
This is described as the stupidity of those who prattle without anything to say. // Pramāṇav_4.35 //
Even in destruction, if there is an imagined distinction between sound and pot,

children.text: na siddhena vināśena tadvataḥ sādhanād dhvaneḥ // Pramāṇav_4.36 //
children.translated_text: it is not [established] through proven destruction — by proving that which possesses it, from utterance. // Pramāṇav_4.36 //
Similarly, if there were a different meaning, the pot too, possessing that, would have impermanence
that is qualified and follows from utterance — if not, because of not preventing the connection. // Pramāṇav_4.37 //
For exclusion is of two kinds: through separation and through non-connection.
But in the case of exclusion where there is non-connection, what is to be prevented does not arise from non-positive-concomitance. // Pramāṇav_4.38 //
That which is to be proved is merely the universal, and there is no proving of what is [already] established.

children.text: viśiṣṭaṃ dharmiṇā tacca na niranvayadoṣavat // Pramāṇav_4.39 //
children.translated_text: That [universal], qualified by the property-bearer, is not subject to the fault of absence of positive concomitance. // Pramāṇav_4.39 //
