By this, [the view that] <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s>, each qualified by the other, [are the object of proof]
is refuted — since one who negates cannot prove in the <s>dharmin</s> alone by this means. // Pramāṇav_4.40 //
For the exclusion of the aggregate is not contradicted in the <s>dharmin</s>.

children.text: sādhyaṃ yatastathā neṣṭaṃ sādhyo dharmo 'tra kevalaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.41 //
children.translated_text: Since what is to be proved is as stated, the <s>dharma</s> (property) alone is what is to be proved here. // Pramāṇav_4.41 //
Even when a single <s>dharmin</s> has various <s>dharmas</s> established in the treatise,
what is to be proved would be just what is accepted by itself — thus the expression 'by itself' is adopted. // Pramāṇav_4.42 //
From the very acceptance of the treatise, since everything is accepted, in refutation —

children.text: tatraikasyāpi doṣaḥ syād yadi hetupratijñyoḥ // Pramāṇav_4.43 //
children.translated_text: there would be a fault even of one [dharma], if in the reason and the assertion [there is inconsistency]. // Pramāṇav_4.43 //
If the non-destruction of sound is to be proved, from the damage to the property of odor being an attribute of earth,
the reason would be contradicted and irrelevant — if not, then the same [fault] applies elsewhere. // Pramāṇav_4.44 //
If the <s>dharmin</s> here is the one under discussion, there would be contradiction of the meaning of the treatise.
Or if one were to state that it is what the proponent accepts, through means of proving <s>dharmin</s>, <s>dharma</s>, and so on — // Pramāṇav_4.45 //

children.text: kaiścit prakaraṇairiccha bhavet sā gamyate ca taiḥ /
children.translated_text: the wish would arise from certain contexts, and it is understood through those.
To forcibly [say] 'this is your wish' — that is clearly the play of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). // Pramāṇav_4.46 //
One who states that [wish] as not having action as its mark is refuted by deviation.

children.text: anāntarīyake cārthe bādhite 'nyasya kā kṣati // Pramāṇav_4.47 //
children.translated_text: And when what is necessary is refuted, what harm is there to something else? // Pramāṇav_4.47 //
And it has been said that inference does not depend on scripture in its own domain.

children.text: siddhaṃ tena susiddhaṃ tanna tadā śāstramīkṣyate // Pramāṇav_4.48 //
children.translated_text: What is well-established through that [inference] — at that time, scripture is not looked to. // Pramāṇav_4.48 //
If there were then abandonment of debate — no, because at that time there is no means [available from debate].

children.text: upāyo hyabhyupāye 'yamanaṅgaṃ sa tadāpi san // Pramāṇav_4.49 //
children.translated_text: For this [scripture] is a means when there is a means [to be employed], and even being a non-component, it still [exists] at that time. // Pramāṇav_4.49 //
At that time, when both domains are purified, the acceptance of scripture

children.text: cikirṣoḥ sa hi kālaḥ syāt tadā śāstreṇa bādhanam // Pramāṇav_4.50 //
children.translated_text: by one who wishes to act — that is the [proper] time; then [there can be] refutation through scripture. // Pramāṇav_4.50 //
Due to the incompatibility of deliberation with that, and the inapplicability to objects established by that —
when one moves to the third position, the acceptance of scripture is proper. // Pramāṇav_4.51 //
Even there, the necessary refutation of the property to be proved
is to be avoided, and [the refutation] of others too, due to the consequence of infinite regress. // Pramāṇav_4.52 //
By what [authority] is there this rule in all deliberations that scripture must be accepted?
If [one says] 'fire should now be grasped not by smoke but by doctrines' — // Pramāṇav_4.53 //
for a being born empty, not seeing merits and faults,
alas, by whom were obtained these uneven houses of doctrine! // Pramāṇav_4.54 //
If, in the case of a proof in one [instance], all scripture in the example

children.text: darśayet sādhanaṃ syādityeṣā lokottarā sthitiḥ // Pramāṇav_4.55 //
children.translated_text: were to show [it], that would be a proof — this is a supramundane position. // Pramāṇav_4.55 //
For an unconnected property, does not an unestablished [reason] fail to establish?
A reason stated for establishing that — does a faulty one succeed there? // Pramāṇav_4.56 //
Without even bringing the property into the example, all [properties] of the <s>dharmin</s> —
speech and what is born from smoke and the like follow consciousness, fire, and so on. // Pramāṇav_4.57 //
One who proves the <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) and cause of an object through deviation
does not desist from [his] own nature in the refutation of someone's argument. // Pramāṇav_4.58 //
And one who resorts to another [position], what is not necessary, with desired
objects to be proved — how is he not instructed by that reason? // Pramāṇav_4.59 //

body.translated_text: Whether stated or not stated [in scripture], how then is it not established? // Pramāṇav_4.59 //

children.translated_text: Whether the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is stated or not stated, what objection does the opponent have here?

children.text: na hi tasyoktidoṣeṇa sa jātaḥ śāstrabādhanaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.60 //
children.translated_text: For it does not become a refutation of scripture merely due to the fault of his statement. // Pramāṇav_4.60 //
If there is a fault because one states that which refutes — if he would not state it,

children.text: kinna bādheta so 'kurvannayuktaṃ kena duṣyati // Pramāṇav_4.61 //
children.translated_text: would it then not refute? One who refrains from acting is not at fault for what reason? // Pramāṇav_4.61 //
In the case of other <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (pseudo-reasons), since one's own desired [thesis] is simply not established,

children.text: duṣyed vyarthābhidhānena nātra tasya prasādhanāt // Pramāṇav_4.62 //
children.translated_text: one would be at fault through a purposeless statement; but here, since that [thesis] is established, [there is no such fault]. // Pramāṇav_4.62 //
If something somewhere is prohibited by scripture as being reasonable,
one who states 'this other thing too is reasonable' — this is the way of the royal court. // Pramāṇav_4.63 //

children.text: sarvānarthān samīkṛtya vaktuṃ śakyaṃ na sādhanam /
children.translated_text: Having equated all disadvantages, one cannot state the means of proof;
thereby the entire framework of <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and <s>sādhana</s> (probans) would be destroyed everywhere. // Pramāṇav_4.64 //
Let refutation be due to the impossibility of contradictories [applying] to a single <s>dharmin</s> (subject);
where there is exclusive contradiction, the opposition is not like that here. // Pramāṇav_4.65 //
Even if there is [alleged] capacity to refute the irrefutable, since the meaning of scripture would be overturned thereby,

children.text: asabhbadde 'pi bādhā cet syāt sarva sarvabādhanam // Pramāṇav_4.66 //
children.translated_text: if refutation could apply even to what is unconnected, then everything would refute everything. // Pramāṇav_4.66 //
If there is a connection [between reason and refutation] only there where refutation occurs, and if not,

children.text: hetoḥ sarvasya cintyatvāt svasādhye guṇadoṣayoḥ // Pramāṇav_4.67 //
children.translated_text: then since every reason's merits and faults with respect to its own <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) must be examined — // Pramāṇav_4.67 //
the invariable connection with the <s>sādhya</s> is the relation, and that is not seen here;

children.text: kevalaṃ śāstrapīḍeti doṣaḥ sānyakṛte samā // Pramāṇav_4.68 //
children.translated_text: the fault is merely 'harm to scripture,' and that is the same [fault] produced by any other [reason]. // Pramāṇav_4.68 //
If the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is to be proved from acceptance of scripture, and if all is seen [only] in scripture,
then the absurd consequence follows that the thesis, established example, and reason are [all merely] statements [of scripture]. // Pramāṇav_4.69 //
If [one says] those two are not [accepted] as means of proof — then, from the standpoint of the desired doctrine,

children.text: nyāyaprāptaṃ na sādhyatvaṃ vacanād vinivarttate // Pramāṇav_4.70 //
children.translated_text: the status of being <s>sādhya</s> (provable), which is obtained by logical procedure, is not averted merely by verbal declaration. // Pramāṇav_4.70 //
If what is not desired [by the proponent] is not a <s>sādhya</s> — then another property not desired by the proponent
is also not a <s>sādhya</s>; in that case, how is what refutes the non-<s>sādhya</s> contradictory? // Pramāṇav_4.71 //
The word 'svayam' (by oneself) is also meaningless if the intended meaning falls outside the definition of <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis);
if in the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) it serves the purpose of volitional engagement, then from where does this doubt arise? // Pramāṇav_4.72 //
That which is not prohibited by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) — by what is one prevented from accepting it?

children.text: niṣiddhaścet pramāṇena vācā kena pravartyate // Pramāṇav_4.73 //
children.translated_text: And if it is prohibited by <s>pramāṇa</s>, by what speech is it made operative? // Pramāṇav_4.73 //
Previously too, this [proponent] accepted a <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) by his own will alone;

children.text: kiñcidanyaṃ satu punargrahītuṃ labhate na kim // Pramāṇav_4.74 //
children.translated_text: why then can he not accept something else again? // Pramāṇav_4.74 //
Seeing the conflicting views here, he composed his own treatise,
showing the unimpairedness of the desired [position], the non-provability [of the opponent's], and the infinite regress. // Pramāṇav_4.75 //
Another [teacher] stated his own treatise for the purpose of accepting
the well-known <s>dharmin</s> (subject) by excluding the distinctions introduced by convention. // Pramāṇav_4.76 //
The well-known [subject], being established, is the locus [of debate] precisely from the context of investigation,
since there is no dispute regarding objects whose distinctions are fabricated by one's own will. // Pramāṇav_4.77 //
Then he stated the non-provability of the <s>dharmin</s> with respect to the established aspect,

children.text: svarūpeṇaiva nirdeśya ityanenaiva tad gatam // Pramāṇav_4.78 //
children.translated_text: [saying] 'it should be indicated by its own nature' — by this very [statement] that [point] is conveyed. // Pramāṇav_4.78 //
For when it is possible to indicate [the <s>dharmin</s>] in the form of an established proof,

children.text: sādhyatvenaiva nirdeśya itīdaṃ phalavad bhavet // Pramāṇav_4.79 //
children.translated_text: [the instruction] 'it should be indicated as the <s>sādhya</s>' would then bear fruit. // Pramāṇav_4.79 //
The fact that <s>anumāna</s> (inference) has universals as its object has also been described

children.text: ihaivaṃ na hyanukte 'pi kiñcit pakṣe virudhyate // Pramāṇav_4.80 //
children.translated_text: in this very [context]; for even if not stated, nothing is contradicted in the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis). // Pramāṇav_4.80 //

children.text: kuryācced dharmiṇaṃ sādhyaṃ tataḥ kiṃ tanna śaktyate /
children.translated_text: If one were to make the <s>dharmin</s> (subject) itself the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), what would follow? It cannot be done —
why? Because of the absence of the <s>hetu</s>'s (reason's) positive concomitance; and there is no fault in those two either. // Pramāṇav_4.81 //
A fault that depends on the other stated members [of the proof] is not considered a fault of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis);
otherwise, faults of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) and so forth would also absurdly become faults of the <s>pakṣa</s>. // Pramāṇav_4.82 //
Since all [such faults] would refute the <s>pakṣa</s>, therefore only those attached to the <s>pakṣa</s> alone
are considered <s>pakṣadoṣas</s> (faults of the thesis), not others — like contradiction with <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the like. // Pramāṇav_4.83 //
Setting aside what is to be addressed by the definitions of <s>hetu</s> (reason) and so forth, the definition of <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis)
is stated for the purpose of excluding under-extension and negative concomitance. // Pramāṇav_4.84 //
The terms 'svayam' (by oneself), 'nipāta' (particle), 'rūpa' (form), and 'ākhyā' (designation) exclude negative concomitance,
while the mention of 'iṣṭa' (desired) together with the unexcluded [elements] excludes under-extension. // Pramāṇav_4.85 //
The acceptance of the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is the definition of <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis); in those [cases], non-thesis status [obtains]:
in the excluded [case], through refutation; in the remainder, through non-conformity with the definition. // Pramāṇav_4.86 //
Even when the purpose is already conveyed by the expression 'desired by oneself,' the additional specification
is stated through connection with the verbal suffix [-tavya] to cut off [objections arising at] another time. // Pramāṇav_4.87 //
Here, the desire that is not a component [of the proof] reaches completion; but again, in the word 'desired,'
it is indeed a component, and by that, unestablished <s>hetu</s> (reason) and the like are excluded. // Pramāṇav_4.88 //
And since [mere words] are non-expressive, [what is] desired by oneself through oneself is inappropriate;
without depending on any scripture, the provability belongs to what is asserted by that proponent. // Pramāṇav_4.89 //
Therefore, even when what is mixed with the undesired is [claimed to be] accepted, in refuting it,
since the non-<s>sādhya</s> (non-probandum) is not refuted, the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) and <s>hetu</s> (reason) are not vitiated. // Pramāṇav_4.90 //
And that acceptance which is not prohibited by the two <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid cognitions) is acknowledged;
when there is doubt, by the statement of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) — [but] the reversed [acceptance] has no basis in the <s>hetu</s>. // Pramāṇav_4.91 //
Through the division of <s>anumāna</s> (inference), that refutation is stated as fourfold;
among these, the [scriptural] acceptance is a component of the effect[-based reason], and the nature of the world is a component of the <s>svabhāva</s>-[reason]. // Pramāṇav_4.92 //
An <s>āpta</s> (authoritative person) is one whose speech is consistent with the ascertainment of reality, who is devoted to non-contradiction of the self;

children.text: āptaḥ svavacanaṃ śastraṃ caikamuktaṃ samatvataḥ // Pramāṇav_4.93 //
children.translated_text: his own statement is the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) — and both are stated as one, due to their equivalence. // Pramāṇav_4.93 //
Just as, when one's own self lacks authority, one's statement does not function [as proof],
so too there is no investigation regarding a matter already established by scripture, nor regarding what does not depend on it. // Pramāṇav_4.94 //
For if [the investigation] depends on the occasion of that [scripture], then 'scripture is the refuter' —
to state this purpose, his own words are cited together, to show the equivalence. // Pramāṇav_4.95 //
The example too is described here as analogous to that,
for in the absence of <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid cognitions), the words of scripture are inapplicable. // Pramāṇav_4.96 //
In <s>āgama</s> (scripture), the clear example is the contradiction with one's own words;
a mere indication of direction there: <s>adharma</s> (demerit) is the root, <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the like, and bathing destroys <s>adharma</s>. // Pramāṇav_4.97 //
But when the author of the <s>śāstra</s> makes a contradictory statement regarding an object that is not the referent of that [scripture],

children.text: na bādhā pratibandhaḥ syāt tulyakakṣatayā tayoḥ // Pramāṇav_4.98 //
children.translated_text: there is no refutation; the necessary connection would require them to be of equal status. // Pramāṇav_4.98 //
Just as [the contradiction applies] with respect to one's own words, so too that [scripture] is then of the nature of his own statement;

children.text: tayoḥ pramāṇaṃ yasyāsti tat syādanyasya bādhakam // Pramāṇav_4.99 //
children.translated_text: whoever possesses a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) for those two — that would be the refuter of the other. // Pramāṇav_4.99 //
Whether [one refutes] the thesis or the inference, [whether by] reasoning devoid of thesis,
or in accordance with reality — how could it refute otherwise? // Pramāṇav_4.100 //
The authoritativeness of <s>āgamas</s> (scriptures) has been refuted already earlier;
therefore, in the investigation of [scriptural] acceptance, this fault is acknowledged. // Pramāṇav_4.101 //
Therefore, to show the difference of domain, [scriptural] acceptance is treated separately,
even though it falls outside <s>anumāna</s> (inference), because of its capacity to refute. // Pramāṇav_4.102 //
Otherwise there would be over-extension, or the separate treatment would be purposeless;
the distinction lies in mere verbal statement, [yet] the necessary connection [applies] even with one's own words. // Pramāṇav_4.103 //
Therefore, from [scriptural] acceptance, if scripture were a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) regarding all objects

children.text: bādhakam yadi necchet sa bādhakaṃ kiṃ punarbhavet // Pramāṇav_4.104 //
children.translated_text: and a refuter — if one does not accept that, what then could be a refuter? // Pramāṇav_4.104 //
There would be no difference between contradiction with one's own words and contradiction between one's own words and scripture;
and the authoritativeness of this [scripture] is fully constituted by human will. // Pramāṇav_4.105 //
Therefore, regarding well-known matters, even the abandonment of scripture causes no harm;
regarding imperceptible matters, where <s>āgama</s> (scripture) is not accepted, no investigation proceeds at all. // Pramāṇav_4.106 //
The examination here too is mostly the bringing out of contradiction; for instance:
<s>rāga</s> (passion) and the like are the root of <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and bathing destroys <s>adharma</s>. // Pramāṇav_4.107 //

children.text: śāstraṃ yatsiddhayā yuktyā svavācā ca na bādhyate /
children.translated_text: A <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) that is not refuted by established reasoning or by one's own words,
whether regarding the seen or the unseen, should be accepted — thus the investigation proceeds. // Pramāṇav_4.108 //
Since [the thesis] is not prohibited regarding [those] objects, and since it follows the will of the person,
an <s>āpta</s> (authoritative person) here is one whose speech is unimpaired, [speaking of] what is denoted by the word 'iṣṭa' (desired). // Pramāṇav_4.109 //
<s>Dharma</s> (duty/virtue) is stated by a well-known word; the conventional usage arising from that,
the <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid cognitions) delimited by <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the rest, are indicated by the attribution of [the term] 'śruti' (scripture). // Pramāṇav_4.110 //
For those [words] that arise dependent on that [convention], which do not prohibit due to conformity with volition,

children.text: kṛtānāmakṛtānāṃ ca yogyaṃ viśvaṃ svabhāvataḥ // Pramāṇav_4.111 //
children.translated_text: the entire [range of] objects is suitable by nature, whether [the words are] coined or uncreated. // Pramāṇav_4.111 //
By [a cognition] that conforms only to the object, whether future or past,
that which obstructs is refuted through the fitness of words thereby. // Pramāṇav_4.112 //
By the force of that fitness alone, a word connected with a real thing —
even when that [particular object] is not cognized, all of it [is established] in that [word]; hence its establishment follows from that. // Pramāṇav_4.113 //
<s>Asādhāraṇatā</s> (uncommon nature) would not obtain here for the refuting reason; otherwise,
the negation of that would follow from inference, since [the reason] does not operate in the meaning of the word [alone]. // Pramāṇav_4.114 //
<s>Asādhāraṇatā</s> (uncommon nature) of reasons [obtains] there where there is no positive concomitance;
the example 'being existent' — how is it considered [a valid] reason in this way? // Pramāṇav_4.115 //
Words depend on <s>saṃketa</s> (convention), and that [convention] depends on mere volition;
there is no non-establishment of what is established by words — thus speaks the doctrine of verbal establishment. // Pramāṇav_4.116 //
Among things established by inference, [this] shows the absence of contradictory and non-deviating [reasons];
thus, [verbal cognitions] would be understood from the standpoint of inference. // Pramāṇav_4.117 //

children.text: atha vā bru vato lokasyānumābhāva ucyate /
children.translated_text: Or else, the absence of inference is stated for the world that speaks;
what of it? The cognition from inference has a different domain. // Pramāṇav_4.118 //
Therefore, [it is] indicated that the operation of [verbal cognition], which is different from inference regarding the existence and non-existence of things,
and which conforms to them, is not under inference's control but arises from volition. // Pramāṇav_4.119 //

children.text: candratāṃ śaśino 'nicchan kāṃ pratītiṃ sa vāñchati /
children.translated_text: One who does not accept the moonness of the moon — what cognition does he desire?

children.text: iti taṃ pratyadṛṣṭāntaṃ tadasādhāraṇaṃ matam // Pramāṇav_4.120 //
children.translated_text: Thus, with respect to him, the example is not seen; that is considered <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon). // Pramāṇav_4.120 //
This is not stated with reference to just one example;

children.text: lakṣaṇatvāt tathā vṛkṣo dhātrītyuktau ca bādhanāt // Pramāṇav_4.121 //
children.translated_text: because it is a definition, [it applies generally] — just as when one says 'a tree is <s>dhātrī</s> (myrobalan),' there is refutation. // Pramāṇav_4.121 //
Here too, since it is observed in the world — in the case of camphor, silver, and the like —
that which operates by convention — what uncommonness could there be? // Pramāṇav_4.122 //

children.text: yadi tasya kvacit sidhyet siddhaṃ vastubalena tat /
children.translated_text: If that [word-meaning relation] were established somewhere, it would be established by the force of the real thing;
if one accepts establishment through cognition, then even regarding the moon there would be no prevention. // Pramāṇav_4.123 //
For that which is established in a real thing, there is no prevention even in [the case of] the moon;

children.text: tadvastvabhāve śaśini vāraṇe 'pi na duṣyati // Pramāṇav_4.124 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of that real thing, even with prevention regarding the moon, there is no fault. // Pramāṇav_4.124 //
Therefore, the objects of <s>dharmas</s> (properties) that arise by the force of convention not restricted to real things
are suitable, since volition is not constrained. // Pramāṇav_4.125 //
That which obstructs that fitness — the inference operating in the domain of fitness,
arising from the non-prohibition of convention, repels [the obstruction] — this is called <s>pratīti</s> (cognition). // Pramāṇav_4.126 //
This is the measure of the meaning of words that follow convention;
'not so' — by this it is stated that the prohibition of these [words' meanings] is contradictory. // Pramāṇav_4.127 //
Whether [one obstructs] the meaning of a <s>śruti</s> (scripture) that is occasioned, or the ultimate meaning
of words — one who obstructs is described as not worthy of refutation. // Pramāṇav_4.128 //
Therefore, to show the difference of domain, <s>pratīti</s> (verbal cognition) is treated separately,
even though it falls outside <s>anumāna</s> (inference), just as before. // Pramāṇav_4.129 //
Showing the purpose of stating the two established [types] separately,
he stated that these, together with their reasons, are not refutations by inference or perception. // Pramāṇav_4.130 //
Here too, in the case of refutation by perception, due to the manifold nature of sound,

children.text: prasiddhasya śrutau rūpaṃ yadeva pratibhāsate // Pramāṇav_4.131 //
children.translated_text: whatever form of the well-known [object] appears in verbal testimony — // Pramāṇav_4.131 //
is non-dual, since the variegated appearance is not perceived, [it] being born of cognition.
The statement of the meaning of that [thesis] itself [constitutes] refutation by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) when [the property] is rejected. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.132 //
That very form is the meaning there; the rest has the character of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>),
the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), being not a real entity, is therefore not an object of perception (<s>akṣa</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.133 //
Therefore, since the imperceptibility of properties that are universals is established,
even in rejection there is no refutation (<s>bādhā</s>) — this is made clear by the verbal statement (<s>śrāvaṇa</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.134 //
Because [the universal] is in every way inexpressible in its nature, and because its establishment depends on [verbal convention],
the object of perception is stated by verbal [testimony] through the force of that refutation. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.135 //
In every case, the property (<s>dharma</s>) which the proponent desires as what is to be proven (<s>sādhya</s>) —
refutation should be with respect to that which possesses that property, not with respect to the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) through a different property. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.136 //
Otherwise, what obstruction is there for him when the <s>dharmin</s> is refuted with respect to something else?
Since the matter is already settled by the definition, the mention of one's own <s>dharmin</s> again in this [context] // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.137 //
would serve to establish that even refutation of the <s>dharmin</s> constitutes refutation [of the thesis],
because through the contradiction of the substratum (<s>āśraya</s>), that which depends on it is [also] contradicted. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.138 //
Otherwise, from the statement that 'a property of this kind is to be proven,'
one would consider the refutation of that alone [sufficient] — hence the specification of one's own <s>dharmin</s>. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.139 //
Objection: This too is established by the meaning [itself]. True, but some [thinkers]
have accepted it as maximally defective even when only the <s>dharmin</s> alone is obstructed. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.140 //
For example, when others state: 'Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) and the like, having an unprecedented nature not produced [by anything else],
are not causes of sound and so forth, because [they produce] only once' — the objector responds: // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.141 //
'Likewise, the <s>dharmin</s>, being not a real entity by its own nature, is space (<s>vyoman</s>) and the like' — even so,

children.text: naivamiṣṭasya sādhyasya bādhā kācana vidyate // Pramāṇav_4.142 //
children.translated_text: there is no refutation whatsoever of the desired <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proven). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.142 //
For even when both [<s>dharmin</s> and <s>dharma</s>] are to be proven, that which obstructs the property to be proven
constitutes refutation — the refutation of the <s>dharmin</s> in that case is described by this [principle]. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.143 //
Likewise here, since the <s>dharmin</s> too is to be proven, [the refutation] does not apply to it alone;
if it were so, then there would be refutation here — [but] the one that is not produced by another has no [separate] capacity. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.144 //
Because [it produces] sound and so forth only once, [it follows that] pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like [are the same] as before;
there would be contradiction here only if the reason (<s>hetu</s>) were absolutely conclusive (<s>aikāntika</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.145 //
Because there is no contradiction between sequential action and permanence, [and] because of exclusion from the dissimilar class (<s>vipakṣa</s>),

children.text: vyāvṛtteḥ saṃśayānnāyaṃ śeṣavad bheda iṣyate // Pramāṇav_4.146 //
children.translated_text: due to doubt, this is not accepted as a difference like the remainder. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.146 //
Since the property (<s>dharma</s>) is desired by oneself as what is to be proven, therefore its substratum

children.text: bādhyo na kevalo nānyasaṃśrayo veti sūcitam // Pramāṇav_4.147 //
children.translated_text: is what is to be refuted — not [the <s>dharmin</s>] alone, nor one dependent on another — thus it is indicated. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.147 //
By verbal [testimony] itself, the refutation of properties belonging to another is called 'refutation' (<s>bādhā</s>);
likewise, [refutation] of another's <s>dharmin</s> by one's own <s>dharmin</s> is also so called. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.148 //
Through a defect in any part of the proof, it is the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) itself that is obstructed;
even so, [it counts as] a thesis-defect (<s>pakṣadoṣa</s>), since it pertains to the assertion (<s>pratijñā</s>) alone. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.149 //
The defect that depends on the subsequent members [of the proof] is connected [to the thesis]
by that [reasoning] — hence it is said that thesis-defects include unestablished substratum (<s>asiddhāśraya</s>) and the like. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.150 //
The refutation of the specific [forms of] <s>dharmin</s> and <s>dharma</s>, and of the intrinsic nature of the <s>dharmin</s>,
as components of what is to be proven — this is demonstrated by this very [principle]. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.151 //
Here, only the direction of illustration is stated for the sake of seeing the meaning:
there is another object, endowed with the definition of substance (<s>dravya</s>), that is perceptible in conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.152 //
The assertion of a qualified [entity] that is imperceptible is purposeless,
for the whole (<s>avayavī</s>) is desired [to be proven] as an effect, [but] it is impossible in imperceptible [things]. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.153 //

body.translated_text: And in proving another [entity] that is unqualified, [the proof] establishes what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

body.text: gurutvādhogatī syātāṃ yadyasya syāt tulānatiḥ // Pramāṇav_4.154 //
body.translated_text: If heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) and downward motion (<s>adhogati</s>) belonged to it, there would be a tilting of the balance. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.154 //

children.translated_text: That [whole], being devoid of qualities and action, is therefore not an inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>);

children.text: tata eva na dṛśyo 'sāvadṛṣṭeḥ kāryarūpayoḥ // Pramāṇav_4.155 //
children.translated_text: for that very reason it is not perceptible, since its effects and forms are unseen. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.155 //
The refutation of that [applies] to another unqualified [entity] that necessarily exists,
like the fall of a ray [of light], due to the weighability of [even] a chain of substances down to the subtlest. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.156 //
Another said: heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) as a separate substance has no movement,

children.text: tasya krameṇaṃ saṃyukte pāṃśurāśau sakṛd yute // Pramāṇav_4.157 //
children.translated_text: because when it [heaviness] gradually conjoins with a heap of dust that is combined all at once, // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.157 //

children.text: bhedaḥ syād gaurave tasmāt pṛthak saha ca tolite /
children.translated_text: there would be a difference in heaviness when weighed separately and together;
therefore the equality in count of gold <s>māṣaka</s>s and the like would not be possible. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.158 //
If, from mustard seeds up to a great heap, heaviness increases progressively
in the chain of effects, then it is simply not perceived. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.159 //
But the heaviness down to the mustard seed, though difficult to discern, is not negligible;
it is weighable, and that is its cause — because the heaviness of the effect is not perceived [separately]. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.160 //
Objection: Like an unseen ray, that object [exists but] its effect is not observed —
like heaviness without movement — because none of its qualities are perceived. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.161 //
The non-excess of <s>māṣaka</s>s and the like, and the non-tilting [of the balance], are perceptible indicators,
just as when form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like, whether greater or lesser, are not seen by their respective senses. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.162 //
The method [of dealing with] the refutation of one's own words and the like is through [showing its] possibility;
the example too, along with the indicated direction, is understood from the [preceding] statement. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.163 //
But because actions pertain to all three times, [the thesis] is not of that nature;

children.text: tathā paraṃ prati nyastaṃ sādhyaṃ neṣṭaṃ tadāpi tat // Pramāṇav_4.164 //
children.translated_text: likewise, what is to be proven, being presented to the opponent, is not accepted — yet even so, that [stands]. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.164 //
However, in the domain of cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>), the statement of what is to be proven
obstructs all [cases of] unestablished [elements], since it does not depend on an undesired particular. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.165 //
Therefore, the example of an unestablished instance (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) and reason (<s>hetu</s>) is given;
otherwise, even in the case of a hare's horn (<s>śaśaśṛṅga</s>) and the like, there would be provability even when everything is unestablished. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.166 //

children.text: sarvasya cāprasiddhatvāt kathañcit tena na kṣamāḥ /
children.translated_text: And since everything would be unestablished, they are in no way adequate for that [purpose],
in the examination of the introduction and resolution of distinctions such as action (<s>karman</s>) and the like. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.167 //
It is wrong [to say] that the component [of the proof] is to be proven because its nature is previously unestablished,

children.text: tulyā siddhāntatā te hi yenopagamalakṣaṇāḥ // Pramāṇav_4.168 //
children.translated_text: for your [position] equally has the character of an accepted conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), being defined by [mere] acceptance. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.168 //
Even when the aggregate is to be proven, the mutual qualification
of each [part] is to be proven — [and] those two, characterized as reason (<s>hetu</s>) and example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), are [then] unestablished. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.169 //
If, due to impossibility, the word '<s>sādhya</s>' (to be proven) is taken as applying to the <s>dharmin</s>,

children.text: śāstreṇālaṃ yathāyogaṃ loka eva pravarttatām // Pramāṇav_4.170 //
children.translated_text: then enough with the treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) — let ordinary usage (<s>loka</s>) prevail as appropriate. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.170 //
From the capacity of stating the proof, provability is understood with respect to that meaning;
and proof through statements of the reason (<s>hetu</s>) and the like, [established] through <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), cannot be doubted. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.171 //
By that prior determination, the description of the definition of the thesis (<s>pratijñālakṣaṇa</s>)

children.text: byarthā vyaptiphalā soktiḥ sāmarthyād gamyate tataḥ // Pramāṇav_4.172 //
children.translated_text: is superfluous — that statement, whose fruit is <s>vyāpti</s>, is understood from [its own] capacity. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.172 //
Contradiction with the desired [thesis], disconnection, unhelpfulness, and co-existence [with the opposite] —
thus, all defects of [any] member [of the proof] become thesis-defects (<s>pratijñādoṣa</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.173 //
And it has been demonstrated that thesis-defects are not dependent on [anything] external;
that which is desired, impossible, and unestablished — that very [thesis] is refuted. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.174 //
One should state thus regarding sound, that it has impermanence and a cause:
apart from the statement of the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), what other demonstration of the meaning exists here? // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.175 //
Having stated [things] differing by particulars, in the continuation of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>),

children.text: na tadvyāptiḥ phalaṃ vā kiṃ sāmānyenānuvartane // Pramāṇav_4.176 //
children.translated_text: is not <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) the result? Or what [would be the result] in the continuation of the universal? // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.176 //
Refutation with respect to sound would [come] just by standing [on the established principle] — hence he said:
'One speaking about a different, contradictory subject does not [thereby] state the otherness of what is heard.' // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.177 //

children.text: sa ca bhedāpratikṣepāt sāmānyānāṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And that [refutation] does not exist for universals, because difference is not rejected [among them],

children.text: vṛkṣo na śiṃśapaiveti yathā prakaraṇe kvacit // Pramāṇav_4.178 //
children.translated_text: just as [one says] 'a tree is not just a <s>śiṃśapā</s>' in a certain context. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.178 //
The prohibition of a single occurrence of every [universal] statement would not [yield] certainty,
because that is impossible when all differences are not of that nature. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.179 //
Because of the difference between what is to be known (<s>jñāpya</s>) and the knower (<s>jñāpaka</s>), the <s>dharmin</s> having the nature of a reason (<s>hetu</s>) —
being unestablished as an informer — is [declared] 'unestablished <s>dharmin</s>' (<s>dharmyasiddha</s>) in one's own proof. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.180 //
Since the distinction between <s>dharma</s> and <s>dharmin</s> is unestablished in all entities,
if the defect is equal everywhere — [the answer is:] not so, because of the distinction through conventional reality (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.181 //
In investigations of ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), because of the non-establishment of [things] as being of that nature,
identity and difference in conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) entities is denied. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.182 //
This is the establishment of the practice of inference (<s>anumāna</s>) and the object to be inferred (<s>anumeya</s>);
and it is constructed by depending on the difference established through cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.183 //
In cognitions that rest on their respective differences, for those who discriminate,
the <s>dharmin</s> and <s>dharma</s>s appear — conventional practice (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is based on that. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.184 //
That very [entity], introduced into conventional usage here, [when] the cognition of difference is not firmly attached,
is what is to be proven — [and when] brought into the role of proof, [its] unestablished [nature] is thereby revealed. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.185 //
From the difference of properties in difference and universality, the relation of principal and subordinate (<s>aṅga-aṅgin</s>) [arises];
just as [sound is] impermanent [and] produced by effort — [so too] an echo, by [the absence of] effort. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.186 //
Even though [it is] a component of the thesis, there is no unestablished [<s>dharmin</s>] in a different <s>dharmin</s>, because there is no refutation;

children.text: yathāśvo na viṣāṇitvādeṣa piṇḍo viṣāṇavān // Pramāṇav_4.187 //
children.translated_text: just as a horse is not [refuted] by having horns — 'this lump has horns.' // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.187 //
Or the membership [as component] at the time of what is to be proven does not [apply], because cessation is observed for that;
even a particular, [though] the meaning of the thesis, is not tenable due to the difference of properties. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.188 //
For the easy comprehension [of the topic] through the classification of thesis-properties (<s>pakṣadharma</s>),
the summary of the <s>sūtra</s> on the meaning of the context of reasons (<s>hetu</s>) is stated. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.189 //
The particle [eva] that expresses exclusion (<s>vyatirekaka</s>) of the property excludes
non-connection, connection, and also absolute non-connection. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.190 //
Uttered together with qualifier (<s>viśeṣaṇa</s>), qualified (<s>viśeṣya</s>), and action (<s>kriyā</s>),
even when not [explicitly] employed, this entire meaning is understood from the intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.191 //
Since a sentence has exclusion (<s>vyavaccheda</s>) as its fruit — [for example,] '<s>Caitra</s> is a bow-bearer,'

children.text: pārtho dhanurdharo nīlaṃ sarojamiti vā yathā // Pramāṇav_4.192 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Pārtha</s> is a bow-bearer,' or 'the lotus is blue' — // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.192 //
exclusion with respect to the counterpart (<s>pratiyogin</s>) is understood in those meanings as well,

children.text: tathā prasiddheḥ samārthyās vivakṣānugamād dhvaneḥ // Pramāṇav_4.193 //
children.translated_text: because of established convention, capacity, conformity to intention, and implication (<s>dhvani</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.193 //
Through the exclusion of non-connection of that, the <s>dharmin</s> qualifies the <s>dharma</s>;
the <s>dharma</s>, as qualified by that, does not suffer the defect of total absence (<s>niranvaya</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.194 //
For the establishment of <s>svabhāva</s> (nature) and <s>kārya</s> (effect), two pairs of reason-reversals [exist];
due to dispute regarding difference and universality, the remainder serves as proof through exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.195 //
For the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of what is to be known with the cause is not [established] by anything other than [its own] nature (<s>svabhāva</s>);
since deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is possible, the result is the twofold occurrence [of the reason]. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.196 //

children.text: prayatnānantaraṃ jñānaṃ prāk sato niyamena na /
children.translated_text: Cognition [arising] immediately after effort does not [arise] necessarily from what previously exists,
because of its complete non-recurrence in the senses and words in every case. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.197 //
Because of the contradiction between occasional dependence and the non-production of an effect,
the occasional result is established — such cognition is the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of that. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.198 //
Even though [the matter] is established by just this much, the separate treatment of <s>svabhāva</s> (nature-based reason)

children.text: kāryeṇa saha nirdeśe mā jñāsīt sarvamīdṛśam // Pramāṇav_4.199 //
children.translated_text: [is given so that] when stated together with <s>kārya</s> (effect-based reason), one should not think everything is of this [latter] kind. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.199 //
The statement of reasons is made for the purpose of understanding, [even] when the inference of the stated meaning [is already obtained];

children.text: atra prabheda ākhyātaḥ lakṣaṇaṃ tu na bhidyate // Pramāṇav_4.200 //
children.translated_text: here the subdivision is declared, but the definition does not differ. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.200 //
Therefore here, even <s>svabhāva</s> (nature), through the mark of effect (<s>kāryaliṅga</s>), shares a common domain;
and hence the similar illustration [applies] — of that which is born from effort (<s>prayatna</s>), as something manifest. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.201 //
That which has existence (<s>sattā</s>) as inseparable, and which is undivided in itself —
that would be non-deviating (<s>avyabhicārin</s>) with respect to it — this is the meaning; that is the subdivision. // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.202 //
In conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) and the like, where the connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is not of that kind,

children.text: na te hetava ityuktaṃ vyabhicārasya sambhavāt // Pramāṇav_4.203 //
children.translated_text: they are not [valid] reasons (<s>hetu</s>) — thus it is said, because of the possibility of deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>). // <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> 4.203 //

children.text: sati vā pratibandhe 'stu sa eva gatisādhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, when the connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) does exist, that alone is the means of establishing the conclusion.

children.text: niyamo hyavinābhāvo niyataśca na sādhanam // Pramāṇav_4.204 //
children.translated_text: For restriction is invariable concomitance, and what is restricted is not a proof. // Pramāṇav_4.204 //
The exclusiveness of exclusion is called invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>),
and that does not exist in things not connected; hence the stability of positive concomitance is from that alone. // Pramāṇav_4.205 //

children.text: svātmatve hetubhāve vā siddhe hi vyatirekitā /
children.translated_text: For if identity with itself or the state of being a reason is established, negative concomitance

children.text: sidhyedato 'viśeṣe na vyatirekā na vānvayaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.206 //
children.translated_text: would be established; therefore, when there is no distinction, neither negative nor positive concomitance [is established]. // Pramāṇav_4.206 //
Taking merely non-observation, negative concomitance alone
has been called inconclusive; therefore it could indicate otherwise. // Pramāṇav_4.207 //
If the absence of breath and the like pervades selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), then upon the negation

children.text: ātmano vinivartteta prāṇādiryadi tacca na // Pramāṇav_4.208 //
children.translated_text: of the self, breath and the like would be negated — but that is not so. // Pramāṇav_4.208 //
Because the negation of one thing through the negation of another is impossible.
If it is of the nature of that, or produced from that — not so, upon the apprehension of the self. // Pramāṇav_4.209 //
Upon the apprehension of that, when it is known and when it is not known, [both] are established.

children.text: te cātyantaparokṣasya dṛṣṭyadṛṣṭī na sidhyataḥ // Pramāṇav_4.210 //
children.translated_text: And for what is entirely beyond perception, neither observation nor non-observation is established. // Pramāṇav_4.210 //
Or whence is it [known] that what has an unobserved nature does not exist in pots and the like elsewhere?
Whence is the pervasion of the exclusion of that whose negative concomitance is unknown? // Pramāṇav_4.211 //
And the existence or non-existence of breath and the like is perceived through observation in certain cases.

children.text: tathātmā yadi dṛśyeta sattvāsattvaṃ pratīyate // Pramāṇav_4.212 //
children.translated_text: If the self were similarly observable, its existence or non-existence would be perceived. // Pramāṇav_4.212 //
By the absence of whichever cause breath is not seen in a pot,

children.text: dehe 'pi yadyasau na syād yukto dehe na sambhavaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.213 //
children.translated_text: if that [cause] were absent in the body too, it would be reasonable that it does not exist in the body. // Pramāṇav_4.213 //

children.text: bhinne 'pi kiñcit sādharmyād yadi tattvaṃ pratīyate /
children.translated_text: If, even among different things, reality is perceived due to some similarity,

children.text: prameyatvād ghaṭādīnāṃ sātmatvaṃ kinna mīyate // Pramāṇav_4.214 //
children.translated_text: why is the selfhood of pots and the like not ascertained from their being objects of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>)? // Pramāṇav_4.214 //
If because it is undesired — well, a means of valid knowledge is the basis of all desires.

children.text: bhāvābhāvavyavasthāṃ kaḥ kartu tena vinā prabhuḥ // Pramāṇav_4.215 //
children.translated_text: Who is capable of determining the existence or non-existence of things without it? // Pramāṇav_4.215 //
Breath, blinking, and the like arise from memory, desire, and effort, and are produced from those.
Those [memory, desire, effort] arise from sense-objects, sense-organs, and mind, and are produced from their own kind. // Pramāṇav_4.216 //
They depend on mutual conditions and possess positive and negative concomitance.
This much is the absence [of need for a self]; in positing another, there is infinite regress. // Pramāṇav_4.217 //
Being auditory, that [reason] is equal [to the opponent's]; because of the deviation of breath and the like.

children.text: na tasya vyabhicāritvād vyatireke 'pi cet katham // Pramāṇav_4.218 //
children.translated_text: If because of the deviation of that — how then even in negative concomitance? // Pramāṇav_4.218 //
'The separation is not from the absence of the probandum itself' — indeed it is stated thus;
the absence of positive concomitance in the similar instance — that same [problem] applies equally elsewhere. // Pramāṇav_4.219 //
'The separation is from the absence of the probandum' — this is said when it exists in the probandum.
By implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>), the observation of both has been stated by a single [statement]. // Pramāṇav_4.220 //
Such non-deviation therefore is not established in things not positively concomitant.
And what other kind of prohibition of prohibition is there, beyond positive statement? // Pramāṇav_4.221 //
Cessation is not to be proved of the non-existent; we do not accept 'not in the non-probandum.'

children.text: neti saiva nivṛttiḥ kiṃ nivṛtterasato matā // Pramāṇav_4.222 //
children.translated_text: 'No' — that itself is cessation; what? Is cessation considered to be of the non-existent? // Pramāṇav_4.222 //
But the absence of cessation is a positive statement; the real existence of the non-existent, even if it be,
the real non-existence does not exist — behold the gesticulation of the barren [woman's son]! // Pramāṇav_4.223 //
If there is cessation in that, why is the occurrence of the reason desired?

children.text: sāpi na pratiṣedho 'yaṃ nivṛttiḥ kiṃ niṣidhyate // Pramāṇav_4.224 //
children.translated_text: If that too is not — this prohibition, what cessation is being prohibited? // Pramāṇav_4.224 //

children.text: vidhānaṃ pratiṣedhaṃ ca muktvā śābdo 'sti nāparaḥ /
children.translated_text: Apart from positive statement and prohibition, there is no other verbal

children.text: vyavahāraḥ sa cāsatsu neti prāptātra mūkatā // Pramāṇav_4.225 //
children.translated_text: usage; and that does not apply to non-existents — thus silence is reached here. // Pramāṇav_4.225 //

children.text: satāṃ ca na niṣedho 'sti so 'satsu ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And there is no prohibition of existents; and that does not exist in non-existents.

children.text: jagatyanena nyāyena nañarthaḥ pralayaṃ gataḥ // Pramāṇav_4.226 //
children.translated_text: By this reasoning, the meaning of the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) has reached dissolution in the world. // Pramāṇav_4.226 //
If it is negation with respect to place and time — what exists is negated as it is;

children.text: na thā na yathā so 'sti tathāpi na niṣidhyate // Pramāṇav_4.227 //
children.translated_text: not in a way it does not exist; and even so, it is not negated. // Pramāṇav_4.227 //
Therefore, depending on the meaning of words, resting on existence and non-existence,
all positive and negative statements are accepted as having no external basis. // Pramāṇav_4.228 //

children.text: tābhyāṃ sa dharmi sambaddhaḥ khyātyabhavo 'pi tādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The property-bearer connected with those two, even the non-existence of appearance, is of that nature.
Since verbal usage exists, that too is accepted as having conventional reality. // Pramāṇav_4.229 //
Otherwise, in the positive and negative statements of objects,
there would be the positive and negative statement of a single property as having every nature. // Pramāṇav_4.230 //
Due to non-manifoldness in difference, unlike manifold positive and negative statements,
there is no combination of positive and negative statements in a single property-bearer. // Pramāṇav_4.231 //
Referring to a single property-bearer, resting on various properties,
in the positive statement of one, it disregards the others, as though they partook of that. // Pramāṇav_4.232 //
And in negation, what is distinguished from that — disregarding those others,
the intellect fabricates conventional usage whose object is unreal, in this way. // Pramāṇav_4.233 //
Having accepted that very thing as resting on the undifferentiated content of non-conceptual [cognition],
they do not contradict the object arisen from beginningless impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), nor the worldly [convention]. // Pramāṇav_4.234 //
Having that result and not having that result — in the object, though one, being differentiated variously,
led by these various disturbances, as if by accumulation and diminution. // Pramāṇav_4.235 //
Even what does not possess that is brought to
a view resting on differentiation, due to some connection; therefore they are of unknown disturbance. // Pramāṇav_4.236 //
And because the occurrence of the means of proving existence is doubtful, it would be non-existent — but that is not so;
and since non-existence is accepted, it is not proper [to say] there is no valid means of knowledge. // Pramāṇav_4.237 //
Even in the negative concomitance of the non-existent, the exclusion from the similar instance

children.text: sandigghaṃ tasya sandehād vipakṣād vinivarttanam // Pramāṇav_4.238 //
children.translated_text: is doubtful; due to the doubt about that, the exclusion from the dissimilar instance [is also doubtful]. // Pramāṇav_4.238 //
When restriction to one is established, the exclusion from the other is established.

children.text: dvairāśye sati dṛṣṭeṣu syāddṛṣṭe 'pi saṃśayaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.239 //
children.translated_text: When there is a twofold possibility among observed things, doubt would arise even in what is observed. // Pramāṇav_4.239 //
There exist objects that pervade the unmanifest, being of that class.
In some cases, restriction [cannot be established] through non-observation, like the writing on earthen and iron [surfaces]. // Pramāṇav_4.240 //
When the existence of contradiction is unobserved, who could remove doubt?

children.text: kvacid viniyamāt ko 'nyastatkāryātmatayā sa ca // Pramāṇav_4.241 //
children.translated_text: Because of restriction in some cases — what else? And that is through the nature of being an effect of that. // Pramāṇav_4.241 //
Even from selflessness, the exclusion of that [self] is doubtful by that [reasoning].

children.text: astu nāma tathāpyātmā nānairātmyāt prasidhyati // Pramāṇav_4.242 //
children.translated_text: Let it be so — even then, the self is not established from selflessness. // Pramāṇav_4.242 //
By which [reasoning] he does not wish the absence or presence of negative concomitance,
just as, even without negative concomitance, breath and the like are not a similar instance. // Pramāṇav_4.243 //
If the reason has no negative concomitance in the similar instance, then the reason has positive concomitance;
if it has neither positive nor negative concomitance, selflessness does not establish the possession of self. // Pramāṇav_4.244 //
That whose own nature is established as inseparable (<s>nāntarīyaka</s>) in activities,

children.text: nivarttakaḥ sa evātaḥ pravṛttau ca pravartakaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.245 //
children.translated_text: that alone is therefore both a preventer in cessation and an impeller in activity. // Pramāṇav_4.245 //
And that inseparability, as a means of proof, requires another means of proof.
Observation and non-observation with respect to an effect — that indeed is the causal relation. // Pramāṇav_4.246 //
There is no way [to establish] that another thing necessarily exists when that exists,
because the non-existence of those that are always present is impossible [when the cause is absent]. // Pramāṇav_4.247 //
Since the differences in the nature of effects arise from their causes,

children.text: tairvinā bhavato 'nyasmāt tajjaṃ rūpaṃ kathaṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_4.248 //
children.translated_text: how could the form born of that exist from something else, existing without those [causes]? // Pramāṇav_4.248 //
For the manifold nature of things is due to differences in the capacity of aggregates.

children.text: sā cenna bhedikā prāptamekarūpamidaṃ jagat // Pramāṇav_4.249 //
children.translated_text: If that [aggregate capacity] is not a differentiator, this world would turn out to be of one form. // Pramāṇav_4.249 //
If it both differentiates and does not differentiate, the differentiated nature would be contradicted.

children.text: ekasya nānārūpatve dve rūpe pāvaketarau // Pramāṇav_4.250 //
children.translated_text: If one thing has manifold forms, the two forms would be fire and the other. // Pramāṇav_4.250 //

children.text: tat tasyā jananaṃ rūpamanyasya yadi saiva sā /
children.translated_text: If the production of that is its form, and if it is the same as the other,

children.text: na tasyā jananaṃ rūpaṃ tadasyāḥ sambhavet katham // Pramāṇav_4.251 //
children.translated_text: the production of that is not its form — how could that belong to this? // Pramāṇav_4.251 //
Therefore, the natures of cause and effect are mutually fixed.

children.text: tasmāt svadṛṣṭāviva tad dṛṣṭe kārye 'pi gamyate // Pramāṇav_4.252 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, just as in the observation of itself, that is understood even when the effect is observed. // Pramāṇav_4.252 //
How can one [effect arise] from many? Like moisture from milk and water —

children.text: dravaśakteḥ yataḥ kledaḥ sā tvekaiva dvayorapi // Pramāṇav_4.253 //
children.translated_text: since moisture comes from the capacity to be fluid, and that capacity is one and the same in both. // Pramāṇav_4.253 //
Is its nature different or non-different? If different, how is fluidity [common]?
It is said to be non-different, because of the non-difference of that form of cognition. // Pramāṇav_4.254 //
Likewise, even amid difference, fire is the basis of the cognition of fire.

children.text: yenāṃśenādadhad dhūmaṃ tenāṃśena tathā gatiḥ // Pramāṇav_4.255 //
children.translated_text: By the aspect by which it does not produce smoke, by that aspect such is the understanding. // Pramāṇav_4.255 //
Since smoke arises from a component of the conditions for fire-cognition, requiring something else,
smoke does not deviate from that — similarly, another effect is likewise. // Pramāṇav_4.256 //
Since fire is established in the condition of smoke being a transformation of fuel and a component of heat,

children.text: anagnicedadhūmo 'sau sa dhūmaścet sa pāvakaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.257 //
children.translated_text: if there is no fire, there is no smoke; and if there is smoke, there is fire. // Pramāṇav_4.257 //
Inseparability (<s>nāntarīyakatā</s>) should be understood in each case with reference to the reason —
as stated previously regarding the nature of destruction and being produced. // Pramāṇav_4.258 //
This entire method of the reasoning about causelessness belongs to the negative concomitant.
It should be inferred from the statement about the auditory [reason], made for seeing the similarity. // Pramāṇav_4.259 //
Since the cessation of the object is described through the continuation of the nature of the reason alone,
in an observable object, this is indicated by the declaration of the nature of the cause of doubt. // Pramāṇav_4.261 //
A negation that does not accept the real aspect is proved by this [method];

children.text: vastunyapi tu pūrvābhyāṃ paryudāso vidhānataḥ // Pramāṇav_4.262 //
children.translated_text: but even in reality, the <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion) is [established] by the first two, through positive statement. // Pramāṇav_4.262 //
Among observable things, existence is [established] by observation, and nothing else.
Thus, for the purpose of making known, a single illustration without qualification is considered [sufficient]. // Pramāṇav_4.263 //
Through the non-existence of the object, the possessor of the object is negated there,
removing doubt regarding cognition and expression — just as [the absence of] fire from [the absence of] burning. // Pramāṇav_4.264 //
Similarly, another [negation]: among observable things, non-existence is [established] through non-apprehension.
Cognitions and words pertaining to that are established as having that as their basis, because of the existence of that. // Pramāṇav_4.265 //
For this convention is established: when something observable is not observed, it does not exist.
When that [non-apprehension] is established and undoubted, even when there is that-nature, cognition and expression [are established]. // Pramāṇav_4.266 //
Even when the object exists, one who, due to delusion, does not affirm it here,

children.text: kevalaṃ siddhasādharmyāt smāryate samayaṃ paraḥ // Pramāṇav_4.267 //
children.translated_text: is merely reminded of the convention through similarity with what is established, by another. // Pramāṇav_4.267 //
Just as the causal relation is established through observation and non-observation,
for the words 'effect' and the like are constructed for the conventional usage of those two. // Pramāṇav_4.268 //
The establishment of an effect from a cause — this is through the inclusion within the nature of [the cause].
In the explanation of the varieties of reasons, a separate illustration has not been shown. // Pramāṇav_4.269 //
From the experience of a single apprehension, 'I do not apprehend this' —
or 'I do apprehend' — the arising of the conceptual [cognition] of the intellect. // Pramāṇav_4.270 //
The particularity of objects is understood only from a distinctive cognition.
And the attainment of being of such a nature is the cause of the cognition of difference. // Pramāṇav_4.271 //
Therefore, the establishment of the difference of cognitions is from themselves; from those two, [the difference] of their objects.

children.text: anyathā hyanavasthāto bhedaḥ sighyenna kasyacit // Pramāṇav_4.272 //
children.translated_text: For otherwise, due to infinite regress, the difference of anything would not be established. // Pramāṇav_4.272 //
From the experience of a distinctive form, the refutation of the other [possibility] follows.
Hence the apprehension of that distinction; and the non-apprehension of that too [follows]. // Pramāṇav_4.273 //
Therefore, this non-apprehension itself is understood directly from perception.
It indicates [non-existence] from its occurrence only in itself, due to the determination of the absence of that. // Pramāṇav_4.274 //
Otherwise, the non-existence of an object would be understood from non-apprehension,
and the non-existence of apprehension [would need to be established] by another — leading to infinite regress. // Pramāṇav_4.275 //
Since certainty is impossible regarding the unobservable, the position [that it exists] elsewhere is contradicted.
Just as in the existences of other things, conceptual construction and the like based on marks are not established. // Pramāṇav_4.276 //
For this [conceptual construction] has no certainty as its result, and is not sufficient for establishing exclusion.
The first [type of non-apprehension] is employed as a reason only when ascertained in [the context of] what is to be proved. // Pramāṇav 4.277 //

children.text: tasyāḥ svayaṃ prayogeṣu svarūpaṃ vā prayujyate /
children.translated_text: In its applications, either its own form is employed,
or the form of object-contradiction — [showing that] from the existence [of one], the non-existence [of the other follows] through [its] existence. // Pramāṇav 4.278 //
Or from the establishment of mutual difference — like the ascertainment of fixed existence [of one thing excluding another];
or from the contradiction by another means of knowledge — like fixed existence that is dependent [on further evidence]. // Pramāṇav 4.279 //
Whence is there a fixed [relation] to what arises from another cause, in [its] proximity?
If existence is the cause of existence, what is the point of laboring through a chain [of intermediate causes]? // Pramāṇav 4.280 //
If [a cause], having produced [an entity], produces its destroyer — [then] it is the destroyer of that [entity];

children.text: tameva naśvaraṃ bhāvaṃ janayed yadi kiṃ bhavet // Pramāṇav_4.281 //
children.translated_text: if it were to produce that very perishable entity [itself] — what would [the destroyer] be? // Pramāṇav 4.281 //

children.text: ātmopakārakaḥ kaḥ syāt tasya siddhatmanaḥ sataḥ /
children.translated_text: What would be a helper of itself, for that [entity] which exists with its nature already established?

children.text: nātmopakārakaḥ kaḥ syāt tena yaḥ samapekṣyate // Pramāṇav_4.282 //
children.translated_text: What would not be a helper of itself? — by that, what [further factor] is required? // Pramāṇav 4.282 //
And if the entity is independent [of any cause for its destruction], is it ever of a nature such that

children.text: yathā na kṣepabhāgiṣṭaḥ sa evodbhūtanāśakaḥ // Pramāṇav_4.283 //
children.translated_text: it does not partake of destruction? That very [entity] is the destroyer when [destruction] has arisen. // Pramāṇav 4.283 //
If [you say] that even for a moment, an entity does not [depend on] the existence of [another] entity when [it is] independent —

children.text: bhāvo hi sa tathā bhūto 'bhāva bhāvastathā katham // Pramāṇav_4.284 //
children.translated_text: [we reply:] that entity is indeed of such a nature; how can a non-entity be an entity of such [a nature]? // Pramāṇav 4.284 //
Those whose existence depends on nothing other [than their own conditions] are fixed in their existence by those [conditions alone];
and the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>), whose obstruction is impossible [once complete], [produces] the action of the effect. // Pramāṇav 4.285 //
